meta.fix_status: 43 findings FIXED_BY_CLAUDE in the working tree on 2026-07-09, 1 PARTIALLY_FIXED, rest OPEN. Desktop+admin typecheck clean (was 80 errors) and desktop build passes. WARNING: line numbers here refer to the PRE-FIX tree — cite enclosing function names, not lines.

findings.title: Offline startup wipes an admin-granted (CLOUD-VERIFIED) full license — paying restaurant locked out
findings.evidence: index.ts:470: `try { stillValid = await checkCloudActivation(machineId) } catch { stillValid = true /* offline = trust local */ }` followed by `if (!stillValid) { ... settingsRepo.set('activation_type',''); settingsRepo.set('activation_status',''); settingsRepo.set('activation_code','') }`. But `checkCloudActivation` (src/main/activation/cloud.ts:125-137) can NEVER throw: it returns `!error && !!data`, and supabase-js v2 converts fetch/network failures into `{ data: null, error }` results (verified in node_modules/@supabase/postgrest-js/dist/index.cjs: `if (!this.shouldThrowOnError) res = res.catch((fetchError) => ({ error: {...}, data: null, ... }))`), plus cloud.ts wraps everything in its own `catch { return false }`. So the 'offline = trust local' branch is dead code, and a network failure is indistinguishable from 'license revoked'. The same dead catch exists at index.ts:485 for serial-licensed machines whose local check failed.
findings.scenario: A restaurant whose full license was granted via the admin dashboard (activation_code = 'CLOUD-VERIFIED', which is how the trial→full upgrade at index.ts:219-221 and admin grants work) boots the POS in the morning while the internet is down (routine in Algeria). checkCloudActivation returns false, the app logs 'SECURITY: Cloud activation revoked' and erases activation_type/status/code from the local DB. The POS drops to the activation page; staff cannot take orders. Even when the internet comes back the license does not self-restore because activation_type is now '' so the startup cloud re-check never runs — the owner must intervene manually. Money/lockout: full business stoppage for a paying customer.
findings.fix: Make checkCloudActivation return a tri-state ('active' | 'absent' | 'unreachable') by inspecting the returned error (network failures have status 0 / FetchError code, a clean no-row is PGRST116). Only revoke on a confirmed 'absent'; on 'unreachable' keep the local license (trust local), matching the intent of the existing dead catch.

refuter.reason: Confirmed end-to-end. (1) checkCloudActivation (src/main/activation/cloud.ts:125-137) can never reject: its whole body is in try/catch returning false, and the installed @supabase/postgrest-js 2.98.0 (dist/index.cjs:155) resolves fetch/network failures to {data:null, error} when shouldThrowOnError is false (default). So the `catch { stillValid = true /* offline = trust local */ }` at src/main/index.ts:470 is dead code, and an offline boot yields stillValid=false, which triggers the wipe of activation_type/status/code at index.ts:471-476. (2) CLOUD-VERIFIED is a real production state (set at index.ts:221 trial-to-full upgrade and index.ts:490) with no serial code to re-enter. (3) The wipe locks the POS: appStore.ts:108 derives `activated` from activation_status==='activated' and App.tsx:183 redirects to /activate; ActivationPage offers only serial entry or trial start (trial.ipc.ts returns trial_expired for an already-used trial). (4) No self-restore: checkCloudActivation's only 3 call sites are gated on activation_type 'full' or 'trial', which is now '', so even after connectivity returns the license never comes back without manual intervention. Same dead catch at index.ts:485. A paying restaurant booting during a routine internet outage loses its license and cannot take orders.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by independent trace. (1) cloud.ts:125-137 `checkCloudActivation` is fully wrapped in `try{...return !error && !!data}catch{return false}` — it can never reject, so the `catch { stillValid = true /* offline = trust local */ }` at index.ts:470 is dead code. (2) Verified in the installed node_modules/@supabase/postgrest-js/dist/index.cjs:155-195 that with default shouldThrowOnError=false a network/fetch failure resolves to `{error:{message:'FetchError...'}, data:null, status:0}` rather than throwing — so offline returns false, indistinguishable from revoked. (3) Concrete trigger state exists: admin-granted licenses store activation_code='CLOUD-VERIFIED' (set at index.ts:219-221 on trial→full upgrade, and index.ts:489-490), and every startup with activation_type='full' + CLOUD-VERIFIED runs the cloud check with NO net.isOnline() guard (contrast the trial path's guard at index.ts:197). Offline boot → stillValid=false → index.ts:471-475 wipes activation_type/status/code → renderer routes to /activate (App.tsx:183 `!activated ? '/activate'`) → POS locked, no orders. (4) No self-heal: with activation_type='' the startup recheck (gated on ==='full'), trial watcher (==='trial'), and trial:start (returns 'trial_expired', trial.ipc.ts:27-28) all dead-end; checkCloudActivation has no IPC exposure, so recovery needs manual support intervention. Same dead catch confirmed at index.ts:485 for the serial-path fallback (wipe at 491-496). Proposed tri-state fix ('active'/'absent'/'unreachable' via status 0/FetchError vs PGRST116) is the right direction and matches the dead catch's intent; adding the trial-path's `net.isOnline()` pre-check would also work as a simpler guard.

findings.title: Owner dashboard 'Today' is bucketed by UTC created_at, not the restaurant-local order_date the POS uses
findings.evidence: `const today = new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]` (line 11) then `.gte('created_at', today + 'T00:00:00Z')` (line 26). owner_orders rows carry a restaurant-LOCAL `order_date` column precisely for this (owner-sync.ts:21 `order.order_date || localDate()`, with a comment explaining the 00:00–00:59 local bug), and `created_at` is UTC ISO (orders.repo.ts inserts `new Date().toISOString()`). The route ignores order_date and buckets by UTC day.
findings.scenario: Algeria is UTC+1 and fast-food places are open past midnight. An order placed at 00:30 local July 3 has created_at 23:30Z July 2. Until 01:00 local it shows on the dashboard mixed into July 2's 'Today'; after 01:00 local (00:00 UTC July 3) the filter becomes July 3 00:00Z and the order vanishes from 'Today' entirely — its revenue is never shown for July 3 even though the POS counts it in July 3's local day (daily_number reset). Owner's dashboard revenue disagrees with the POS Z-report every night.
findings.fix: Filter on the local-day column the POS already writes: compute today's date in Africa/Algiers (e.g. `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA',{timeZone:'Africa/Algiers'}).format(new Date())`) and use `.eq('order_date', localToday)` instead of the created_at gte filter.

refuter.reason: Confirmed across the cited files. admin/app/api/owner/data/route.ts:11 computes `today` via `new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]` (always UTC date), then line 26 filters owner_orders by `.gte('created_at', today + 'T00:00:00Z')`, and the stats (totalRevenue/orderCount, lines 33-36) are derived from this UTC-filtered set. owner_orders rows carry a restaurant-LOCAL `order_date` column (owner-sync.ts:21,32 `order.order_date || localDate()`, with an in-code comment at lines 16-20 documenting exactly this 00:00-00:59-local bug), while `created_at` is UTC ISO (orders.repo.ts:145 `new Date().toISOString()` → owner-sync.ts:33). The route ignores order_date. Failure trace (Algeria UTC+1): an order placed 00:30 local July 3 has created_at 23:30Z July 2 but POS order_date/daily_number = July 3. During local daytime July 3 the route filters created_at >= 2026-07-03T00:00Z, which excludes the 23:30Z-July-2 order — so every order in the first local hour after midnight (busy late-night fast-food window) is permanently missing from the dashboard's Today, making owner revenue disagree with the POS Z-report nightly. Not refutable: `.toISOString()` is UTC irrespective of Vercel server TZ; the excluded orders never reach the client, so no client re-bucketing can recover them. Proposed fix (.eq order_date with Africa/Algiers local date) matches how POS/owner-sync store data.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by full trace. POS inserts orders with created_at = new Date().toISOString() (UTC instant, orders.repo.ts:145/164) and order_date = localDate() (restaurant-local day, orders.repo.ts:12-14,153). owner-sync.ts:32-33 mirrors both to owner_orders, with an explicit comment (lines 16-20) that order_date is the correct local-day bucketing key. The dashboard route ignores order_date: route.ts:11 computes today via new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0] (UTC calendar date — Vercel runs UTC and .toISOString() is UTC unconditionally) and route.ts:26 filters .gte('created_at', today + 'T00:00:00Z') — a UTC-day window over the UTC created_at column. Concrete scenario (Algeria UTC+1, open past midnight): an order placed 00:30 local July 3 has created_at 2026-07-02T23:30:00Z and order_date 2026-07-03 (daily_number = July 3 #1; POS Z-report/daily view buckets it in July 3 via WHERE order_date=?). On the dashboard it is first lumped into UTC July 2's 'Today', then once local time passes 01:00 (00:00Z July 3) the filter becomes created_at >= 2026-07-03T00:00:00Z and the order (23:30Z July 2) falls below the bound and disappears from July 3's 'Today' entirely. Systematically, every order in the first local hour (00:00-00:59) of each day is permanently excluded from that day's owner-dashboard revenue/order count, so the dashboard totals diverge from the POS every night — a money-correctness bug. Proposed fix direction is correct: filter on the order_date column with a restaurant-local 'today' (.eq('order_date', localToday)) matches exactly how the POS buckets. Minor caveat: hardcoding Africa/Algiers is fine given the stated Algeria-only (fixed UTC+1, no DST) deployment but would need the per-machine timezone if the product ever served other zones.

findings.title: Daily revenue/order-count stats are computed from at most the latest 100 orders
findings.evidence: `.order('created_at', { ascending: false }).limit(100)` and then `const nonCancelled = orderList.filter(...); const totalRevenue = nonCancelled.reduce((s, o) => s + Number(o.total), 0)` — the day's totals (Revenue, Orders, Avg Order, Popular Today) are derived from the same 100-row page used for the order list, not from all of today's rows.
findings.scenario: A busy restaurant does 150 orders in a day. From order #101 onward, the owner dashboard's 'Revenue' card silently drops the morning's first 50 orders — showing e.g. 90,000 DA when the real day is 130,000 DA — and Popular Items ranks only the afternoon. The owner makes money decisions off understated numbers with no warning.
findings.fix: Run a separate unlimited aggregate query for the day's stats (or select only total/status/items_summary for all of today's rows and keep limit(100) just for the rendered order list).

refuter.reason: CONFIRMED real. In admin/app/api/owner/data/route.ts the owner_orders query (lines 22-28) fetches today's rows ordered by created_at DESC with an explicit .limit(100), and the day's stats are then computed from that same truncated page: totalRevenue (line 34), orderCount (line 35), avgOrder (line 36), and popularItems (lines 39-55). owner-sync.ts (lines 22-36) upserts exactly ONE row per order keyed on (machine_id, order_number, order_date), and daily_number is unique per local day, so 150 orders = 150 distinct rows — the limit truncates them. The consumer OwnerDashboard.tsx does a single fetch (line 354) and renders data.stats verbatim (line 418 -> Revenue card 495-497, Orders 501, Avg 519, Popular Today 524-541) with no client-side re-aggregation and no pagination; the separate week/month 'Stats' tab hits a different endpoint (/api/owner/stats) so it does not compensate. Because the query orders DESC, the dropped rows are the earliest (morning) orders. Failure scenario: a fast-food shop doing 150 orders in a local day — the 'Today' tab's Revenue card shows the sum of only the latest 100 orders (e.g. ~90,000 DA instead of ~130,000 DA), the Orders count caps at 100, Avg Order and Popular Today are skewed to the afternoon, and the owner sees silently understated numbers with no warning. 100+ orders/day is realistic for the target market, so the bug triggers in normal busy operation. Only caveat (does not refute): the UTC 'today' boundary vs local day is a separate concern, but it does not prevent the >100-row truncation. Fix: run an unlimited aggregate query for the day's stats (or select total/status/items_summary for all of today's rows) and keep limit(100) only for the rendered order list.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by full trace. In admin/app/api/owner/data/route.ts the GET handler (triggered when the owner opens the dashboard, fetched at OwnerDashboard.tsx line 354: `fetch('/api/owner/data?machineId=...')`) runs ONE query: lines 22-28 select owner_orders filtered `.gte('created_at', today+'T00:00:00Z')`, `.order('created_at',{ascending:false})` (newest-first), `.limit(100)`. Line 30 `const orderList = orders || []` is therefore at most the newest 100 rows of the day. Lines 33-36 derive ALL day stats from that same page: `nonCancelled = orderList.filter(status!=='cancelled')`, `totalRevenue = nonCancelled.reduce(+Number(o.total))`, `orderCount = nonCancelled.length`, `avgOrder`. Lines 40-55 compute popularItems from `nonCancelled` too. Line 57-62 returns `stats` + `popularItems`. The consumer (OwnerDashboard.tsx lines 418-528) reads `data.stats` / `data.popularItems` and renders them straight into the "Revenue", "Orders", "Avg Order" cards and Popular Items list — no separate aggregate call exists. Concrete failure: a restaurant with 150 non-cancelled orders today. `created_at DESC` + limit(100) keeps only the 100 most-recent (afternoon/evening) orders and silently drops the first ~50 (morning) rows. If each order ~867 DA, the Revenue card shows ~90,000 DA instead of the true ~130,000 DA, Orders shows 100 not 150, Avg Order is skewed toward larger late-day tickets, and Popular Today ranks only the last 100 orders' items. No warning is shown. Reachable: 100+ orders/day is normal for a busy fast-food shop. Fix direction is essentially correct (run a dedicated aggregate query, or select only total/status/items_summary for all of today's rows and keep limit(100) for the rendered list), BUT note a plain Supabase/PostgREST select without .limit() still hits PostgREST's default max-rows cap (~1000), so a shop exceeding ~1000/day would still truncate; the fully-correct fix is a DB-side SUM/COUNT aggregation (RPC) rather than pulling rows into JS. For the realistic 150-order case either variant of the proposed fix resolves it.

findings.title: TV pairing resolves to an arbitrary (last-synced) display profile instead of the default display
findings.evidence: `.eq('settings->>_pairing_code', code).order('updated_at', { ascending: false }).limit(1)` — the comment only worries about "two restaurants share a 4-digit code", but the desktop writes the SAME machine-wide pairing code into EVERY profile row (src/main/sync/cloud-sync.ts:76 `settings._pairing_code = getPairingCode()`, run for each profile by syncAllDisplayProfiles). syncAllDisplayProfiles iterates ['default', ...named] sequentially with `await`, so the LAST named profile always has the freshest updated_at and always wins this order-by. The POS shows the pairing code ONLY on the 'default' tab (AmbianceScreen.tsx:443 `activeProfile === 'default' && pairingCode`), and the TV app (MainActivity.kt) pins the returned `profile` into both the LAN URL (`/display?profile=X`) and the cloud fallback URL (the uncommitted diff now adds `?profile=` to cloudUrl too), then remembers it in prefs.
findings.scenario: A restaurant creates a second display profile 'kitchen' for a back-of-house screen. Staff install the Fast Food TV app on the customer-facing TV and type the 4-digit code shown on the POS default tab. /api/pair returns profile='kitchen' (its row was synced last, milliseconds after default), so the customer TV permanently shows the kitchen profile's design/panels instead of the main display, on both LAN and cloud paths, and the app remembers the wrong URL across reboots.
findings.fix: When multiple rows match the code for the same machine_id, prefer the 'default' profile row — e.g. `.order('profile_name', { ascending: true })` after de-duplicating by machine, or fetch all matches, group by machine_id, pick the freshest machine then its 'default' row.

refuter.reason:
CONFIRMED. The path holds end to end in the current working tree.

1) admin/app/api/pair/route.ts:35-37 resolves a 4-digit code by `.eq('settings->>_pairing_code', code).order('updated_at', {ascending:false}).limit(1)` — a pure freshest-row tiebreak with no preference for the 'default' profile.

2) The code is machine-wide, not per-profile: src/main/tablet/pairing.ts:16-23 stores/returns a single `pairing_code` setting.

3) That same code is stamped into EVERY profile row: src/main/sync/cloud-sync.ts:76 sets `settings._pairing_code = getPairingCode()` unconditionally inside syncDisplaySettings(profileName), called for each profile.

4) The last-synced row is always a NAMED profile: syncAllDisplayProfiles (cloud-sync.ts:213-218) iterates getLocalProfiles() = ['default', ...named] with sequential `await`, and each upsert writes updated_at=new Date().toISOString(). 'default' is written first (oldest), the last named profile last (newest max updated_at). So /api/pair returns the named profile, never 'default', whenever any named profile exists.

5) The POS shows the code ONLY on the default/Main tab (renderer AmbianceScreen.tsx:443 `activeProfile === 'default' && pairingCode`; comment 475-476 confirms "one code per POS, shown on Main Display"). Staff type it intending the main customer display.

6) The TV pins the wrong profile on BOTH transport paths and persists it: MainActivity.kt:278 reads `profile`; lanDisplayUrl (165-169) appends `?profile=kitchen` to the LAN URL, and route.ts:62-64 builds cloudUrl as `.../tv/{machine}?profile=kitchen` for the cloud fallback; connectWithCode persists last_url (307) + via_cloud (302) across reboots.

Failure scenario: a restaurant adds a 'kitchen' display profile. Staff install the TV app on the customer-facing television and enter the 4 digits from the POS Main tab. /api/pair returns profile='kitchen' (its row synced milliseconds after 'default', so it has the freshest updated_at), and the TV permanently shows the kitchen profile's design/panels on the customer TV, on LAN and cloud, remembered across reboots.

Refutations fail: named rows are not excluded from carrying the code (line 76 is unconditional); getPairingCode is machine-wide; getLocalProfiles puts 'default' first so it is never the freshest when named profiles exist; reconcileDisplayProfiles only deletes orphans, not the active named profile; and the TV clearly consumes the returned profile. 'default' only wins when there are no named profiles — the case the scenario explicitly excludes.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by full working-tree trace. (1) getPairingCode() (src/main/tablet/pairing.ts:16-23) returns a single machine-wide code; syncDisplaySettings writes it into settings._pairing_code for EVERY profile (src/main/sync/cloud-sync.ts:76). (2) syncAllDisplayProfiles (cloud-sync.ts:213-218) iterates getLocalProfiles() = ['default', ...named] (default forced first at line 205; profiles appended after default in AmbianceScreen.tsx:302) sequentially with await, each upsert stamping updated_at=new Date().toISOString() (line 84), so the last named profile gets a strictly-later timestamp than default. Deterministic, not a race. (3) admin/app/api/pair/route.ts:35-37 .eq('settings->>_pairing_code',code).order('updated_at',{ascending:false}).limit(1) therefore returns the named profile row, not default, and builds cloudUrl with ?profile=<named> (lines 52,62-64). (4) tv-app MainActivity.kt reads profile (line 278) and pins it into BOTH the LAN URL (lanDisplayUrl -> /display?profile=named, lines 165-169,286) and the cloud fallback (line 291), then persists last_url+code to prefs (lines 302,307) so it reconnects to the wrong URL every boot. (5) The POS shows the code only on the default tab (AmbianceScreen.tsx:443; comment 475-476 'one code per POS'), so staff cannot pick a profile. Concrete scenario: a restaurant that added a 'kitchen' back-of-house display profile pairs its customer-facing TV with the 4-digit code and permanently gets the kitchen profile's design instead of the main display, on LAN and cloud, remembered across reboots. Any restaurant with >=1 named profile hits this every time. Fix-direction note: preferring the default row for the matched machine is correct, BUT the reporter's specific `.order('profile_name', {ascending:true})` suggestion is itself wrong — it selects the alphabetically-first profile, so a profile named e.g. 'bar'/'counter' (b/c < 'd') would win over 'default'. Correct fix: resolve code->freshest machine, then explicitly select that machine's profile_name='default' row (or simply always return profile='default' since the pairing code only represents the main display; named screens are reached via their direct ?profile= URL per AmbianceScreen.tsx:475-476).

findings.title: Admin-supplied 'until' is stored with zero validation; an unparseable date silently locks out a paying restaurant and later makes 'extend' throw a 500
findings.evidence: `subscription_until: body?.until || (Number.isFinite(days) ? addDaysIso(null, days) : ...)` — `body.until` is written verbatim into the DB (any string, number, or object; no Date.parse check). In effective() (line 62) `new Date(sub)` on e.g. "31/12/2026" yields Invalid Date, so `now <= subDate` is false and the derived status becomes 'expired' even though the row says status='active'. Worse, a later 'extend' hits addDaysIso() (line 53): `new Date(base).getTime()` is NaN and `new Date(NaN).toISOString()` throws RangeError — the whole request 500s (there is no try/catch in fetch()).
findings.scenario: Admin activates a paid customer with {action:'activate', until:'31/12/2026'} (DD/MM/YYYY is the natural format in Algeria). The mutate call returns ok and the row shows status 'active', but every /v1/license/check derives 'expired' → the POS locks out a restaurant that just paid. Trying to fix it with {action:'extend', days:30} then returns a raw 500 because addDaysIso throws on the invalid stored date.
findings.fix: Validate `until` before storing: require a string, reject if isNaN(Date.parse(until)) with a 400, and normalize to ISO 8601. Also guard addDaysIso against an invalid `fromIso` base.

refuter.reason: The core bug is real and concrete in the current working tree. license-server/src/index.ts line 218 (`activate`) writes `body?.until` verbatim into `subscription_until` with zero validation (no type check, no Date.parse). In effective() (lines 62-65), `new Date(sub)` on a locale-formatted value like '31/12/2026' yields Invalid Date (V8 rejects month 31), so `now <= subDate` coerces to `number <= NaN` = false and the derived status becomes 'expired' even though the row's status='active'. handleCheck() then signs a token with st:'expired' (line 133-147), so every /v1/license/check locks out a restaurant that just paid — a real, money/availability-critical failure. The endpoint is a bare admin API (ADMIN_API_KEY only, arbitrary JSON body; the in-repo Supabase admin portal is a separate legacy system), and DD/MM/YYYY is the natural Algerian format, so the bad input is plausible. ONE sub-claim is refuted: the alleged 'extend throws a 500' does NOT happen — the extend guard at line 227 (`new Date(lic.subscription_until) > new Date()`) evaluates to false on an Invalid Date, so base falls back to null and addDaysIso(null, days) does not throw; extend returns a normal 200. That embellishment is wrong, but the primary defect (silent lockout from unvalidated 'until') is confirmed, so the finding stands as real.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by trace. license-server/src/index.ts:218 stores admin-supplied `body.until` verbatim (no Date.parse/validation) and line 262 binds it directly into the UPDATE. Input {action:'activate', until:'31/12/2026'} (natural Algerian DD/MM/YYYY) stores subscription_until='31/12/2026'. On the next /v1/license/check (line 133 -> effective()), line 62 `new Date('31/12/2026')` = Invalid Date (verified: month>12 unparseable in V8/Workers). Line 65 `now <= subDate` coerces to `now <= NaN` = false, so an active row derives st='expired'; line 147 returns status:'expired' in the signed token -> the paying restaurant's POS is locked out. That is a concrete, real money/lockout bug. A SECOND real bug is also confirmed: {action:'activate'} with no days/until/plan on a pre-provisioned shell row (subscription_until NULL) sets plan='monthly' but leaves subscription_until NULL, which effective() line 64 treats as a lifetime license -> permanent free 'monthly' license, lost revenue. HOWEVER the reporter's tertiary 'extend throws a 500' claim is FALSE: line 227's guard `new Date(lic.subscription_until) > new Date()` evaluates `Invalid Date > now` = false, so base becomes null and addDaysIso(null,30) uses new Date() and returns a valid ISO string (verified) — no RangeError; addDaysIso is in fact never reached with an invalid base anywhere. Proposed fix is directionally correct for the lockout (validate/reject NaN Date.parse, normalize to ISO) but incomplete: it does not fix the free-lifetime activate path, cannot disambiguate DD/MM dates with day<=12 (e.g. '11/12/2026' silently parses as US Nov 12), and the addDaysIso guard it adds protects a path that cannot currently be triggered.

findings.title: checkTrialStatus never throws NETWORK_ERROR — failed cloud checks are treated as successful verification, defeating the whole trial offline/stale lock
findings.evidence: cloud.ts:118-121: `} catch { // Network error — caller handles this case (offline timer)\n throw new Error('NETWORK_ERROR') }`. This catch is dead code: supabase-js v2 returns fetch failures as `{ data: null, error }` (verified in the installed postgrest-js bundle), so a network failure hits `if (error || !data) return { status: 'not_found' }` (line 100-102) instead. In index.ts checkTrialCloud (lines 199-206), ANY non-throwing result — including this bogus 'not_found' — executes `clearOfflineCountdown(); cumulativeOfflineSeconds = 0; lastCloudSuccessTime = Date.now()`, i.e. a FAILED verification is recorded as a SUCCESSFUL one. The catch at index.ts:233 and the 'Cloud unreachable' catch at trial.ipc.ts:34 are likewise dead.
findings.scenario: A trial machine where the NIC is up but Supabase is unreachable (ISP DNS failure, Supabase outage, or the user simply adding supabase.co to the hosts file): net.isOnline() stays true so checkOfflineInstant never starts a countdown, and every 30s checkTrialCloud gets 'not_found', resets cumulativeOfflineSeconds and refreshes lastCloudSuccessTime — so neither the 2-min offline lock, the 5-min cumulative lock, nor the 10-min stale-cloud lock can ever fire. An expired trial stays fully unlocked indefinitely (the exact enforcement the OFFLINE_LOCK/CLOUD_STALE machinery exists to provide). Same path means an admin deleting a trial row (instead of marking it expired) also leaves the app unlocked forever.
findings.fix: In checkTrialStatus, distinguish error kinds: return 'not_found' only for a genuine zero-row result (error.code === 'PGRST116'); for network-level errors (status 0 / FetchError) throw NETWORK_ERROR as intended. checkTrialCloud then must NOT refresh lastCloudSuccessTime/cumulativeOfflineSeconds on 'not_found' or on throw.

refuter.reason: Verified end-to-end. (1) Installed @supabase/postgrest-js 2.98.0 (dist/index.cjs line 155) converts rejected fetches into a RESOLVED { data: null, error, status: 0 } when shouldThrowOnError is false — the app never calls .throwOnError() and createClient (cloud.ts:12) passes no options — so the catch at cloud.ts:118-121 ('throw new Error(NETWORK_ERROR)') is dead for network failures; checkTrialStatus instead returns { status: 'not_found' } via the error guard at cloud.ts:100-102. (2) checkTrialCloud (src/main/index.ts:201-206) treats ANY resolved result, including this bogus 'not_found', as a successful cloud verification: clearOfflineCountdown(); cumulativeOfflineSeconds = 0; lastCloudSuccessTime = Date.now(); 'not_found' then matches neither the active nor expired/paused branches, so no lock is emitted. (3) In the scenario (NIC up, Supabase unreachable — ISP DNS failure, outage, or hosts-file block), net.isOnline() stays true so the 2-min offline countdown (index.ts:182) never starts, the 5-min cumulative counter never accrues, and the 10-min CLOUD_STALE lock (index.ts:175-180) — built exactly for this case per the comment at line 129 — can never fire because lastCloudSuccessTime is refreshed every 30s by failed checks. (4) No fallback enforcement exists: the renderer locks only on main-process trial:locked/trial:status-update events (App.tsx:42-67); trial_expires_at is used locally only for a cosmetic countdown in SettingsPage. An expired trial (or one whose row an admin deleted — .single() zero rows → PGRST116 → same 'not_found' path) therefore stays fully unlocked indefinitely. The dead catches at index.ts:233 and trial.ipc.ts:34 are also as claimed. Not covered by the excluded 'renderer-side trial lock' item, which concerns where enforcement lives, not this main-process logic never firing.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by independent trace. cloud.ts checkTrialStatus (lines 94-121) never calls .throwOnError(), and the installed @supabase/postgrest-js 2.98.0 bundle (dist/index.cjs lines 50, 155-196) resolves fetch failures as { data: null, error: {message: 'FetchError...'}, status: 0 } instead of rejecting — so the catch{ throw new Error('NETWORK_ERROR') } at cloud.ts:118-121 is dead code and a network failure returns { status: 'not_found' } via lines 100-102. In src/main/index.ts checkTrialCloud (192-236), any non-throwing result unconditionally executes clearOfflineCountdown(); cumulativeOfflineSeconds = 0; lastCloudSuccessTime = Date.now() (lines 204-206), and 'not_found' matches neither the 'active' nor 'expired'/'paused' branches, so no lock event is sent. checkOfflineInstant (170-189) only locks on net.isOnline()===false (countdown) or lastCloudSuccessTime older than 600s — but the 30s checkTrialCloud interval refreshes lastCloudSuccessTime on every failed check, so the stale lock can never fire. No other code compares trial_expires_at to the clock (grep-verified: only writes/passthroughs), and the renderer lock (App.tsx:42-67) is driven solely by main-process events. Concrete repro: expired trial + NIC up but Supabase unreachable (hosts-file block of ijdiiixkemrmkhhkbcng.supabase.co, ISP DNS failure, or Supabase outage) → app stays fully unlocked indefinitely; likewise an admin deleting the trial row. This is distinct from the accepted 'renderer-side trial lock' item because the main process never detects the failure at all. The proposed fix direction is sound (PGRST116 = genuine zero rows; FetchError/status 0 = throw NETWORK_ERROR, letting the existing index.ts:233 catch skip the counter refresh so the 10-min stale lock works), with one implementation note: the network-failure marker `status: 0` is on the resolved response object, not on `error`, so checkTrialStatus must also destructure `status` or match error.code/message.

findings.title: Removing a worker's printer assignment never sticks: stale workers.printer_name keeps routing kitchen tickets to the old printer
findings.evidence: getPrinterForWorker() checks the workers table FIRST and returns early: `if (worker?.printer_name) return worker.printer_name` (printer-assignments.repo.ts:82). saveFullConfig() claims to clear-and-rebuild ("clears everything and rebuilds", line 110) but only clears the printer_assignments table. The companion sync in src/main/ipc/printer.ipc.ts:363-370 only SETS workers.printer_name for workers still present in the new config (`workersRepo.update(workerId, { printer_name: printer.printerName } as any)`) and never clears workers whose 'worker_<id>' task was removed. workersRepo.update() can't clear it anyway: `(input as any).printer_name ?? current.printer_name` (workers.repo.ts:119) coalesces null back to the old value. SettingsPage even re-seeds its UI from workers.printer_name (SettingsPage.tsx:212-213), so the removed assignment visually reappears after save.
findings.scenario: Owner had cook #5's tickets going to printer 'EPSON-A'. The printer is retired, so in Settings he removes cook #5's task from EPSON-A (expecting fallback to the kitchen_all printer) and saves. printer_assignments is rebuilt without the row, but workers.printer_name for cook #5 is still 'EPSON-A'. Every subsequent order with items assigned to cook #5 routes its kitchen ticket to the dead 'EPSON-A' printer (auto-print silently fails), so the kitchen never receives those tickets; reopening Settings shows the assignment back again, making it impossible to remove through the UI.
findings.fix: In the saveFullConfig flow, first clear all worker printer links (`UPDATE workers SET printer_name = NULL`) inside the same transaction, then set printer_name only for workers present in the new config (or change getPrinterForWorker to prefer the printer_assignments table over workers.printer_name).

refuter.reason: Confirmed in working tree. getPrinterForWorker() returns workers.printer_name first (printer-assignments.repo.ts:82) before checking printer_assignments or the kitchen_all fallback. saveFullConfig() only clears the printer_assignments table (:122), and the companion sync in printer.ipc.ts:363-371 — the ONLY writer of workers.printer_name in the codebase — only SETS names for workers present in the new config, never clearing removed ones; workersRepo.update (:119) uses `?? current.printer_name` so even a null can't clear it. Both kitchen ticket paths (printer.ipc.ts:480 and :514) route via getPrinterForWorker, so after removing a worker's printer task, tickets for that worker's items keep going to the stale/retired printer forever. One evidence detail is wrong: the SettingsPage.tsx:212-213 seed goes into `workerPrinters` state that is never rendered, so the removed assignment does NOT visually reappear — the UI shows it removed while routing silently uses the dead printer, making the bug invisible rather than merely annoying. Core claim and scenario stand; proposed fix (clear worker links in the same transaction, or prefer the assignments table) is correct.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by independent trace. (1) getPrinterForWorker (printer-assignments.repo.ts:82) early-returns stale workers.printer_name before consulting printer_assignments or the kitchen_all fallback. (2) saveFullConfig (repo:122) only DELETEs printer_assignments; the companion sync (printer.ipc.ts:364-371) only SETS workers.printer_name for worker_ tasks present in the NEW config and never clears removed ones. (3) Nothing else can clear it: the worker edit form (WorkerManagement.tsx:145-163) omits printer_name, and workers.repo.ts:119 `(input as any).printer_name ?? current.printer_name` coalesces null back to the old value. Concrete repro: cook #5 on 'EPSON-A' (workers.printer_name='EPSON-A' from a prior save), another cook still has a worker task (so split_kitchen_tickets stays 'true' per printer.ipc.ts:360); owner removes worker_5's task and saves; next order with cook #5 items hits printOrder split path -> getPrinterForWorker(5) at printer.ipc.ts:480 -> returns 'EPSON-A' -> ticket prints to the retired printer; manual reprint (printer.ipc.ts:514) misroutes regardless of split. ONE SUB-CLAIM WRONG: the assignment does NOT visually reappear — workerPrinters/handleWorkerPrinterChange (SettingsPage.tsx:77,210-216,415) is dead code never rendered; the visible config UI reads printer_assignments and correctly shows removal, making the misroute silent (worse). Edge case: if the removed task was the ONLY worker_ task, split flips to 'false' and auto-print recovers via getKitchenAllPrinter (printer.ipc.ts:452), but per-worker reprint still misroutes. Proposed fix direction is sound (clear-then-set, or prefer printer_assignments), with caveats: must use direct SQL/dedicated method since workersRepo.update cannot write NULL (the `??` at workers.repo.ts:119), and the clear+set should be inside the saveFullConfig transaction, not the post-hoc IPC loop.

findings.title: Telegram password reset always fails: reset:resetPassword re-validates a one-shot code already consumed by reset:validateTelegram
findings.evidence: Handler 'reset:validateTelegram' (src/main/ipc/activation.ipc.ts:64-66) calls validateTelegramResetCode(code), which CONSUMES the code on success (src/main/activation/activation.ts:112-114: "// Consume the code after successful validation / settingsRepo.set('telegram_reset_code', '')"). The renderer then calls reset:resetPassword(code, newPassword, 'telegram') (src/renderer/src/components/ui/PasswordGate.tsx:200-201), and the handler's telegram branch re-validates: "if (method === 'telegram') { valid = validateTelegramResetCode(code) }" (activation.ipc.ts:75-76) — but the stored code is now '' so it returns false and the handler responds { success: false, error: 'Invalid or expired code' }. The handler's own doc comment (activation.ipc.ts:70) says "method='telegram': validate with local 6-digit code (already validated in renderer, just hash+save)" — the code contradicts it.
findings.scenario: Restaurant owner forgets the admin password, clicks Forgot Password, receives the 6-digit code via the configured Telegram bot, types the CORRECT code (validates OK, advances to the new-password screen), enters the new password twice, and gets 'Invalid or expired code'. The Telegram self-service reset path — the default path when Telegram is configured (PasswordGate.tsx:103) — fails 100% of the time; the owner stays locked out of all admin screens until support issues an HMAC unlock code.
findings.fix: In the 'telegram' branch of reset:resetPassword, do not re-validate (trust the prior validateTelegram step per the comment) — or better, make reset:validateTelegram non-consuming and consume only inside reset:resetPassword. Must be fixed together with the PasswordGate truthiness bug (see separate finding), otherwise removing re-validation lets any wrong code through.

refuter.reason: Confirmed real. Traced the full working-tree path. reset:validateTelegram (src/main/ipc/activation.ipc.ts:64-66) calls validateTelegramResetCode(code), which on a CORRECT code returns true AND consumes the one-shot code by clearing telegram_reset_code/telegram_reset_expires to '' (src/main/activation/activation.ts:113-114). The renderer (src/renderer/src/components/ui/PasswordGate.tsx:128-131) then advances to the new-password step and later calls reset.resetPassword(telegramCode.trim(), newPassword, 'telegram') (PasswordGate.tsx:200-201). The telegram branch of reset:resetPassword re-validates the same code (activation.ipc.ts:75-76 valid = validateTelegramResetCode(code)), but telegram_reset_code is now '' so validateTelegramResetCode hits the `if (!stored ...) return false` guard (activation.ts:105) and returns false, so the handler responds { success:false, error:'Invalid or expired code' } (activation.ipc.ts:80-81). Preload (src/preload/index.ts:227,229) confirms the channel mapping. This directly contradicts the handler's own doc comment (activation.ipc.ts:70 'already validated in renderer, just hash+save'). Net effect: an owner who enters the CORRECT Telegram code passes validation, reaches the new-password screen, then gets 'Invalid or expired code' 100% of the time — the default reset path when Telegram is configured (PasswordGate.tsx:103) is broken. Could not refute.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by end-to-end trace. reset:validateTelegram (activation.ipc.ts:64-66) calls validateTelegramResetCode(code), which on a correct code CONSUMES it (activation.ts:112-115: settingsRepo.set('telegram_reset_code','')). The renderer then calls reset.resetPassword(telegramCode, newPassword, 'telegram') (PasswordGate.tsx:200-201, preload/index.ts:229), and the handler's telegram branch RE-validates via validateTelegramResetCode(code) at activation.ipc.ts:76. Because telegram_reset_code is now '' , the guard `if (!stored || !expiresAt) return false` (activation.ts:105) trips immediately, so valid=false and the handler returns {success:false, error:'Invalid or expired code'} (activation.ipc.ts:80-82). Concrete scenario: owner (Telegram configured, so default resetMethod='telegram' per PasswordGate.tsx:103) requests a code, receives 6-digit code e.g. 482913, types it correctly (validate step succeeds, advances to new-password screen), enters new password twice — and gets 'Invalid or expired code'. Fails 100% of the time on the correct code; the doc comment at activation.ipc.ts:70 ('already validated in renderer, just hash+save') contradicts the code. Proposed fix direction is correct: Option B (non-consuming validateTelegram, consume only in resetPassword) is the more robust choice and, unlike Option A (remove re-validation), does not depend on also fixing the truthiness bug to stay secure.

findings.title: Default printed receipt TOTAL ignores the order's discount — customer sees pre-promo amount
findings.evidence: Line 230: `const subtotal = items.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.total_price, 0)` and lines 263-266 print `${subtotal.toFixed(2)} ${currencySymbol}` labelled 'TOTAL'. But orders.repo.create() stores `total = subtotal - discount` (orders.repo.ts:125-127) and the POS passes promotion discounts (`OrderScreen.tsx:719 discount_amount: currentDiscount`). The default receipt never reads `order.total` or `order.discount_amount` and prints no discount line. (The custom-template path correctly uses `order.total` at line 89, so default vs template receipts disagree.)
findings.scenario: Restaurant runs a promotion (e.g. 200 DA off a 2000 DA order). POS charges 1800 DA, orders table stores total=1800, Telegram/owner dashboard say 1800 — but the printed customer receipt says 'TOTAL 2000.00 DA'. Customer is overcharged if the cashier reads the receipt, or disputes the bill if they paid 1800; every discounted order prints a wrong money total.
findings.fix: In the default receipt HTML use `order.total` for the TOTAL row, and when `order.discount_amount > 0` print subtotal + a 'Discount: -X' line above it (mirroring the template 'total' block).

refuter.reason: Confirmed real money bug in src/main/ipc/printer.ipc.ts. The default customer-receipt renderer computes `subtotal = items.reduce((sum,i)=>sum+i.total_price,0)` (line 230) and prints it as the TOTAL row (lines 264-265: `${subtotal.toFixed(2)} ${currencySymbol}`), with no discount line anywhere in the default template (lines 245-271). Traced the full path: OrderScreen.tsx:719 passes a separate `discount_amount` (from computeDiscount in orderStore.ts) while items keep full price; orders.repo.create() stores item total_price at full price, subtotal=Σtotal_price (pre-discount), and total=subtotal-discount (orders.repo.ts:111-126,158-160); getById does SELECT * so order.total and order.discount_amount are both available. Thus on any discounted order the reduce-computed `subtotal` equals order.subtotal (pre-discount), NOT order.total. The custom-template path is correct by contrast — line 89 uses Number(order.total) and lines 90-92 print a Discount line — so default vs template receipts disagree. The default path is the standard fallback used whenever no active receipt template is configured (getReceiptHTML lines 160-171). Scenario: 2000 DA order with 200 DA promo -> DB/dashboard say 1800, default printed receipt says TOTAL 2000.00 DA. No refutation: discount is only passed when >0, item prices are never pre-discounted, and the fields are populated. Fix: use order.total for the TOTAL row and add a discount line when order.discount_amount > 0, mirroring lines 89-92.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED money bug at src/main/ipc/printer.ipc.ts:230+263-266. Full trace: (1) POS applies a promo, OrderScreen.tsx:719 passes discount_amount:currentDiscount; (2) orders.repo.ts:125-126 stores subtotal, discount_amount, and total=subtotal-discount as three columns; (3) printing calls printOrder→getById (SELECT *, so order.total/subtotal/discount_amount all present)→getReceiptHTML; (4) getReceiptHTML line 162 calls receiptTemplatesRepo.getActiveTemplate(), which returns null on any restaurant with no active custom template (receipt-templates.repo.ts:8-14 — the default/fresh-install state), so execution falls through to the default receipt (lines 226-271); (5) line 230 computes subtotal = sum of item.total_price, which equals the PRE-discount amount because the discount is order-level, not distributed to items; (6) lines 263-266 print that subtotal labelled 'TOTAL' with no discount line and never reads order.total. Concrete failure: 2000 DA order with a 200 DA promo → DB/Telegram/owner-dashboard show total=1800, but the printed customer receipt reads 'TOTAL 2000.00 DA'. Every discounted order prints a wrong total whenever the default (non-custom) receipt is used, which is the out-of-the-box state. The template path (line 88-93) already uses order.total + a discount line, so the two receipt paths disagree exactly as reported. Proposed fix direction is correct: use order.total for the TOTAL row and add a subtotal + 'Discount: -X' line when order.discount_amount>0; both fields exist on the getById object and order.total===subtotal for non-discounted orders, so the change is safe.

findings.title: Analytics sync only ever pushes exactly 'yesterday' — any day the app doesn't run the following day is permanently missing from the owner dashboard
findings.evidence: Line 31: `const yesterdayStr = localDate(new Date(Date.now() - 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000))` — the function unconditionally syncs only the single day 'yesterday', then line 79 `settingsRepo.set('last_analytics_sync_date', today)`. The `lastSync === today` guard (line 24) only prevents same-day re-runs; there is no backfill loop for days between the last successful sync and yesterday.
findings.scenario: Restaurant is closed every Saturday and the POS PC is off. Friday's trading data is supposed to sync on Saturday — but the app never runs on Saturday. On Sunday, syncDailyAnalytics runs with yesterday=Saturday (0 orders, just marks synced) and Friday — typically one of the busiest days — never reaches daily_stats/daily_top_items. This repeats every single week: the owner dashboard permanently under-reports weekly revenue by one full day, with no error anywhere.
findings.fix: Persist the last successfully SYNCED data date (yesterdayStr, not today), and on each run loop day-by-day from lastSyncedDataDate+1 through yesterday, upserting each day's summary (the upserts are already idempotent on (machine_id,date)).

refuter.reason: Confirmed in the working tree: src/main/sync/analytics-sync.ts:31 syncs only the single day 'yesterday' (localDate(now-24h)); the line-24 guard (lastSync===today) only blocks same-day re-runs, and lines 38/79 stamp last_analytics_sync_date=today without recording which data date was actually pushed — no backfill loop exists. Traced the scenario: restaurant closed Saturday with PC off → Sunday's run computes yesterday=Saturday (0 orders, line 37-40 just marks synced) and Friday's data is permanently skipped, silently (catch at line 81 swallows nothing here — it's not even an error path). Refutation attempts failed: repo-wide grep shows daily_stats/daily_top_items are written ONLY by analytics-sync.ts; the owner dashboard (admin/app/api/owner/stats/route.ts:19 → OwnerDashboard.tsx:230) and admin overview (admin/app/admin/overview/page.tsx:30-31) read daily_stats/daily_top_items directly with no reconstruction from owner_orders, which is a separate per-order live feed that never aggregates into daily_stats. Only mitigating nuance: if the POS stays on past local midnight into the closed day, the hourly interval would catch the prior day — but any full off-day (weekly closure, holiday, outage) permanently loses the preceding trading day from the dashboard, exactly as claimed. Proposed fix (persist last synced DATA date, loop day-by-day; upserts already idempotent on (machine_id,date)) is sound.

tracer.reason: Verified by trace. src/main/sync/analytics-sync.ts:31 computes the only synced date as localDate(Date.now()-24h) — purely wall-clock 'yesterday', never derived from last_analytics_sync_date (line 21). Trigger is startAnalyticsSync() (index.ts:525) via 30s setTimeout + hourly setInterval, so nothing runs while the PC is off. Concrete failure: lastSync='2026-06-26' (Fri); PC off Sat 06-27; Sun 06-28 run has today='2026-06-28' ≠ lastSync so guard (line 24) passes, yesterdayStr='2026-06-27', getProfitSummary returns 0 orders (closed Sat) → lines 37-39 mark today synced and return; Friday 06-26 is never queried again since every future run computes yesterday from Date.now() only. analytics-sync.ts is the sole writer of daily_stats/daily_top_items (grep: admin overview/page.tsx:30-31 and api/owner/stats/route.ts:18-23 only read), so the owner dashboard permanently under-reports every weekly closed-day-preceding day and all but one day of any multi-day closure, silently (catch at line 81 is also silent). Proposed fix direction (persist last synced DATA date, loop day-by-day with the idempotent (machine_id,date)/(machine_id,date,rank) upserts) is correct, with two implementation caveats: the existing key semantically stores 'today' so it needs a new key or one-time migration, and first-run/missing-key must be bounded (cap backfill days or start at earliest local order_date); zero-order days must still advance the cursor.

findings.title: syncAllDisplayProfiles makes TV pairing resolve to the LAST named profile instead of the Main Display
findings.evidence: New `syncAllDisplayProfiles()` (cloud-sync.ts:213-218) runs every 5 minutes and re-upserts EVERY profile sequentially, default first: `for (const name of getLocalProfiles()) { try { await syncDisplaySettings(name) } ... }`. Each upsert stamps `updated_at: new Date().toISOString()` and — crucially — `settings._pairing_code = getPairingCode()` (cloud-sync.ts:76), the single machine-wide 4-digit code, into EVERY profile row. The pairing resolver (admin/app/api/pair/route.ts:32-37) selects by `.eq('settings->>_pairing_code', code).order('updated_at', { ascending: false }).limit(1)` and returns `profile = row.profile_name`. Because the loop syncs 'default' first and named profiles after, the last named profile's row is ALWAYS the freshest, so the resolver returns that profile — and this same diff makes the TV app actually honor it: `lanDisplayUrl(ip, port, profile)` appends `?profile=` (MainActivity.kt:165-169) and the route now builds `cloudUrl: .../tv/<id>?profile=<name>` (pair/route.ts:62-64). Before the diff only 'default' was periodically synced (its row stayed freshest) and the TV ignored `profile` entirely.
findings.scenario: Restaurant creates one extra screen profile, e.g. 'menu-board', in Ambiance Screen. From the next 5-minute sync onward, any TV that pairs (or auto-re-pairs after a power cut / POS IP change via the saved code, or runs reprobeLanIfOnCloud) with the 4-digit code from the 'Main Display' tab resolves to profile='menu-board' and permanently loads http://<pos>:3333/display?profile=menu-board — the main customer TV shows the menu-board design instead of the main display, and there is no way to get the default profile via the code at all.
findings.fix: Make the resolver deterministic: prefer the 'default' profile row among matching rows (e.g. `.order('profile_name', ...)` with default-first, or `.eq('profile_name','default')` for the code path), or only stamp `_pairing_code` into the default profile's settings blob in syncDisplaySettings (named profiles are reached via their own ?profile links / short codes anyway).

refuter.reason: Verified end-to-end in the working tree. cloud-sync.ts:76 stamps the single machine-wide 4-digit code (pairing.ts:16-23) into EVERY profile row, and the new syncAllDisplayProfiles (cloud-sync.ts:213-218, wired into the 5-min/initial sync at 255-267, replacing the old default-only syncDisplaySettings() per git diff HEAD) sequentially upserts default first then named profiles (getLocalProfiles keeps default first; AmbianceScreen.tsx:302 appends new profiles last), each stamping updated_at=now — so the last named profile row is strictly freshest after every tick. The resolver (admin/app/api/pair/route.ts:32-37) selects by settings->>_pairing_code ordered by updated_at desc limit 1 with no default preference, returns that row's profile_name, and builds ?profile= cloudUrl (62-64); MainActivity.kt honors it on fresh pairing (278/286), saved-code re-pair after power cut (100-101, 123-134), and reprobeLanIfOnCloud (138-162) via lanDisplayUrl ?profile= (165-169). The code shown to staff is displayed only on the default/Main Display tab (AmbianceScreen.tsx:443). Refutations failed: /api/pair never consults the per-profile short_codes table; the only other syncDisplaySettings caller (tablet.ipc.ts:164, on Ambiance save) is overwritten by the next 5-min loop; sequential awaited upserts preclude timestamp ties. Net effect: with any extra profile (e.g. 'menu-board'), pairing/re-pairing the main TV with the 4-digit code resolves to the named profile instead of the Main Display, with no code path to the default profile. Minor wording caveat only: default can transiently be freshest right after an Ambiance save, until the next periodic sync.

tracer.reason: Verified end-to-end in the working tree. (1) cloud-sync.ts:215-217 syncAllDisplayProfiles iterates getLocalProfiles() sequentially with default guaranteed first (line 205 unshift; AmbianceScreen.tsx:302 appends new profiles after default), so the last named profile's upsert always gets the latest updated_at (line 84). (2) syncDisplaySettings stamps the single machine-wide 4-digit code into EVERY profile row (cloud-sync.ts:76 `settings._pairing_code = getPairingCode()`; pairing.ts:16-23 shows one code per POS, no per-profile code). (3) The pair resolver picks the freshest matching row (admin/app/api/pair/route.ts:32-37 `.order('updated_at', {ascending:false}).limit(1)`) and returns its profile_name plus a ?profile= cloudUrl (lines 52, 62-64). (4) The TV app honors it: MainActivity.kt:278/286 builds lanDisplayUrl(ip,port,profile) appending ?profile= (lines 165-169), persists it as last_url (line 307); reprobeLanIfOnCloud (138-163) and auto re-pair after power cut (retrySaved 122-134) re-resolve the code unattended and lock onto the wrong profile. The UI confirms intent: the code is only shown on the default tab (AmbianceScreen.tsx:443) with a comment that named profiles have no pairing code (line 475). Fix direction is sound — stamp _pairing_code only into the default row (the full settings blob is replaced on each upsert, so stale keys self-clear) or prefer default in the resolver — but the specific `.order('profile_name')` suggestion is fragile since e.g. 'bar' sorts before 'default'; use an explicit eq('profile_name','default') preference instead.

findings.title: markRemoteOrder ignores the update result — a failed 'processed' write leaves the row 'pending' and the order is re-created (duplicated) on next app launch
findings.evidence: Line 79: `await supabase.from('remote_orders').update({ status } as never).eq('id', id)` — the returned `{ error }` is discarded, and the surrounding try/catch never fires because supabase-js returns network failures as error results, not throws. handleRemoteOrder creates the local order FIRST (line 114, with stock deduction, loyalty accrual, auto-print, Telegram) and only then calls `await markRemoteOrder(id, 'processed')` (line 137). The only duplicate guard is the in-memory `inFlight` set (line 22), which is empty after a restart.
findings.scenario: Customer places a remote order; the poll fetches it and ordersRepo.create() succeeds (kitchen ticket prints, stock deducted, loyalty credited), then the connection drops (or Supabase returns 5xx) exactly when markRemoteOrder runs — the failure is silently swallowed and the cloud row stays status='pending'. inFlight blocks re-processing for the rest of the session, but the next time the app starts (restaurants restart the POS daily, or a mid-day crash/update), the 10s poll re-selects the still-pending row and creates the SAME order again: second kitchen print (food cooked twice), double stock deduction, double customer loyalty total_spent/order_count, duplicate row in the owner dashboard.
findings.fix: Make markRemoteOrder return success/failure by checking the update result's `error` (and `count`/returned rows); on failure, retry the status update (e.g. keep the id in a pending-mark queue retried by the poll) and only rely on inFlight meanwhile. Optionally also dedupe on startup by recording processed remote_order ids locally (e.g. a settings/table entry) so a restart can never re-create an already-created remote order.

tracer.reason: Confirmed by code trace. src/main/sync/remote-order-listener.ts:79 discards the supabase update result: `await supabase.from('remote_orders').update({ status } as never).eq('id', id)`. findings.title: Firewall allow-rule is never created: single-quoted rule name breaks both the PowerShell string and netsh parsing, and the function reports success anyway
findings.evidence: const del = `netsh advfirewall firewall delete rule name='${RULE_NAME}'` ... const ps = `$ErrorActionPreference='SilentlyContinue'; Start-Process -FilePath cmd.exe -ArgumentList '/c ${inner}' -Verb RunAs ...`. RULE_NAME is 'Fast Food Manager Display' (contains spaces and is wrapped in single quotes) and `inner` is embedded inside another single-quoted PowerShell string. The inner quotes terminate/reopen the outer PS string, so -ArgumentList receives 7 fragmented arguments ("/c netsh ... name=Fast", "Food", "Manager", "Display; netsh ... name=Fast", ...). cmd.exe then runs ONE mangled netsh command (";" is not a command separator in cmd, and netsh/cmd do not treat single quotes as quoting), so netsh fails with a usage error and no rule is ever added. Additionally `child.on('exit', (code) => resolve(code === 0))` checks powershell.exe's exit code, which is 0 even when Start-Process fails (UAC declined) or netsh errors, because errors are suppressed by SilentlyContinue and Start-Process never propagates the child's exit code — contradicting the doc comment "Resolves true ... false otherwise (incl. declined UAC)".
findings.scenario: Restaurant PC has the network marked Public (the exact case this feature exists for). Owner clicks the TV-setup 'allow firewall' option, accepts the UAC prompt; tablet.ipc.ts `tablet:allowFirewall` returns { ok: true } so the UI reports success. In reality no inbound rule for port 3333 exists, the TV's LAN probe keeps failing, and every TV silently falls back to the slow cloud path (or shows nothing if cloud sync is unavailable). Because the API also returns true when UAC is declined, the failure is undiagnosable from the app.
findings.fix: Run netsh directly with properly escaped double quotes, e.g. build the elevated command as `-ArgumentList "/c netsh advfirewall firewall delete rule name=\"\"Fast Food Manager Display\"\" & netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name=\"\"...\"\" ..."` (use `&` for cmd chaining, escape the outer PS quotes), or simpler: use a rule name without spaces (e.g. FFM_Display) and `&` instead of `;`. To report real success, have the elevated process write a marker (or use `-PassThru`/`$proc.ExitCode` and `exit $proc.ExitCode` in the PS script) instead of powershell.exe's own exit code.

refuter.reason: Core claim CONFIRMED empirically: in firewall.ts lines 26-34, RULE_NAME 'Fast Food Manager Display' embedded as name='...' inside the single-quoted PS argument '/c ${inner}' breaks the string. Reproduced the exact spawn on this Windows machine: PowerShell 5.1 throws ParameterBindingException ('A positional parameter cannot be found that accepts argument Fast'), so Start-Process NEVER executes — no UAC prompt appears, netsh never runs, and the firewall rule is never created. The feature is 100% broken; TVs on Public networks permanently lose the LAN path. However, two sub-claims are wrong: (1) 'reports success anyway' is REFUTED — powershell.exe exits 1 even with SilentlyContinue (verified), so resolve(code===0) is false, tablet:allowFirewall returns {ok:false}, and the UI shows the failed state ('Skipped (still works via internet)'), not success; (2) the mechanism is misdescribed — ArgumentList does not get 7 fragments and cmd never runs a mangled netsh; binding fails before execution, so the scenario's 'accepts the UAC prompt' cannot occur. Real bug at the cited line, but severity is 'feature never works with misleading skip message', not 'silent false success'.

tracer.reason: Core defect CONFIRMED by exact empirical repro: in src/main/tablet/firewall.ts:26-34 the single-quoted RULE_NAME 'Fast Food Manager Display' is nested inside the single-quoted PS -ArgumentList string, so PowerShell fails at parameter binding ("A positional parameter cannot be found that accepts argument 'Fast'", PositionalParameterNotFound). Start-Process never executes: no UAC prompt, no cmd/netsh, and the port-3333 allow rule is NEVER created — the feature is 100% broken on every Windows POS (trigger: AmbianceScreen.tsx:460 button → tablet.ipc.ts:77 → addFirewallRule). HOWEVER, half the claim is wrong: powershell.exe exits 1 even under SilentlyContinue (verified), so resolve(code===0) yields false, tablet:allowFirewall returns { ok: false }, and the UI shows the 'failed' text "Skipped (still works via internet)" — it does NOT report success, and the claimed scenario ("accepts the UAC prompt", "{ ok: true }", "cmd runs one mangled netsh") never occurs since execution dies before cmd/UAC. Net effect the restaurant sees: clicking the button never shows a UAC prompt, always ends in the skipped/failed state, and TVs on Public-profile networks permanently fall back to the slow cloud path. Proposed fix direction is sound: space-free rule name (FFM_Display) + '&' chaining is the robust variant, and the marker/-PassThru + exit $proc.ExitCode part is genuinely required — once quoting is fixed, Start-Process -Wait exits 0 regardless of netsh's result and a declined-UAC error is non-terminating (swallowed by SilentlyContinue → exit 0), which WOULD then create the false-success the reporter described.

findings.title: /api/order accepts fractional, huge, and Infinity quantities — bypasses the forceMenuPrice money defense and can corrupt revenue/loyalty stats
findings.evidence: .filter((it: any) => it && Number.isFinite(Number(it.menu_item_id)) && Number(it.quantity) > 0).map((it: any) => ({ ..., quantity: Number(it.quantity), ... })) — quantity is only checked for `> 0`. `Number('0.001') > 0` and `Number('Infinity') > 0` are both true. orders.repo.ts line 111 then computes `const totalPrice = unitPrice * item.quantity`, so the client-controlled quantity directly scales the money amount that forceMenuPrice was added to protect (comment on line 286-287: "a LAN client could otherwise POST unit_price: 0").
findings.scenario: The self-order QR code is displayed to customers, so any phone on the shop WiFi can POST to /api/order (PIN disabled is the default; with PIN, any paired tablet session works). POST items:[{menu_item_id:5, quantity:0.01}] creates an order for a 500 DA pizza with total 5 DA — it auto-prints to the kitchen and gets made. POST quantity:'Infinity' (or 1e15) stores subtotal/total = Infinity, which flows into daily revenue stats, the owner dashboard sync, and customers.total_spent via the loyalty upsert — permanently garbling reports until manual DB surgery.
findings.fix: Tighten the sanitizer: `const q = Number(it.quantity); Number.isInteger(q) && q > 0 && q <= 99` (or Math.min(Math.floor(q), 99)) before accepting the item; same clamp for menu_item_id (Number.isInteger).

refuter.reason: CONFIRMED. In src/main/tablet/server.ts line 290 the /api/order sanitizer accepts any item whose `Number(it.quantity) > 0`, then passes `quantity: Number(it.quantity)` straight through. This admits fractional ("0.01"), huge (1e15), and Infinity (JSON string "Infinity" -> Number("Infinity") === Infinity, and "Infinity" > 0 is true) values. In orders.repo.ts line 111, `totalPrice = unitPrice * item.quantity`; `forceMenuPrice: true` only fixes unitPrice from the menu, it does NOT bound quantity, so the client-controlled quantity directly scales the money amount. Concrete failures: (1) quantity 0.01 on a 500 DA item creates a real order with total 5 DA that still auto-prints to the kitchen (server.ts 315-316) and gets made; (2) quantity "Infinity" or 1e15 stores subtotal/total = Infinity/huge, which is written to orders and accrued into customers.total_spent via the loyalty upsert (orders.repo 134-138, customers.repo upsertFromOrder) and into daily revenue/dashboard stats, permanently garbling reports. Reachability is real: validateSession (server.ts 174-183) returns true whenever tablet_pin_enabled !== '1', which is the default (setting unset), so any LAN device using the self-order QR can POST without auth. menu_item_id is guarded (invalid id throws -> rollback) but quantity has no such guard; order_items.quantity is INTEGER but SQLite affinity keeps 0.01 as REAL (lossless-only conversion) and there is no CHECK constraint or downstream clamp. The fix (Number.isInteger(q) && q>0 && q<=99) is appropriate.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by full code trace. src/main/tablet/server.ts:290 sanitizes /api/order items with only `Number(it.quantity) > 0`, which passes fractional ('0.001'), Infinity, and huge (1e15) values; line 293 stores `quantity: Number(it.quantity)` unchanged. orders.repo.ts:111 computes `totalPrice = unitPrice * item.quantity` — forceMenuPrice (line 110) protects unit_price but NOT quantity, so the client-controlled quantity directly scales money. Concrete scenarios: (1) default PIN-disabled means any phone on shop WiFi that scanned the self-order QR passes validateSession (server.ts:176) and can POST items:[{menu_item_id:5, quantity:0.01}] → a 500 DA item is recorded/printed to kitchen (server.ts:316) as 5 DA. (2) quantity:'Infinity' or 1e15 stores garbled subtotal/total (orders.repo.ts:158-159), which flows into daily revenue stats, the owner-dashboard upsert, stock deduction (orders.repo.ts:200 → -Infinity/NaN), and — if customer_phone is supplied (server.ts:303) — into customers.total_spent via upsertFromOrder's `total_spent = total_spent + ?` (customers.repo.ts:71), permanently poisoning loyalty until manual DB surgery. No other quantity validation exists on the path. Proposed fix direction is sound: `Number.isInteger(q) && q > 0 && q <= 99` rejects fractional/Infinity/NaN and the <=99 bound is what stops huge integers (Number.isInteger(1e15) is true); tightening menu_item_id to isInteger is harmless but not money-critical.

findings.title: Tablet self-orders are never synced to owner_orders — owner dashboard undercounts revenue by the whole tablet channel
findings.evidence: The POST /api/order handler (lines 300-317) runs `performAutoBackup(); sendOrderNotification(order); printOrder(...)` under the comment `// Same side-effects as normal orders`, but never calls `syncOrderToCloud(order)` (server.ts has no owner-sync import). The other two creation paths do: orders.ipc.ts:24 and remote-order-listener.ts:127. Later `syncOrderStatusToCloud` only does an UPDATE on owner_orders (owner-sync.ts:55-60), which no-ops because the row was never inserted.
findings.scenario: A restaurant using the tablet self-order kiosk: every tablet order is cooked, counted locally, and included in daily_stats, but never appears in owner_orders. The owner's live phone dashboard (api/owner/data sums owner_orders) and the cloud TV queue (api/tv-orders reads owner_orders) miss every tablet order — the dashboard's 'today' revenue is lower than the POS by the entire self-order channel, and daily_stats vs owner_orders disagree for the same day.
findings.fix: Import syncOrderToCloud in server.ts and call `syncOrderToCloud(order).catch(() => {})` after create, exactly like orders.ipc.ts:24 and remote-order-listener.ts:127.

refuter.reason: Confirmed real. In src/main/tablet/server.ts the POST /api/order handler (lines 283-321) creates a real order via ordersRepo.create() at line 300-308 (increments local daily_number, deducts stock, accrues loyalty, appears in daily_stats and the local queue) and at lines 309-316 runs the same side-effects as normal orders (performAutoBackup, sendOrderNotification, auto-print) but never calls syncOrderToCloud. server.ts imports (lines 1-16) have no owner-sync import, and a repo-wide grep confirms server.ts is not among the syncOrderToCloud callers. tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by full code trace. server.ts POST /api/order (lines 283-317) creates the order via ordersRepo.create() at line 300 — a genuine third creation path — then at line 309 sends 'tablet:new-order' to the renderer and runs performAutoBackup()/sendOrderNotification()/printOrder() (lines 311-316) under the comment '// Same side-effects as normal orders', but never calls syncOrderToCloud, and server.ts's imports (lines 1-16) contain no '../sync/owner-sync' import. findings.title: Cloud (support-issued) reset code can never reset the password: renderer maps it to method 'support' whose handler only accepts HMAC unlock codes, and the one-time code is burned at validation
findings.evidence: PasswordGate.tsx:158-170: when the local HMAC check fails, it validates via window.api.reset.validateCloud(...) and on success calls setValidatedMethod('support'). validateCloudResetCode marks the code used immediately (src/main/activation/cloud.ts:187: "await supabase.from('reset_codes').update({ used: true }).eq('id', data.id)"). Then handleResetPassword (PasswordGate.tsx:200-201) invokes reset:resetPassword(code, newPassword, 'support'), whose handler (src/main/ipc/activation.ipc.ts:73-79) runs "valid = validateUnlockCode(code)" — a pure HMAC comparison (activation.ts:84-88). The cloud code already failed that exact check at line 158 (that's the only way the cloud branch is reached), so valid is deterministically false and the reset returns { success: false }.
findings.scenario: Owner forgot the admin password and has no Telegram bot configured; support generates a one-time reset code in the admin dashboard (reset_codes table). The owner types it — validation succeeds, the new-password form appears — then the final step always fails with 'Invalid or expired code', AND the one-time code is already marked used=true in Supabase, so retyping it also fails. Support must issue codes repeatedly with no way to make this path work; only the HMAC unlock code path functions.
findings.fix: Add a 'cloud' method to the reset:resetPassword IPC contract that calls validateCloudResetCode (or trusts the just-validated state), and have PasswordGate pass validatedMethod 'cloud' when cloudValid was the successful check. Alternatively, defer marking the reset_codes row used until the password is actually reset.

refuter.reason: Confirmed by reading the full path. PasswordGate.tsx:160 enters the cloud branch ONLY when local HMAC validateUnlockCode already returned false. reset:validateCloud (trial.ipc.ts:76-79) calls validateCloudResetCode(getMachineId, code), which on success marks used=true immediately (cloud.ts:187) and its lookup filters .eq('used', false) (cloud.ts:174), so the one-time code is burned and cannot be retried. Line 170 unconditionally sets validatedMethod='support' for both local and cloud success. handleResetPassword (PasswordGate.tsx:200-201) then sends code=unlockCode.trim() with method 'support' to reset:resetPassword, whose 'support' branch (activation.ipc.ts:77-79) runs valid=validateUnlockCode(code) — the pure HMAC compare in activation.ts:84-88 against generateUnlockCode(getMachineId()). Both IPC calls execute in the main process with the same deterministic getMachineId() and UNLOCK_KEY, so this is the exact check that already failed in step 1; it deterministically returns false, yielding {success:false, error:'Invalid or expired code'}. There is no cloud fallback in the 'support' branch. If the cloud code had matched the HMAC code, localValid would have been true and the cloud branch never entered, so whenever cloud validation succeeds the final HMAC check is guaranteed to fail. Net effect: support cloud reset validates, burns the code, then always fails the final reset — owner is locked out on that path; only the HMAC unlock-code path works. Preload mappings (index.ts:228-230) confirm the renderer calls route to these exact handlers.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by full cross-file trace. The cloud reset code is a random 8-hex value from admin/lib/keygen.ts:20-24 (generateOneTimeCode), stored in reset_codes — a different code space from the deterministic HMAC unlock code (activation.ts:79-88). Path: PasswordGate.handleValidateUnlockCode (l.158) runs validateUnlockCode(randomCode)=false, then validateCloud (l.162 → trial.ipc.ts:76-79 → cloud.ts:161 validateCloudResetCode) returns valid:true, so it does setValidatedMethod('support') and advances (l.170-171). Final handleResetPassword (l.200-201) sends the random code with method='support' to reset:resetPassword (activation.ipc.ts:73), whose 'else' branch (l.78) runs valid=validateUnlockCode(randomCode) — the identical HMAC check that already failed — so valid is deterministically false and it returns {success:false, error:'Invalid or expired code'} (l.80-82). There is NO code branch in reset:resetPassword that validates a cloud reset_codes code, so this path can never succeed. A restaurant owner with no Telegram bot cannot ever reset a forgotten admin password via support codes; only the HMAC unlock-code path works. Two caveats on the reporter's ancillary claims (they do NOT weaken the core bug): (1) the 'code is burned at validation' sub-claim is doubtful — SETUP.md:131-133 grants the anon key SELECT-only on reset_codes with no UPDATE policy, so cloud.ts:187 .update({used:true}) most likely no-ops under RLS (this is actually a separate finding in the repo's own docs/ffm_findings_raw.json:253). The core defect stands regardless of whether the code is burned. (2) The telegram path shares the same double-validate flaw: handleValidateTelegramCode (l.128 → reset:validateTelegram) calls validateTelegramResetCode which CONSUMES the code on first success (activation.ts:112-115), then reset:resetPassword method='telegram' (activation.ipc.ts:76) re-validates against the now-cleared code and also fails — so both reset flows are broken by the same validate-then-re-validate-a-consumed-code pattern. FIX ASSESSMENT: the proposed direction is sound but must be the 'trust the just-validated state' variant (or defer the burn) applied to BOTH methods; simply adding a method='cloud' that RE-calls validateCloudResetCode in the final step would itself fail if the burn ever succeeds, and would leave the telegram path broken. The best fix makes the final reset step not re-validate an already-consumed/burned one-time code (e.g., a short-lived server-issued or main-process reset token), covering telegram and cloud uniformly.

findings.title: Day Recap queries by UTC date — between 00:00 and 01:00 local it shows the previous day's numbers under today's date
findings.evidence: Line 49: `const today = new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]` feeds getProfitSummary/getTopSellingItems/getOrderTypeBreakdown, which filter on `order_date` — a restaurant-LOCAL date (orders.repo localDate()). The header (line 88) shows the LOCAL date via toLocaleDateString. A `localToday()` util was added at src/renderer/src/utils/localDate.ts for exactly this bug but is only wired into OrdersHistory.
findings.scenario: Algeria (UTC+1), shop open past midnight. Owner opens Day Recap at 00:30 to close the till: `today` = yesterday's UTC date, so the modal shows yesterday's revenue/orders while the header displays today's date, and the orders just rung up at 00:05-00:30 (order_date = local today) are absent. Meanwhile Telegram /today (bot.ts localDate) reports the new local day — the two 'today' numbers disagree every night from 00:00 to 01:00.

refuter.reason: Confirmed end-to-end. DayRecapModal.tsx:49 computes `today` from `new Date().toISOString()` = UTC date, then passes it as start/end to getProfitSummary/getTopSellingItems/getOrderTypeBreakdown, which all filter `WHERE order_date BETWEEN ? tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by full trace. DayRecapModal.tsx line 49 `const today = new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]` yields a UTC date, but the queries it feeds filter on `order_date`, a restaurant-LOCAL date. orders.repo.ts create() (line 92) writes `order_date = localDate()` (local-shifted formula, lines 12-15), and analytics.repo.ts filters `WHERE order_date BETWEEN ?
