findings.title: LAN re-probe switch persists last_url/via_cloud BEFORE verifying the load and ignores load failure — can permanently kill a working cloud display
findings.evidence: In reprobeLanIfOnCloud(): `prefs.edit().putString("last_url", lanUrl).putBoolean("via_cloud", false).apply(); switched = true; ui.post { loadDisplay(lanUrl) { } }`. The prefs are flipped before the LAN page is verified, the loadDisplay result callback is empty `{ }` (no showPairing/scheduleRetry on failure), and `switched = true` ends the 10-minute reprobe chain. This directly contradicts the invariant documented at line 300-301 ("only write last_url AFTER the load is verified... so a dead/HTTP-error URL never becomes the remembered target").
findings.scenario: TV is on the cloud fallback (via_cloud=true). The POS PC comes up with port 3333 accepting TCP but the /display route failing (server still initializing, returns 500, or the profile was deleted → 404). reachable() passes, prefs are rewritten to the broken LAN URL, loadDisplay fails via onReceivedHttpError → onResult(false) → ignored. No retry is scheduled and the reprobe loop has terminated, so the customer-facing menu TV sits on a WebView error page indefinitely. Even after a reboot, connectWithCode probes the LAN first, reachable() still passes (TCP-level only), so the broken LAN URL is chosen again and the cloud fallback is never reached — the README's "The screen always works" promise is broken until someone fixes the POS server.
findings.fix: In the reprobe switch, load the LAN URL first and only persist last_url/via_cloud=false inside a `{ ok -> if (ok) ... }` callback; on !ok, fall back to reloading the saved cloud URL and re-post the 10-minute reprobe (don't set switched=true until the load is verified).

refuter.reason: Confirmed real at MainActivity.kt:153-155 (reprobeLanIfOnCloud). The reachable() check is only a 900ms TCP connect (line 344-353), so it passes the moment the POS's port 3333 socket accepts, even if /display returns 5xx or isn't ready (mid-reboot / mid-auto-update). Line 153 persists last_url=LAN URL and via_cloud=false BEFORE the load is verified; line 154 sets switched=true; line 155 loads with an empty callback {} that swallows the onReceivedError/onReceivedHttpError failure path (lines 221-244 → fail() → onResult(false) → no-op). Because switched=true, line 161 (`if (!switched) ... reprobe in 10min`) never re-arms, and this path calls neither scheduleRetry() nor showPairing(). There is no other in-session recovery (only retryRunnable and the reprobe chain exist as timers; onWindowFocusChanged just hides UI). Result: the customer-facing menu TV strands on a WebView error page until manual power-cycle. This directly violates the invariant the code states at lines 300-301 and correctly implements in connectWithCode (line 307 writes last_url only inside the ok==true callback; lines 309-312 showPairing+scheduleRetry on failure). The onReceivedHttpError handler (237-244) proves the authors expect 5xx pages, making the TCP-open/HTTP-fail window concrete. Could not refute; the proposed fix (verify inside a real callback, revert to cloud + re-post reprobe on failure) is the correct contract.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by trace. findings.title: Date-only 'until' values expire at UTC midnight = 01:00 Algeria time, locking the restaurant out for the entire final paid day
findings.evidence: `return now <= subDate ? { st: 'active', sub } : { st: 'expired', sub }` with `subDate = new Date(sub)`. A date-only admin value like "2026-08-31" (accepted verbatim via the unvalidated 'until' param at line 218) parses as 2026-08-31T00:00:00Z — 01:00 on Aug 31 in restaurant-local UTC+1. "Paid through Aug 31" therefore ends at the START of Aug 31 local, not the end.
findings.scenario: Admin records a payment as {action:'activate', until:'2026-08-31'}. At 01:00 local on August 31 the derived status flips to 'expired' and the POS locks; the restaurant loses the whole last day it paid for and has to call the owner mid-service.
findings.fix: When 'until' matches /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/, normalize it to end-of-day in Africa/Algiers (or at minimum T23:59:59Z) before storing; the addDaysIso() paths are exact-millisecond and unaffected.

refuter.reason: Confirmed on the working tree. license-server/src/index.ts:218 stores body.until verbatim with no validation/normalization (unlike machineId which is regex-checked at line 196), and effective() at lines 62/65 does subDate=new Date(sub); now<=subDate. I verified in Node that new Date('2026-08-31') = 2026-08-31T00:00:00.000Z, which is 01:00 Africa/Algiers (UTC+1); at 05:00 UTC (06:00 local) on Aug 31, now<=subDate is false, so the very next /v1/license/check derives st:'expired'. So a machine set {action:'activate', until:'2026-08-31'} ("paid through Aug 31") locks the POS from ~01:00 local Aug 31 onward, losing the entire final paid business day. The input is realistic and documented: schema.sql:14 calls subscription_until "ISO 8601" (date-only YYYY-MM-DD is valid ISO 8601 and the native output of HTML <input type=date>), and the activate comment invites an "explicit date" while the endpoint validates nothing. The claim correctly excludes the addDaysIso() paths, which emit exact toISOString() timestamps. Beyond the UTC offset, treating a date-only paid-through as start-of-day (midnight) instead of end-of-day is itself a day-losing semantic bug. Confidence is medium (not high) only because this is the untracked WIP license-server skeleton and the failure requires the admin to pass a date-only string rather than a full timestamp; but given the zero validation and documented ISO-date contract, that is the natural case, so the defect is real and concrete.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by trace. Admin path (line 194-219, action:'activate') stores body.until verbatim into subscription_until with no validation/normalization — line 218 `subscription_until: body?.until || ...` short-circuits on any truthy string, and the code comment (line 214) explicitly advertises "explicit date" as a supported input. A paid-through date like '2026-08-31' (the natural form, and exactly what an HTML date picker yields) is saved as-is. In effective() (line 62) `new Date('2026-08-31')` parses per ECMAScript as UTC midnight = 2026-08-31T00:00:00Z = 01:00 Africa/Algiers (UTC+1). Line 65 `now <= subDate ? active : expired` therefore flips to 'expired' at 01:00 local on Aug 31, and handleCheck (line 147) returns status:'expired' — a lock, since the token's st is authoritative and the exp/grace field only covers offline use, not an already-expired status. Concrete state+input: row status='active', subscription_until='2026-08-31'; a /v1/license/check any time after 01:00 local Aug 31 returns 'expired', locking a restaurant that paid through Aug 31 for its entire final business day. The addDaysIso() paths carry the current time-of-day and are unaffected, as the reporter notes. Proposed fix direction is correct: normalizing a /^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$/ until to end-of-day Algiers (or T23:59:59Z) pushes expiry to the end of the local paid day; both variants fix it. Honest caveats that slightly limit real-world blast radius (not the correctness of the defect): (1) license-server is an untracked WIP skeleton with no app-side consumer wired up yet — the shipping app still uses the Supabase trials path in cloud.ts, so this endpoint isn't in the live lock path today; (2) it only triggers on the date-only form of until, not full-ISO. Neither changes that the server's documented behavior is wrong.

findings.title: Signed token contains no request nonce, so a replayed old token defeats revoke/expire; combined with a client clock rollback, indefinitely
findings.evidence: `exp: nowSec + ttlDays * 86400` — the payload {v, mid, st, plan, sub, name, iat, exp} contains nothing that binds the token to the specific check request. The Ed25519 signature (crypto.ts) prevents forging, but replay-freshness rests entirely on the client comparing `exp` to its own local clock — the only clock it has. The design intent stated in the header ('the app can no longer lie about being licensed') is not achieved against replay: the server never learns whether the app actually received a fresh token.
findings.scenario: A restaurant stops paying and the owner hits 'revoke'. On the POS PC, the hosts file redirects the license domain to a tiny local responder that replays the machine's last 'active' token (captured any time in the previous 7 days). The app stays licensed through the whole TOKEN_TTL_DAYS window, and if the machine clock is set back before each launch, forever — the kill switch never lands.
findings.fix: Have the desktop client send a fresh random nonce in the /v1/license/check body; include that nonce in the signed payload; client rejects any token whose nonce does not match the one it just sent. Keep iat/exp purely as the offline-grace window. This must be baked into the token format now, before the client verifier is written.

verifier_notes.refuterReason: The code is quoted correctly (index.ts:143 payload has no nonce), but the claimed bug is not a concrete production defect. (1) license-server/ is an untracked WIP skeleton with only signToken and NO client verifier — grep across src/ and admin/ finds zero consumers of /v1/license/check, the Ed25519 token, graceExp, or a shipped public key; the live app still uses the old Supabase activation path (src/main/activation/cloud.ts). Line 143 currently produces a token nothing reads, so no restaurant experiences any behavior from it. The claim itself admits this ('before the client verifier is written'). (2) The exploit requires the machine OWNER to edit hosts and roll back their own clock to defeat their own license — the same accepted risk class as the explicitly do-not-report items 'renderer-side trial lock' and 'machineId used as a secret'. (3) The replay-within-window is an intentional, documented tradeoff: TOKEN_TTL_DAYS is labeled 'offline grace window' and the field is 'graceExp'; every offline-grace scheme honors a cached token for the grace period by design. (4) The proposed nonce fix is non-responsive: a nonce challenge needs online round-trips, contradicting the offline-grace goal the fix says to keep; under the described hosts redirect the client just falls back to its cached token within the window (revoke still doesn't land for TTL days), and the 'forever via clock rollback' half is unaffected by a nonce since iat/exp are still judged against the local clock. It is a forward-looking design opinion on a not-yet-integrated skeleton, not a concrete working-tree bug.
verifier_notes.tracerReason:
The technical observation is accurate — the signed payload at license-server/src/index.ts:135-144 ({v,mid,st,plan,sub,name,iat,exp}) contains no request-bound nonce, and crypto.ts signs exactly those bytes — but this does NOT qualify as a real, concrete, traceable bug for three reasons:

1) NO ENFORCEMENT CODE EXISTS TO TRACE. The claimed "wrong outcome" (revoke never lands) can only occur inside the CLIENT token verifier that decides to accept/reject the token. That verifier does not exist in the repo. src/main/index.ts still uses the OLD, unrelated licensing path (getMachineId + checkCloudActivation via Supabase + serial/integrity checks, lines 200-502); nothing consumes the Cloudflare Worker's Ed25519 token or its graceExp. The reporter concedes this ("before the client verifier is written"). So there is no execution path from trigger to wrong behavior — it's a design critique of a WIP untracked skeleton, exactly the speculative/future-code category to exclude.

2) IT IS AN ACCEPTED CLASS OF WEAKNESS, NOT A DEFECT. The scenario requires the paying customer to attack their own machine (hosts-file redirect of the license domain + a captured 7-day-old token + local clock rollback). That is DRM piracy, not "wrong behavior a restaurant would experience" in normal operation, and it is the same client-side-trust class the owner has explicitly accepted out of scope (renderer-side trial lock, machineId-as-secret). Replay + clock-rollback is inherent to ANY offline-grace-window license design.

3) THE PROPOSED FIX IS PARTLY WRONG. A per-request nonce only defends the ONLINE fresh-check: a local replay responder can't mint a token bearing the just-sent nonce because it lacks the private key. But the whole design goal is a 7-day OFFLINE grace window (TOKEN_TTL_DAYS, graceExp) where the app must run without the server. During that offline grace the client necessarily compares exp to its own local clock — so the "set the clock back before each launch = licensed forever" half of the scenario survives the nonce fix untouched, and a mandatory online nonce round-trip conflicts with the stated offline-grace requirement. The fix would need clock-tamper detection / monotonic-time anchoring, not just a nonce.

Verdict: technically-true note about a not-yet-wired token format, but not a concrete money/behavior bug in shipping code, and the suggested remedy is incomplete for the very "forever" case it targets.

findings.title: validateCloudResetCode cannot actually mark the code used (anon RLS is SELECT-only) and never checks the update result — 'one-time' support reset codes are reusable for 24h
findings.evidence: Line 187: `await supabase.from('reset_codes').update({ used: true }).eq('id', data.id)` — result discarded, then `return { valid: true }`. Per admin/SETUP.md (lines 131-133) the anon role has only `CREATE POLICY "anon_select_reset_codes" ON reset_codes FOR SELECT` — no UPDATE policy — so under RLS this update silently affects 0 rows. Even if the live policy differed, any failed update still returns { valid: true } because nothing checks the error or affected-row count. The function's own docstring says 'If valid, marks it as used so it can't be reused.'
findings.scenario: Support generates a reset code for a restaurant. Anyone who sees the code (an employee glancing at the owner's phone) can reuse it repeatedly for the full 24h expiry window to reset the admin password via reset:validateCloud, because `used` never flips to true in Supabase. The single-use guarantee the feature is named for does not exist.
findings.fix: Mark the code used server-side where the service key lives (e.g. an admin/Next.js API route or a Postgres RPC with SECURITY DEFINER), or add a scoped anon UPDATE policy; in the client, check the update result (error + affected rows) and return { valid: false } if the consume step failed.

refuter.reason: Confirmed at src/main/activation/cloud.ts:187 — the update({used:true}) result is discarded and {valid:true} is returned unconditionally; admin/SETUP.md:131-133 shows anon RLS on reset_codes is SELECT-only, so under RLS the update silently affects 0 rows and `used` never flips. No other code path consumes the code (only the admin INSERT route and cloud.ts touch reset_codes). The 'one-time' code therefore validates successfully on every call for the full 24h window, contradicting the function's own docstring. One impact caveat: the full password-reset attack does not complete end-to-end because of a SECOND bug — reset:resetPassword (activation.ipc.ts:73-86) re-validates method='support' with the HMAC validateUnlockCode, which a random 8-hex cloud code never matches — so the reused code repeatedly reaches the new-password screen but the final write is rejected. That does not refute the claimed defect (the single-use guarantee genuinely does not exist and the proposed fix is correct); it means the cloud reset feature is additionally broken for legitimate owners, and both must be fixed together.

tracer.reason: Verified by full code trace. src/main/activation/cloud.ts:187 runs `await supabase.from('reset_codes').update({ used: true }).eq('id', data.id)` with the anon client, discards the result, and unconditionally returns { valid: true } (line 189). The repo's own schema doc (admin/SETUP.md:131-133) grants anon only a SELECT policy on reset_codes ("anon can only SELECT (to validate)"); under Postgres RLS an UPDATE with no policy silently affects 0 rows without error, and supabase-js never throws on API errors anyway (it resolves with {error}), so the catch at line 190 can never fire. Therefore `used` never flips to true, and re-entering the same code within the 24h expiry re-matches the SELECT at lines 169-175 (.eq('used', false)) and returns { valid: true } every time — the docstring's one-time guarantee (line 159) is deterministically violated. Concrete repro: support generates a code via admin POST /api/reset/generate (random 8-hex, used=false, 24h); any holder enters it in PasswordGate.tsx:162 → reset:validateCloud (trial.ipc.ts:76) → valid:true → repeat indefinitely for 24h. CAVEAT on scenario severity: the claimed end state ("reset the admin password") is currently blocked by a second bug the reporter missed — after cloud validation PasswordGate uses method='support', and reset:resetPassword (activation.ipc.ts:77-78) validates 'support' with validateUnlockCode (local HMAC code), which the random cloud code never matches, so the final password change fails; reuse today only repeatedly unlocks the new-password screen. The single-use defect itself is real and becomes a full takeover as soon as that companion bug is fixed. Proposed fix direction is right (consume server-side via service-role RPC/route, or scoped anon UPDATE policy + check error/affected rows via .select() after .update()), but incomplete: reset:resetPassword must also accept and atomically consume the cloud code, otherwise the feature cannot complete legitimately and consuming at validate-time burns the code before the password is set.

findings.title: updateItems persists an edited customer_phone but never relinks customer_id or loyalty, so loyalty is lost or credited to the wrong customer
findings.evidence: `const customerPhone = info && 'customer_phone' in info ? info.customer_phone : order.customer_phone` is written into the orders row (line 464-465), but customer_id is never recomputed and the loyalty adjustment at lines 468-472 (`UPDATE customers SET total_spent = MAX(0, total_spent + ?) ... WHERE id = ?` with `order.customer_id`) still targets the ORIGINAL customer. create() only links loyalty at creation time (lines 131-142). OrderScreen.tsx:686 really does send customer_phone in the info object on edit.
findings.scenario: Cashier creates an order without a phone (customer_id NULL). The customer then asks to attach their loyalty number, so the cashier edits the order and adds the phone. The order header now shows the phone, but no customers row is created or updated — total_spent/order_count never accrue and the order never appears under that customer in the Loyalty dashboard. Conversely, if the phone is corrected from customer A's number to customer B's, the spend stays on A's record, and a later cancelOrder() reverses the total from A while the order displays B's phone.
findings.fix: In updateItems, when the effective customer_phone differs from order.customer_phone: reverse the old accrual on order.customer_id (total_spent - order.total, order_count - 1), call customersRepo.upsertFromOrder(newPhone, total, customerName) for the new phone, and write the returned id into orders.customer_id (NULL when the phone is removed); only fall back to the existing delta logic when the phone is unchanged.

refuter.reason: Confirmed in the working tree. orders.repo.ts updateItems (lines 457-465) persists an edited customer_phone onto the order but never calls customersRepo.upsertFromOrder and never writes customer_id — upsertFromOrder's only caller in src/main is create() (line 134), and the IPC handler (orders.ipc.ts:57-81) adds no relinking. The loyalty adjustment at 468-472 targets the stale order.customer_id, as do cancelOrder (347-351) and cancel-restore (302-306). Result: a dine-in order edited to delivery gets a phone but customer_id stays NULL (no loyalty accrual, invisible in getCustomerOrders), and a corrected phone leaves loyalty accruing/reversing against the old customer while the order shows the new phone. tracer.reason: Confirmed by full trace. OrderScreen.tsx:641-690 (edit mode) sends info.customer_phone via updateItems; validation at OrderScreen.tsx:645 forces a phone on dine-in→delivery edits, so this is the feature's primary flow. In orders.repo.ts updateItems, line 459 picks up the new phone and the UPDATE at 463-465 persists it, but the statement has no customer_id column and the function never calls customersRepo.upsertFromOrder (unlike create() at lines 131-142/162). findings.title: updateItems changes customer_phone on the header but never re-links customer_id — loyalty delta credited to the wrong (or no) customer

findings.title: performAutoBackup / backup:createNow copy the raw .db without a WAL checkpoint — every external backup is missing the newest committed orders
findings.evidence: `copyFileSync(dbPath, destPath)` copies only the main file while the DB runs in WAL mode (connection.ts:59 `journal_mode = WAL`). Committed transactions live in fastfood-manager.db-wal until a checkpoint. Contrast with database/backup.ts:31 which correctly runs `db.pragma('wal_checkpoint(FULL)')` before copying. performAutoBackup is called right after each order commit (orders.ipc.ts:15), so the very order that triggered the backup is still WAL-only and absent from the copy; settings:resetAll (settings.ipc.ts:119) uses this same checkpoint-less copy as the 'backup before factory reset' and then resetAllData deletes the -wal file.
findings.scenario: Owner presses Logout (factory reset): performAutoBackup snapshots the .db, resetAllData deletes db+wal — the last ~minute of orders (everything since the live-backup's 60s checkpoint) is permanently absent from the pre-reset backup in their configured backup folder. Same staleness applies to the nightly scheduled backup and every per-order USB backup they might restore after a disk failure.
findings.fix: Call `getDb().pragma('wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)')` (or use better-sqlite3's `db.backup(destPath)`) in performAutoBackup and the createNow handler before copyFileSync.

refuter.reason: Confirmed on the working tree. connection.ts:59 enables WAL with no autocheckpoint override, so committed transactions live in fastfood-manager.db-wal until a checkpoint. performAutoBackup (backup.ipc.ts:15-36) and backup:createNow (line 70-92) copy ONLY the main file (lines 28, 84) with no wal_checkpoint and never copy the -wal sidecar. The correct pattern exists elsewhere (database/backup.ts:31 runs wal_checkpoint(FULL) then also copies -wal at 37-41), proving the external-backup path is simply missing it. performAutoBackup runs right after each order commit (orders.ipc.ts:13-15) with no checkpoint in between, so the triggering order is WAL-only and absent from the copy. Factory reset is real: settings.ipc.ts:117-124 calls performAutoBackup() then resetAllData(), and resetAllData (connection.ts:81-90) deletes db + -wal + -shm, permanently losing the WAL orders the stale backup omitted. Skeptical note: the live-backup system is running (index.ts:356) and checkpoints every 60s (backup.ts:100-102,31), which bounds the loss to orders committed since the last checkpoint (~1 min) rather than the whole WAL — this bounds severity but does not refute the bug; the claim's scenario already states this window accurately. Net effect: restoring an external/USB or pre-reset backup silently loses up to ~1 minute of the newest real orders. Could not refute.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED. backup.ipc.ts:28 (performAutoBackup) and :84 (backup:createNow) do copyFileSync(dbPath, destPath) with no WAL checkpoint and no -wal sidecar copy, while the DB runs in WAL mode (connection.ts:59) on a long-lived singleton connection that is never closed during operation. Committed orders sit in fastfood-manager.db-wal until a checkpoint, so these external copies miss them. The sibling database/backup.ts:31 does it correctly (wal_checkpoint(FULL) first). Callers confirmed: orders.ipc.ts:15 after every ordersRepo.create, tablet server.ts:311, remote-order-listener.ts:128, scheduled backup at backup.ipc.ts:204, and settings.ipc.ts:119 (settings:resetAll) which runs performAutoBackup then resetAllData() (connection.ts:81-90) deleting .db/-wal/-shm. Concrete scenario: last live checkpoint at 14:00:00; orders #145-147 committed to WAL at 14:00:15/30/45 (WAL far below the 1000-page autocheckpoint threshold, so no auto-flush; main .db still reflects 14:00:00); owner presses Logout at 14:00:50 -> resetAll copies the stale main .db to backup_paths, then deletes .db+.db-wal+.db-shm -> orders 145-147 permanently gone from the only surviving external backup. Same staleness hits every per-order USB backup restored after a disk failure. Staleness is bounded to ~60s because the live-backup system (database/backup.ts, started index.ts:356) runs wal_checkpoint(FULL) on the shared connection every 60s (the reporter's '60s checkpoint' framing is accurate), so this is real-but-bounded data loss, not unbounded. Fix direction is correct: checkpoint (FULL/TRUNCATE) before copyFileSync mirrors the existing correct pattern, and single-connection means TRUNCATE won't be blocked. Caveat on the alt fix: better-sqlite3 db.backup() is async, so performAutoBackup/createNow would need to become async to use it; the primary proposed fix (pragma checkpoint before copy) is sound and sync.

findings.title: Kitchen tickets are rendered at the RECEIPT printer's paper width — per-printer width/font settings are ignored
findings.evidence: getReceiptHTML uses one global value for both ticket types: `const paperWidth = parseInt(settings.printer_width || '80')` (line 173, also line 39 in buildFromTemplate). printer:saveFullConfig syncs that key from the receipt printer only: line 355 `printer_width: receiptPrinter?.paperWidth || ...`. The per-assignment `paper_width`/font columns exist and repo helpers `getReceiptSettings()`/`getKitchenSettings()` were written for this (printer-assignments.repo.ts:38-59) but are never called.
findings.scenario: Settings UI lets the owner set Printer 1 (receipt) = 80mm and Printer 2 (kitchen) = 58mm. Every kitchen ticket is generated with `body{width:72mm}` and printed on the 58mm printer: long item names and notes are clipped off the right edge of every kitchen ticket, and the per-printer kitchen font size choice does nothing.
findings.fix: In printOrder/printOrderForWorker resolve width+font from the matched assignment (use getKitchenSettings()/getReceiptSettings(), falling back to settings) and pass them into getReceiptHTML instead of reading global printer_width.

refuter.reason: Confirmed real for the paper-width defect. getReceiptHTML (src/main/ipc/printer.ipc.ts:173) reads a single global settings.printer_width for BOTH kitchen and receipt tickets and derives maxWidth = paperWidth===58?'48mm':'72mm' (line 174), applied to the kitchen body at line 195. printer:saveFullConfig syncs that global key from the receipt printer only (line 355: printer_width: receiptPrinter?.paperWidth ...), where receiptPrinter is the assignment tagged 'receipt' (line 349). The per-printer paper_width is genuinely stored per assignment (printer-assignments.repo saveFullConfig + migration 010) and the Settings UI exposes an independent 58/80mm select per printer (SettingsPage.tsx:1043-1050). The purpose-built helpers getReceiptSettings()/getKitchenSettings() (printer-assignments.repo.ts:38-59) are defined but never called (grep over src finds only definitions). Concrete failure: receipt=80mm, kitchen=58mm makes printer_width='80', so every kitchen ticket renders body{width:72mm} and prints on the 58mm printer, clipping item names/notes on the right edge — on all kitchen paths (printOrder lines 454/487, printOrderForWorker 517). NOTE: the scenario's secondary claim that per-printer kitchen FONT does nothing is inaccurate — kitchen_font_size is correctly synced from the kitchen printer (line 357) and read at line 188. But the anchored line-173 width bug is real and restaurant-visible, so the finding stands.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by full code trace. Kitchen tickets are rendered at the receipt printer's paper width because getReceiptHTML (src/main/ipc/printer.ipc.ts:173) reads the global `settings.printer_width`, and printer:saveFullConfig syncs that legacy key ONLY from the receipt printer: line 355 `printer_width: receiptPrinter?.paperWidth || config.assignments[0]?.paperWidth || '80'` (receiptPrinter = the assignment whose tasks include 'receipt'). The kitchen printer's own paper_width lives in its printer_assignments row but is never read at print time. Concrete scenario: owner sets Printer 1 (receipt task) = 80mm and Printer 2 (kitchen_all task) = 58mm via the per-printer width selector (SettingsPage.tsx:1042-1045, bound to config.paperWidth). saveFullConfig writes settings.printer_width='80'. Any kitchen print (printer:printKitchen button, or auto-print from orders.ipc.ts:22 / tablet/server.ts:316 / remote-order-listener.ts:131) -> printOrder(orderId,'kitchen') -> line 452 correctly targets the 58mm kitchen printer via getKitchenAllPrinter(), but line 454 calls getReceiptHTML(order, settings, 'kitchen'); line 173 paperWidth=80 -> line 174 maxWidth='72mm' -> line 195 body width:72mm printed on the 58mm printer (printable ~48mm), so long item names/notes clip off the right edge of every kitchen ticket. The helper methods getReceiptSettings()/getKitchenSettings() (printer-assignments.repo.ts:38-59) that would return the correct per-assignment paper_width are never called anywhere (grep confirms only the definitions plus the bug-report doc). CAVEATS: (1) The reporter overstates the font part — kitchen_font_size IS synced from the kitchen printer at line 357 (kitchenPrinter?.kitchenFontSize) and is read at line 188, so the per-kitchen-printer font choice DOES take effect for the single-kitchen-printer case; only the WIDTH is broken. (2) The proposed fix (route width via getKitchenSettings()/getReceiptSettings() into getReceiptHTML) is directionally correct for width but incomplete: getKitchenSettings() uses LIMIT 1, so in split-by-worker mode with multiple kitchen/worker printers of differing widths it still won't give each its own width — a fully correct fix should resolve paper_width from the specific matched assignment/printer used for each ticket.

findings.title: Removing a worker's printer task never clears workers.printer_name — tickets keep going to the old (possibly removed) printer
findings.evidence: saveFullConfig only SETS overrides: `for (const task of printer.tasks) { if (task.startsWith('worker_')) { ... workersRepo.update(workerId, { printer_name: printer.printerName }...) } }` — workers whose task was unchecked are never reset to null. getPrinterForWorker checks the workers-table override FIRST (printer-assignments.repo.ts:78-82), so it wins over the freshly rebuilt printer_assignments table forever.
findings.scenario: Owner had 'Kitchen: Ali' assigned to Printer B, then Printer B breaks and they remove that assignment in Settings (expecting Ali's items on the main kitchen printer). Ali's split kitchen tickets still resolve to 'B'; doPrint fails silently (auto-print ignores the result via `.catch(() => {})` in orders.ipc.ts:22), so Ali's items never reach the kitchen.
findings.fix: In the saveFullConfig handler, first clear all overrides (`UPDATE workers SET printer_name = NULL`) inside the same transaction, then re-apply the ones present in config.assignments.

refuter.reason: Confirmed real. In src/main/ipc/printer.ipc.ts the saveFullConfig handler (loop at lines 364-371) only SETS workers.printer_name for workers whose worker_<id> task is present in the incoming config; it never clears the override for workers whose task was removed. Grep confirms the only two writers of workers.printer_name are workers.repo.ts update() and this loop — no `UPDATE workers SET printer_name = NULL` exists anywhere. getPrinterForWorker (printer-assignments.repo.ts:78-82) reads the workers-table override FIRST and returns it if non-null, so it beats the rebuilt printer_assignments fallback chain (worker row -> kitchen_all -> default). The split-kitchen path (printer.ipc.ts:479-481) uses getPrinterForWorker per worker. The renderer savePrinter (SettingsPage.tsx:312-323) sends the full config and, when a worker task is unchecked, simply omits worker_<id> from tasks — with no separate call to clear the override; the post-save reload rebuilds the UI only from printer_assignments, so the stale workers.printer_name is invisible. Concrete failure: owner assigns Ali->Printer B, B breaks, owner removes the assignment expecting fallback to the main kitchen printer; workers.printer_name for Ali stays 'B', getPrinterForWorker returns 'B' (so the `|| settings.kitchen_printer_name` fallback never fires), and Ali's split kitchen ticket prints to dead printer B. orders.ipc.ts:22 auto-kitchen-prints with `.catch(() => {})` and doPrint resolves {success:false} instead of throwing, so the failure is swallowed silently and Ali's items never reach the kitchen. Could not refute.

tracer.reason:
CONFIRMED by full trace. saveFullConfig (src/main/ipc/printer.ipc.ts:364-371) only SETS workers.printer_name for worker_ tasks present in the new config (via workersRepo.update, workers.repo.ts:103-119); it never clears workers whose worker_ task was removed. getPrinterForWorker (printer-assignments.repo.ts:76-82) checks the workers table FIRST and returns worker.printer_name at line 82 before consulting the freshly-rebuilt printer_assignments table, so a stale override wins forever. printOrder's kitchen split branch (printer.ipc.ts:479-480) uses getPrinterForWorker, and auto-print swallows failures via printOrder(order.id,'kitchen').catch(()=>{}) (orders.ipc.ts:22).

Concrete state: Ali=worker_5->Printer B and Fatima=worker_6->Printer C both saved (workers.printer_name='B' for Ali, split_kitchen_tickets='true'). Printer B breaks; owner unchecks Ali's task but keeps Fatima, saves. split stays 'true' (worker_6 present, line 360) and printer_assignments loses Ali's worker row, but the loop only re-updates worker_6, leaving Ali's workers.printer_name='B'. Next order with Ali's items -> split branch -> getPrinterForWorker(5) returns stale 'B' -> doPrint to the dead printer fails, error swallowed, Ali's kitchen ticket silently lost.

Caveat on scope: the bug only manifests when at least one OTHER worker assignment survives (keeping split_kitchen_tickets='true'); the reporter's literal 'remove the only assignment' would flip that setting to 'false' and route through getKitchenAllPrinter, avoiding the stale override. The realistic multi-station case triggers it. Proposed fix direction (UPDATE workers SET printer_name=NULL then re-apply, ideally inside the same transaction as the printer_assignments rebuild) is correct and targets the root cause.

findings.title: Receipts are loaded as a data: URL — a large logo file pushes the URL past Chromium's 2MB limit and every print times out
findings.evidence: `printWin.loadURL(`data:text/html;charset=utf-8,${encodeURIComponent(html)}`)` embeds the logo inline: getLogoHTML (lines 25-28) base64-encodes the raw logo file with no size limit, and settings:uploadLogo (settings.ipc.ts:83) copies the user's original file unresized. A ~1.5MB+ logo → >2MB base64 → the data URL exceeds Chromium's max URL length, loadURL never fires did-finish-load, and the promise only resolves via the 10s timeout at line 552 ('Print timeout').
findings.scenario: Restaurant uploads its logo straight from a phone photo (3-5MB JPEG) in Settings > General. From then on every receipt and preview that includes the logo waits 10 seconds then fails with 'Print timeout' — receipts stop printing entirely, with no hint that the logo is the cause.
findings.fix: Downscale/re-encode the logo on upload (e.g. nativeImage resize to ≤300px, save as PNG), and/or load the print HTML via a temp file (loadFile) instead of an encodeURIComponent data URL.

refuter.reason: Verified all three cited facts in the working tree. settings.ipc.ts:83 copies the uploaded logo unresized (copyFileSync of the original file); no image resize exists anywhere (grep: no nativeImage/resize; renderer handleUploadLogo just stores the returned path). printer.ipc.ts:25-28 (getLogoHTML) base64-encodes the raw logo bytes and inlines them with no size cap. printer.ipc.ts:530 (doPrint) navigates a printWin via loadURL('data:text/html;charset=utf-8,'+encodeURIComponent(html)). Critically, doPrint (lines 532-557) only registers did-finish-load plus a 10s timeout — there is NO did-fail-load handler and NO catch on the un-awaited loadURL promise, so a failed navigation resolves ONLY via the timeout, returning {success:false,error:'Print timeout'}. Numerically the mechanism triggers: Chromium's hard max URL length is 2MB (url::kMaxURLChars=2*1024*1024); a 3-5MB phone-photo logo → base64 ~4-6.7MB → encodeURIComponent tripling of +///= adds ~6% → data URL far exceeds 2MB (even a ~1.5MB logo crosses it). The oversized-URL navigation fails, did-finish-load never fires, and every customer receipt (getReceiptHTML always calls getLogoHTML) hangs 10s then fails; kitchen tickets omit the logo and still print, matching the 'receipts stop with no obvious cause' symptom. Minor overreach in the evidence: previewReceipt returns HTML directly to the renderer (line 298) and does not go through doPrint, so preview does not time out — but the core bug (actual receipt PRINTING breaks after a large logo upload) is real and concrete. Only caveat is I asserted Chromium/Electron loadURL behavior from established knowledge rather than a runtime test, but the 2MB URL cap and did-finish-load semantics are well-documented and the code has zero mitigation.

tracer.reason: Confirmed by full trace. settings.ipc.ts:83 copyFileSync stores the uploaded logo unresized with no size cap; getLogoHTML (printer.ipc.ts:25-28) base64-encodes it inline with no limit; the default receipt (getReceiptHTML line 246) always embeds it; doPrint line 530 makes the entire HTML the navigation URL via loadURL(`data:text/html;...${encodeURIComponent(html)}`). A ~1.5MB image → ~2MB base64, and a 3-5MB phone photo → 4-6.6MB base64, both exceeding Chromium's url::kMaxURLChars (2MB). The over-length data URL is refused: did-finish-load (line 532) never fires, webContents.print is never called, and the promise resolves only via the 10s setTimeout (lines 552-557) as {success:false,error:'Print timeout'}. printOrder('receipt') runs automatically on new/remote/tablet orders (orders.ipc.ts:21, remote-order-listener.ts:130, server.ts:315) and manual buttons, so every receipt hangs 10s then fails. Two minor scenario corrections that don't change the verdict: kitchen tickets don't embed the logo (kitchen HTML lines 191-224 omit getLogoHTML) so they still print, and printer:previewReceipt returns HTML to the renderer without loadURL so preview doesn't time out. Fix direction is correct: nativeImage resize on upload is the proper root fix; loadFile via temp file is a valid secondary mitigation but alone (without shrinking) would print a broken/missing logo, so the resize is the load-bearing change.

findings.title: daily_stats is a one-shot snapshot taken while the shop is still open — later cancellations/edits of that day's orders never re-sync
findings.evidence: Lines 21-24: `const lastSync = settingsRepo.get('last_analytics_sync_date'); if (lastSync === today) return` — the sync for `yesterdayStr` runs once, on the first hourly tick after local midnight (interval at line 95 fires every hour, initial run 30s after launch), then is locked for the whole day at line 79.
findings.scenario: Shop open until 02:00 local. At ~00:30 the hourly tick syncs 'yesterday' (the trading day that just ended) to daily_stats while several of its orders are still status 'preparing'. At 01:30 staff cancels one of those orders (300 DA) from Orders History; ordersRepo.cancelOrder excludes it locally, but daily_stats was already synced and `lastSync === today` blocks any re-run — the owner dashboard week view (api/owner/stats reads daily_stats) permanently overstates that day by 300 DA versus the POS analytics/Telegram.
findings.fix: Re-upsert yesterday's row on a later tick (e.g. also sync when the current summary differs), or delay the daily sync a few hours past midnight and additionally re-sync the previous date once more the following day.

refuter.reason: Confirmed by reading the full path. analytics-sync.ts:24 (`if (lastSync === today) return`) + :79 (`settingsRepo.set('last_analytics_sync_date', today)`) form a hard one-shot-per-day lock: once yesterday (day D) is synced on the first hourly tick after local midnight, every later tick that day returns early, and subsequent days only sync their own yesterday (D+1) — day D is never revisited. getProfitSummary (analytics.repo.ts:4-12) recomputes live from `orders ... WHERE status != 'cancelled'`, so it counts still-'preparing' orders at sync time and drops them after cancelOrder (orders.repo.ts:317-320) flips status to 'cancelled'. But daily_stats is already upserted and frozen. The owner week/month view (admin/app/api/owner/stats/route.ts:18-25) reads only daily_stats, and grep confirms daily_stats has no other writer or backfill. Concrete failure: shop open past midnight, day-D order (300 DA) still 'preparing' when the ~00:30 tick syncs day D; staff cancels it at 01:30; daily_stats stays inflated by 300 DA permanently versus POS analytics/Telegram. Bug is even broader — any same-day-as-sync or later correction of an already-synced day is swallowed. line 30's 'complete day' assumption is false whenever the trading day's orders can still change after the sync fires. Could not refute: the guard truly blocks re-sync, the summary truly drifts, and daily_stats is the sole dashboard source.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by full trace. analytics-sync.ts:20-24 gates on `if (lastSync === today) return`, so once date D is synced (on the first tick after local midnight on day D+1 via the 30s timeout / hourly interval at lines 90-97), daily_stats for date D is frozen for the rest of that day; the next day's run targets date D and never revisits D. analytics.repo.ts:7-12 getProfitSummary sums `status != 'cancelled'`, a LIVE projection, while the upserted daily_stats snapshot (lines 47-57) was taken with the order still counted. orders.repo.ts:317-320 cancelOrder sets status='cancelled' on any order id with no date restriction; OrdersHistory.tsx:58 exposes window.api.orders.cancel to staff for past orders. admin/app/api/owner/stats/route.ts:18-25 reads the week/month view straight from daily_stats, never recomputing. Concrete scenario: a 300 DA order with order_date=D placed at 23:45, shop open past midnight; the ~00:30-01:00 tick on D+1 syncs date D while the order is still 'preparing'; at 01:30 staff cancel it — local analytics/Telegram drop it, but lastSync===today (D+1) blocks any re-run, so daily_stats for D permanently overstates revenue by 300 DA. The bug is actually broader than the reporter's midnight edge case: ANY cancellation/edit of a date-D order made after that morning's sync (e.g. voiding last night's fraudulent order at 9 AM) is lost forever, because daily_stats is treated as a write-once snapshot instead of an idempotent projection. Fix-direction note: the reporter's second proposal (delay a few hours + one extra re-sync the following day) is only a partial mitigation — a cancellation/dispute two or more days later is still missed. The correct fix is to drop the 'already synced today' short-circuit for a rolling recent window and idempotently re-upsert the last N days (daily_stats AND daily_top_items) every tick; the existing onConflict machine_id,date makes that safe.

findings.title: daily_stats / daily_top_items upsert errors are never checked, then the day is marked synced — a transient failure permanently drops that day's stats
findings.evidence: Line 47: `await supabase.from('daily_stats').upsert({...}, { onConflict: 'machine_id,date' })` and line 65 daily_top_items upsert — neither result's `error` is inspected, and supabase-js reports network/RLS/5xx failures via the result object rather than throwing, so the catch at line 81 does not fire. Execution falls through to line 79 `settingsRepo.set('last_analytics_sync_date', today)`, and the `lastSync === today` guard plus the yesterday-only logic mean the day is never retried.
findings.scenario: The 30-second post-startup sync runs; net.isOnline() was true at line 16 but the Wi-Fi drops (or Supabase returns a 5xx) during the upsert. Both writes fail silently, the day is stamped as synced, and yesterday's order_count/revenue/top-items never appear in the owner dashboard — permanently, since tomorrow's run targets a different date.
findings.fix: Destructure `{ error }` from each upsert; if any write failed, log and return WITHOUT setting last_analytics_sync_date so the hourly interval retries the same day.

refuter.reason: Confirmed. In src/main/sync/analytics-sync.ts the daily_stats upsert (line 47) and daily_top_items upserts (line 65) never inspect the result's `error`, and line 79 unconditionally stamps last_analytics_sync_date. Installed @supabase/postgrest-js 2.98.0 provably returns both HTTP errors and fetch/network rejections via the resolved result object when throwOnError() is not used (PostgrestBuilder.ts: shouldThrowOnError=false default, line 212 throws only if shouldThrowOnError, lines 227-228 catch fetch rejections into a resolved { error }), so the catch at line 81 cannot fire for these failures. getClient() (src/main/activation/cloud.ts) is a plain createClient with no throwOnError. last_analytics_sync_date is set nowhere else, the lastSync===today guard blocks the hourly retry, and the sync targets only yesterdayStr — so a transiently failed day is permanently dropped. daily_stats has no other writer, and the owner dashboard (admin/app/api/owner/stats/route.ts and admin/app/admin/overview/page.tsx) reads daily_stats/daily_top_items directly with no fallback, so the restaurant owner permanently loses that day's revenue/order stats. net.isOnline() only checks interface state, making the mid-upsert failure scenario realistic.

tracer.reason: Verified by trace. src/main/index.ts:525 starts the sync; 30s after launch syncDailyAnalytics() runs. analytics-sync.ts:47 and :65 await supabase upserts to daily_stats/daily_top_items WITHOUT reading the result — supabase-js v2 (package.json ^2.98.0, plain createClient in cloud.ts:12, no throwOnError) returns 5xx/RLS/network failures via the resolved { error } object (fetch rejections are caught inside PostgrestBuilder.then and returned with status 0), so the catch at line 81 never fires. Execution falls through to line 79 settingsRepo.set('last_analytics_sync_date', today), and line 24's lastSync===today guard blocks the hourly retries; next day line 31 targets a new yesterdayStr, so the failed date is never re-attempted. Concrete scenario: Wi-Fi drops (or Supabase 5xx) between the net.isOnline() check at line 16 and the upserts on a day that had orders — yesterday's revenue/order-count/top-items are permanently absent from the owner dashboard, which reads exactly these tables (admin/app/admin/overview/page.tsx:30-31, admin/app/api/owner/stats/route.ts:19). Proposed fix is correct in direction: check { error } on every upsert and return without stamping last_analytics_sync_date so the hourly timer retries; safe because both writes are idempotent upserts on (machine_id,date[,rank]). Minor edge: on retry after a partial top-items write, stale higher-rank rows could linger if the top-10 list changed, but that is negligible vs the current permanent drop.

findings.title: Active promotions are applied only by the POS renderer — tablet self-orders and remote orders always pay full price
findings.evidence: Remote orders: `ordersRepo.create({ ... forceMenuPrice: true, items: validItems })` (lines 114-121) with no discount_amount; tablet: server.ts:300-308 likewise. computeDiscount lives only in src/renderer/src/store/orderStore.ts (line 60), so no main-process creation path ever computes a promo discount — while the customer-facing ambiance/TV display advertises the same active promotions in its 'Special Offers' panel (display-ui.ts:801-821, fed from promotionsRepo.getActivePromotions in server.ts:45).
findings.scenario: Owner activates a '20% on everything' promotion. The TV in the dining room advertises it. A customer orders 1000 DA of items on the self-order tablet and is charged 1000 DA (order_number receipt total), while the identical order rung at the counter costs 800 DA. Remote/online orders are likewise charged full price. Channel-dependent pricing that contradicts the advertised promo.
findings.fix: Move promo discount computation into the main process (e.g. a computeDiscount in promotions.repo used by ordersRepo.create when forceMenuPrice is set), so tablet/remote orders get discount_amount/discount_details like POS orders.

refuter.reason: CONFIRMED. ordersRepo.create() (src/main/database/repositories/orders.repo.ts:90-229) applies a discount ONLY from the caller-supplied input.discount_amount (line 125: `const discount = Math.min(Math.max(0, input.discount_amount ?? 0), subtotal)`); it performs no active-promotions lookup. The only code that computes promo discounts is computeDiscount, which exists exclusively in the renderer store (src/renderer/src/store/orderStore.ts:60-91). The POS counter path passes the computed discount in: OrderScreen.tsx:712-720 sends `discount_amount: currentDiscount>0 ? currentDiscount : undefined` from store.getDiscount(). But the two untrusted channels do not: the tablet self-order server (src/main/tablet/server.ts:300-308) calls ordersRepo.create({...forceMenuPrice:true, items}) with NO discount_amount, and the remote-order listener (src/main/sync/remote-order-listener.ts:114-121) likewise calls ordersRepo.create({...forceMenuPrice:true, items:validItems}) with NO discount_amount. In both cases discount resolves to Math.min(Math.max(0, undefined ?? 0), subtotal) = 0, so the stored total = subtotal (full price). Meanwhile the customer-facing display advertises the same active promotions: server.ts:45 maps promotionsRepo.getActivePromotions() into the payload, and display-ui.ts:801-828 renders them as a 'Special Offers' panel showing e.g. '-20%'. Concrete failure: with a '20% on everything' promo active, a 1000 DA cart rung at the POS counter charges 800 DA (discount_amount applied), but the identical cart placed on the self-order tablet or via an online/remote order is charged 1000 DA — channel-dependent pricing contradicting the advertised promo. The claim's file+line citations are accurate and the scenario is real; money-correctness bug.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by full code trace. Promo discount is computed ONLY in the renderer: computeDiscount in src/renderer/src/store/orderStore.ts:60-91, invoked at OrderScreen.tsx:712 and passed as discount_amount/discount_details into orders.create (OrderScreen.tsx:719-720) → orders.ipc.ts:13 → orders.repo.ts. In ordersRepo.create, the ONLY discount source is input.discount_amount (orders.repo.ts:125: discount = Math.min(Math.max(0, input.discount_amount ?? 0), subtotal)). The tablet self-order path (server.ts:300-308) and the remote-order path (remote-order-listener.ts:114-121) both call ordersRepo.create with forceMenuPrice:true and NO discount_amount, so discount evaluates to 0 and total = subtotal (full price). A repo-wide grep confirms no main-process path computes a promo discount. Meanwhile the customer TV advertises the same active promotions: server.ts:45 promotionsRepo.getActivePromotions() feeds display-ui.ts:801-821 'Special Offers'. Concrete scenario: owner activates a 20%-on-everything promotion (PromotionsPage → is_active=1); TV shows '-20%'; a 1000 DA order on the self-order tablet is charged 1000 DA (receipt printer.ipc.ts:90 shows no discount line since discount_amount=0), while the identical order at the counter is 800 DA; remote/online orders are likewise full price. Proposed fix direction (compute promo discount in the main process and apply it in ordersRepo.create for tablet/remote) is correct; minor note: gating on forceMenuPrice conflates price-trust with promo-application but functionally works because those are exactly the untrusted paths that omit discount_amount, so POS orders (which already supply discount_amount and leave forceMenuPrice off) won't be double-discounted.

findings.title: TV 'Text scale' setting is a no-op: percentage font-size on #panelStage cannot affect rem/vw/px-sized text
findings.evidence: function applyTextScale(scale) { var multiplier = scale === 'small' ? 0.8 : scale === 'large' ? 1.3 : 1.0; document.getElementById('panelStage').style.fontSize = (multiplier * 100) + '%'; } — but every visible text element in this page declares its own font-size in rem, vw, or px (e.g. .welcome-name: clamp(2.6rem, 6vw, 5.5rem); .menu-heading: 0.85rem; .order-badge-number: clamp(3rem, 6vw, 5rem)). rem resolves against the ROOT element and vw against the viewport, so a percentage font-size on an ancestor changes nothing; no element inherits panelStage's size.
findings.scenario: Owner opens Ambiance Screen, presses the user-facing 'Large' text-scale button (AmbianceScreen.tsx:652, persisted as display_*_text_scale) because the TV is far from customers — the LAN TV re-renders with exactly the same sizes. Small/large are both indistinguishable from medium.
findings.fix: Set the scale on the root instead — `document.documentElement.style.fontSize = (multiplier * 100) + '%'` — so all rem-based clamps scale, and/or multiply into a CSS variable used by the clamp() expressions (vw terms need the variable approach).

refuter.reason: Confirmed real. applyTextScale (src/main/tablet/display-ui.ts:565-568) sets a percentage font-size on #panelStage: document.getElementById('panelStage').style.fontSize = (multiplier*100)+'%'. Per CSS, a % font-size on an ancestor only affects descendants that inherit their size, but every visible text element in this page declares its own size in rem/vw/px (e.g. .welcome-name clamp(2.6rem,6vw,5.5rem) @103, .order-badge-number clamp(3rem,6vw,5rem) @309, .menu-heading 0.85rem @393, .orders-heading @273, all .menu-*/.social-*/.promo-*/.slide-caption). rem resolves against <html> and vw against the viewport, neither influenced by #panelStage; the two em uses (@147, @442) inherit from rem/vw-sized parents, not panelStage. applyTextScale never touches documentElement font-size, and no CSS var feeds the clamps, so nothing scales. The control is fully reachable and persisted: AmbianceScreen.tsx:652 (updateSetting textScale) -> settings key display[_profile_]text_scale -> server.ts:100/133 sends textScale -> display-ui.ts:1082/1100 applyTextScale. Result: pressing Small/Medium/Large on the Ambiance Screen leaves the LAN TV kiosk with visually identical text sizes. Correct CSS-mechanics diagnosis, valid caller path, concrete user-facing failure. Fix (target documentElement, or scale a CSS var used in the clamps) is directionally right; vw terms still need the variable approach but that does not weaken the bug.

tracer.reason: Confirmed by full code trace. applyTextScale (display-ui.ts:565-567) sets an inline percentage font-size on #panelStage, but #panelStage (lines 76-79) has no font-size and every visible text descendant declares its own font-size in rem/vw/px (e.g. .welcome-name clamp(2.6rem,6vw,5.5rem) L103, .menu-heading 0.85rem L393, .order-badge-number clamp(3rem,6vw,5rem) L309). rem resolves against :root, vw against the viewport, px is absolute — none inherit panelStage's computed size; the two em sub-elements (L147, L442) are relative to rem/vw parents so also don't scale. Trigger chain is deterministic: AmbianceScreen.tsx:652 updateSetting('textScale','large') persisted as display_<profile>_text_scale -> display-ui.ts:1082 state.textScale='large' -> L1100 applyTextScale('large') -> L567 panelStage.style.fontSize='130%' -> zero visual change. So the LAN TV renders small/medium/large identically; the user-facing control is a no-op. Severity is cosmetic/UX, not money. Fix-direction is essentially correct: moving the scale to document.documentElement (root) scales all rem terms, including the rem max of each clamp() which is commonly the active value on wide TVs, so it makes a visible difference; the reporter's caveat that pure-vw terms still need a CSS-variable multiplier is accurate. Fix is valid, not misdirected.

findings.title: readJsonBody concatenates Buffer chunks as strings — multi-byte UTF-8 (Arabic notes/names) split across TCP reads gets corrupted into U+FFFD
findings.evidence: let body = ''; req.on('data', (chunk) => { ... body += chunk ... }) — `req.setEncoding` is never called, so `chunk` is a Buffer and `body += chunk` calls chunk.toString('utf8') on each chunk independently. A multi-byte UTF-8 sequence (every Arabic character is 2 bytes) that straddles a chunk boundary decodes to replacement characters on both sides of the seam.
findings.scenario: A tablet order with a cart of many items and Arabic notes/customer name produces a JSON body of a few KB, which arrives over WiFi in multiple TCP segments (~1.4 KB each) and thus multiple 'data' events. When a boundary lands mid-character, the parsed order stores a note like 'بدون بص��ل' — the kitchen ticket and order history show garbled text; if the split lands inside an escaped sequence the whole request 400s and the customer's order is rejected.
findings.fix: Accumulate Buffers and decode once: `const chunks: Buffer[] = []; let size = 0; req.on('data', c => { chunks.push(c); size += c.length; if (size > MAX_BYTES) {...} }); ... JSON.parse(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf8'))` — this also makes the 256 KB cap count real bytes.

refuter.reason: Confirmed. src/main/tablet/server.ts:205-215 accumulates request body as a string (`body += chunk`) with no req.setEncoding anywhere in src/ (grep verified), so each 'data' chunk is a Buffer decoded independently via chunk.toString('utf8'); a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence straddling a chunk boundary decodes to U+FFFD on both sides. The path genuinely carries multi-byte text: tablet-ui.ts:669 sends a free-text `notes` field via JSON.stringify (which does not \u-escape Arabic/French), the server stores it (server.ts:305) and prints it on kitchen tickets (line 316), and tablets connect over real WiFi LAN (0.0.0.0 + QR LAN URL), where bodies >~1.4KB arrive in multiple TCP segments/data events. Result: intermittent silent mojibake in kitchen-ticket/order-history notes (e.g. garbled Arabic modifiers). One correction to the claim: the '400/order rejected' sub-scenario cannot occur — browsers don't escape Arabic and U+FFFD is valid in JSON strings while structural chars are single-byte ASCII, so JSON.parse always succeeds; the failure is silent corruption only. The secondary point that the 256KB cap counts UTF-16 code units, not bytes (line 210), is also accurate. Proposed Buffer.concat fix is the standard correct remedy.

tracer.reason: Confirmed by code trace. src/main/tablet/server.ts:205-215: readJsonBody does `let body = ''; req.on('data', (chunk) => { ... body += chunk ... })` and `req.setEncoding` appears nowhere in src/ (grep: 0 matches), so each chunk is a Buffer decoded independently via implicit toString('utf8'); a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence straddling a chunk boundary decodes to U+FFFD on both sides. Trigger path is real: the tablet UI ships an Arabic locale (tablet-ui.ts:355) with a free-text notes input (line 298/669) POSTed as raw UTF-8 via fetch+JSON.stringify (line 679) to POST /api/order (server.ts:278→283); a multi-item cart with a long Arabic note (server allows 500 chars ≈ 1000 bytes, server.ts:305) exceeds one WiFi TCP segment (~1460B MSS), producing multiple 'data' events with arbitrary byte boundaries. Since U+FFFD is a valid JSON string char, JSON.parse (219) succeeds and the garbled note is persisted by ordersRepo.create (300-308), auto-printed on the kitchen ticket (316), and shown in history — silent order-data corruption. Two report inaccuracies (non-fatal): the '400s the whole request' sub-scenario is wrong (JSON.stringify emits raw Arabic, and escape sequences are pure ASCII so splitting them is harmless; a mid-character split cannot break JSON syntax), and the bug is probabilistic — small single-segment bodies are unaffected. Proposed fix (accumulate Buffer[] + Buffer.concat + single decode) is correct and also fixes the secondary flaw that the 256KB cap at line 210 counts UTF-16 code units, not bytes; req.setEncoding('utf8') alone would also fix the corruption but not the byte-accurate cap.

findings.title: Tablet self-orders never appear on the TV 'Now Preparing' queue — no queue push after /api/order creates the order
findings.evidence: After `ordersRepo.create(...)` the handler only does `mainWin?.webContents.send('tablet:new-order', order)` plus print/backup/telegram — it never calls `pushDisplayUpdate(getQueuePayload())` even though both functions live in this same file. The LAN display page (display-ui.ts) updates its queue ONLY from SSE 'queue' events; it never polls /api/display-queue. The only 'queue' pushes come from the renderer's OrderScreen (pushQueueToDisplay), and OrderScreen's onNewOrder listener (OrderScreen.tsx:153-155) only calls `loadOngoingCount()`. remote-order-listener.ts likewise creates orders with no queue push.
findings.scenario: Customer orders from the self-order tablet, gets 'Order #12 received!', and looks at the TV — #12 never shows in 'Now Preparing'. The TV queue only refreshes when the cashier next places or completes an order through the POS screen, so during a quiet period the tablet/remote order is invisible on the display the whole time it is being prepared.
findings.fix: In the /api/order success path (and in remote-order-listener after create), call `pushDisplayUpdate(getQueuePayload())`.

refuter.reason: Verified every link of the claimed path; could not refute it. (1) src/main/tablet/server.ts:300-321 — the /api/order success path calls ordersRepo.create, then only mainWin?.webContents.send('tablet:new-order', order), performAutoBackup, sendOrderNotification, and optional printOrder; it never calls pushDisplayUpdate(getQueuePayload()), even though getQueuePayload (line 136) and pushDisplayUpdate (line 151) live in the same file. (2) The LAN TV page (src/main/tablet/display-ui.ts) updates its 'Now Preparing' queue ONLY from SSE: initial 'info'+'queue' sent at connect (server.ts:350-354) and 'queue' events (display-ui.ts:1105-1110). It has no polling of /api/display-queue (that endpoint has zero fetch callers anywhere), and its only reconnect is es.onerror → setTimeout(connect, 3000) (display-ui.ts:1122-1125); the server sends no SSE heartbeat, so a healthy connection receives nothing until pushDisplayUpdate fires. (3) A repo-wide grep shows pushDisplayUpdate is only reachable via IPC 'tablet:pushDisplayUpdate' (tablet.ipc.ts:83-85), whose only callers are cashier-action handlers in OrderScreen.tsx: create order (752), save edit (698), markDone (798), confirmCancel (811), restoreOrder (822). (4) The tablet:new-order listeners do NOT push: App.tsx:100-103 shows a 5s toast; OrderScreen.tsx:153-155 only calls loadOngoingCount(), which just sets a badge count. (5) remote-order-listener.ts:112-137 creates remote orders with the same side-effects (sync/backup/telegram/print + 'remote:new-order' IPC) and also never pushes a queue update; it doesn't import from server.ts. (6) No EventEmitter/order-created hook exists in src/main that could push indirectly. So the concrete scenario holds: a tablet (or Supabase remote) order enters the DB as pending/preparing, the customer sees 'Order #N received', but the TV 'Now Preparing' list is stale until the cashier next places/completes/cancels an order in the POS — during a quiet period the order is invisible on the display for its entire preparation. Proposed fix (call pushDisplayUpdate(getQueuePayload()) after create in both paths) is correct and consistent with existing code.

tracer.reason: Confirmed by full code trace. server.ts /api/order success path (lines 309-317) does mainWin?.webContents.send('tablet:new-order', order) + backup/notification/print but never calls pushDisplayUpdate(getQueuePayload()), both defined in the same file (lines 136/151). The TV display (display-ui.ts) updates state.queue ONLY from SSE events ('info' at 1076, 'queue' at 1105-1110) over one EventSource('/api/display-events') (1117); it never polls /api/display-queue, and reconnect only happens on es.onerror. The only 'queue' producer in the repo is OrderScreen.tsx pushQueueToDisplay (564-577), called solely from cashier POS actions (698/752/798/811/822); OrderScreen's tablet:new-order listener (153-155) only calls loadOngoingCount(), and App.tsx (100-103) only shows a toast. remote-order-listener.ts (114-134) likewise creates the order with no pushDisplayUpdate. Since ordersRepo.create inserts with status 'preparing' (orders.repo.ts:144), a tablet/remote order belongs in the "Now Preparing" list but the TV never learns of it: customer gets 'Order #12 received!' while #12 stays invisible on the TV until the cashier's next OrderScreen action or an SSE drop/reconnect. Proposed fix is correct in direction: add pushDisplayUpdate(getQueuePayload()) after create in /api/order (works as-is, same module) and in remote-order-listener (minor detail: getQueuePayload is currently module-private, so export it or add an exported pushQueueUpdate() helper).

findings.title: Tablet ordering page injects menu/category/cart names into innerHTML with no escaping — broken rendering and stored XSS on customer tablets
findings.evidence:
renderItems: row.innerHTML = `...
${getName(item)}
...` (line 539); renderCats: card.innerHTML = `...
${getName(c)}
` (line 518, plus ${c.icon} line 517); renderCartContents: `${c.name}` (line 627). None are escaped — unlike display-ui.ts, which has and uses esc() for the same data. Names come from /api/menu (owner-edited menu, also writable via the cloud admin portal menu sync).
findings.scenario: Owner names an item 'Tacos ' — everything from '<' is parsed as a tag, so the tablet shows just 'Tacos' in the list and cart (and a stray unclosed element can break the row layout). Worse, a name containing '' executes on every customer tablet that loads the menu: stored XSS that can read the PIN session token from localStorage and silently POST arbitrary orders.
findings.fix: Add the same esc() helper used in display-ui.ts and wrap every interpolation of getName()/c.name/c.icon/item.emoji in the three innerHTML templates (or build these nodes with document.createElement + textContent).

refuter.reason: Verified in the working tree: tablet-ui.ts injects getName(item)/getName(c)/c.icon/c.name into innerHTML unescaped at lines 517-518 (renderCats), 537/539 (renderItems), and 627 (renderCartContents). The data path has no sanitization anywhere: menu.repo.ts create/update (lines 84-137) store owner-entered names raw, /api/menu (server.ts lines 254-258) serves repo rows verbatim with no auth, getName() returns the raw string, and no esc() helper exists in tablet-ui.ts. The served page has no CSP (headers at server.ts 244-248 are Content-Type/cache only, no meta http-equiv), so an injected executes; the PIN session token sits in localStorage (ffm_session_*, lines 429-456) and is used as a Bearer token for POST /api/order (line 678), making the token-theft/rogue-order scenario concrete. Even without an attacker, an innocent name like 'Tacos ' renders truncated as 'Tacos' on customer tablets - a real restaurant-visible bug. The sibling display-ui.ts defines and consistently uses esc() (lines 537-539, 755-974) on the exact same menu data, proving tablet-ui.ts is an inconsistency, not a design choice. Every refutation angle (escaping elsewhere, impossible input, CSP mitigation, token inaccessibility) fails on inspection.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by full trace. server.ts:254-257 (GET /api/menu) returns categoriesRepo.getAll()/menuRepo.getAll() verbatim (name, name_ar, name_fr, icon, emoji), owner-edited and admin-syncable. tablet-ui.ts:475 stores it, then injects into innerHTML with zero escaping at: renderCats line 517 ${c.icon} + line 518 ${getName(c)}; renderItems line 537 ${emojiChar} + line 539 ${getName(item)}; renderCartContents line 627 ${c.name} (c.name = getName(item), set at addToCart line 569). getName (502-506) returns raw DB strings. Concrete failures: (1) guaranteed broken rendering for any name containing '<' or '&' — a realistic menu name like 'Menu < 500 DA' or 'Tacos ' renders as just 'Menu'/'Tacos' in list and cart, dropping the rest (browser treats it as an unclosed tag); (2) stored XSS — a name '' executes on every tablet loading the menu and can read the session token from localStorage['ffm_session_v'+PIN_VERSION] (set line 455) and POST to /api/order (line 679). The bug is proven by contrast with sibling display-ui.ts, which defines esc() (line 537) and uses it for the exact same fields (esc(items[j].name) line 974, esc(catName) line 969); tablet-ui.ts simply omits it. Proposed fix is correct: add the same esc() and wrap getName()/c.name/c.icon/emoji, or use textContent. Caveat: server forces menu prices (forceMenuPrice, server.ts:286), so XSS cannot zero-out prices, but broken rendering and token-theft/bogus-order injection are real. Not on the do-not-report exclusion list (renderer-trial-lock/machineId/etc.); this is server-provided menu data escaping.

findings.title: startBot re-entry guard checks isRunning (still false while connecting) — second Start spawns a duplicate poller and the first failure nulls the live bot
findings.evidence: `if (isRunning && bot) return { success: true }` — isRunning only flips in onStart after grammy's getMe resolves. A second startBot while the first is pending creates a new Bot and overwrites the module `bot`, leaving the first poller orphaned (two getUpdates pollers → Telegram 409 conflicts). Worse, the first call's `.catch` (lines 61-66) does `isRunning = false; bot = null`, clobbering the second, healthy bot.
findings.scenario: telegram_auto_start fires at app launch on a slow connection; owner opens Telegram settings a few seconds later, sees 'Stopped' (isRunning still false) and clicks Start Bot. Two pollers now fight over getUpdates; if either start() later rejects, `bot` is set to null so sendOrderNotification returns at `if (!bot || !isRunning)` — order notifications stop until app restart, and the orphaned poller can't be stopped.
findings.fix: Guard on the bot instance itself (`if (bot) return { success: true }`), keep a per-instance reference in the .catch closure (`const thisBot = bot; ... if (bot === thisBot) { bot = null; isRunning = false }`), and stop any existing instance before creating a new one.

refuter.reason: Confirmed in working tree: bot.ts line 31 guard `if (isRunning && bot)` fails during grammy's async startup because the uncommitted diff moved `isRunning = true` into the onStart callback (lines 56-59), which grammy 1.40 only invokes after getMe succeeds (with up-to-1-hour withRetries backoff on network errors). During that window a second startBot() — reachable via the Settings Start button (telegram.ipc.ts:32, TelegramSettings.tsx shows 'stopped' since isBotRunning() is false) after the boot auto-start (index.ts:445), or a simple double-click — replaces `bot` with a new Bot(token) and starts a second poller; the first is orphaned (stopBot only stops the current reference). Verified in installed grammy source that getUpdates 409 is rethrown, rejecting one start() promise whose .catch (lines 61-66) unconditionally nulls the shared `bot`/`isRunning` even if the orphan survives — so sendOrderNotification (line 108) silently goes dark and the orphan poller persists until app restart. Pre-diff code set isRunning synchronously, so this regression was introduced by the diff.

tracer.reason: Confirmed by code trace of the working tree. src/main/telegram/bot.ts line 31 guards with `if (isRunning && bot)`, but the uncommitted diff removed the synchronous `isRunning = true` (verified via git diff) and moved it into grammy's async `onStart` callback (lines 56-60), which only fires after a network round-trip (getMe). During that window `isRunning` is false while `bot` is non-null, so a second startBot() — realistically triggered because index.ts:445 auto-starts the bot at boot while telegram:status (telegram.ipc.ts:42) still reports isRunning=false, making the Settings UI show 'stopped' and inviting the owner to click Start (or simply double-clicking Start) — falls through the guard, reassigns the module-level `bot` at line 37, and starts a second getUpdates long-poller on the same token. The orphaned first poller keeps running (stopBot() at lines 76-82 only stops the current reference), producing Telegram 409 Conflict fights until app restart. Aggravator confirmed: the orphan's `.catch` (lines 61-66) mutates shared state, so a later rejection of the orphan's start promise sets `bot = null`, after which sendOrderNotification (line 108 `if (!bot || !isRunning) return`) silently drops all new-order notifications. Proposed fix direction is sound: `bot` is set synchronously (line 37) and nulled on all failure/stop paths (lines 65, 71, 79), so `if (bot) return { success: true }` (or a synchronous isStarting flag) closes the window without regressing the bad-token recovery the diff was fixing.

findings.title: Shape mismatch: renderer treats reset:validateTelegram's { valid: boolean } object as a boolean, so wrong/expired Telegram codes advance to the new-password screen
findings.evidence: Handler returns an object: "ipcMain.handle('reset:validateTelegram', (_, code) => { return { valid: validateTelegramResetCode(code) } })" (src/main/ipc/activation.ipc.ts:64-66). Renderer (PasswordGate.tsx:128-129): "const valid = await window.api.reset.validateTelegram(telegramCode.trim()); if (valid) {" — an object is always truthy, so { valid: false } passes the check. Contrast with the cloud path which correctly does "result?.valid === true" (PasswordGate.tsx:163).
findings.scenario: Owner mistypes the 6-digit Telegram code: instead of 'Invalid or expired code' at the validation step, the UI advances to the new-password form, the owner picks and confirms a new password, and only then gets a confusing failure. Worse, if the always-fails re-validation bug in reset:resetPassword is fixed by 'trusting the renderer' as its comment intends, this truthiness bug alone would let ANYONE reset the admin password with an arbitrary wrong code — a full admin bypass. The two must be fixed together.
findings.fix: Check the field, not the object: "const res = await window.api.reset.validateTelegram(...); if (res?.valid === true) {" — or change the handler to return a bare boolean to match the renderer's expectation.

findings.fix: Move the whole import into one main-process IPC handler that runs clear + all inserts inside a single better-sqlite3 transaction (parse rows in renderer, send the arrays), and validate/coerce Price with a clear per-row error before touching the DB.

findings.title: Orders History table renders the raw UTC created_at string — every order time shown one hour off (and as an unformatted ISO timestamp)
