findings.evidence: const url = `https://wa.me/${selectedCustomer.phone.replace(/[^0-9]/g, '')}`. Customer phones are entered at the POS in Algerian local format (05/06/07 + 8 digits). wa.me requires the full international number without a leading 0, so the generated link is e.g. https://wa.me/0551234567.
findings.scenario: Owner opens Loyalty, selects a customer with phone "0551 23 45 67", clicks the green WhatsApp button. The system browser opens wa.me/0551234567 and WhatsApp shows "The phone number shared via url is invalid." for essentially every customer in the database — the feature never works.
findings.fix: Normalize before building the URL: strip non-digits, then replace a leading '0' with the country code, e.g. `const digits = phone.replace(/\D/g, ''); const intl = digits.startsWith('0') ? '213' + digits.slice(1) : digits`.

refuter.reason: Confirmed real. In LoyaltyDashboard.tsx:117 the WhatsApp link is `https://wa.me/${selectedCustomer.phone.replace(/[^0-9]/g, '')}`, which only strips non-digits and leaves the leading 0 with no country code. Tracing storage: phone is captured in OrderScreen.tsx as a raw `type="tel"` field (store.customerPhone, generic "Customer phone" placeholder, no format enforcement), passed verbatim to orders.repo.ts (input.customer_phone) and into customersRepo.upsertFromOrder -> INSERT customers.phone as-is (customers.repo.ts:81-87). A grep across src for `+213`/`startsWith('0')`/`slice(1)` finds NO phone normalization anywhere (only the WhatsApp SVG icon and social-platform config). So Algerian local numbers (0X + 8 digits) are stored and rendered as e.g. wa.me/0551234567, which WhatsApp rejects as invalid because it needs full international format (213551234567) without the leading 0. The feature is broken for essentially every customer, matching the reviewer's scenario. Proposed fix (replace leading 0 with 213) is correct.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by full code trace. Guilty line is verbatim at LoyaltyDashboard.tsx:117: `const url = `https://wa.me/${selectedCustomer.phone.replace(/[^0-9]/g, '')}``. Trace of how phone reaches it: (1) OrderScreen.tsx:1367-1375 — the delivery phone is a plain free-text type="tel" input stored raw via store.setCustomerPhone(val); placeholder is only "Customer phone"/"هاتف العميل" with no international hint, so Algerian staff type local format 0XXXXXXXXX. (2) orders.repo.ts:132-138 — input.customer_phone is passed to customersRepo.upsertFromOrder with NO normalization. (3) customers.repo.ts:83-86 — phone is INSERTed verbatim into customers.phone. (4) LoyaltyDashboard loads via window.api.customers.getAll, so selectedCustomer.phone is that raw local string. Concrete scenario: a delivery order with phone "0551 23 45 67" is saved -> customers.phone = "0551 23 45 67" -> owner opens Loyalty, selects that customer, clicks the green WhatsApp button (onClick at line 116-119) -> window.open("https://wa.me/0551234567"). wa.me requires E.164 (country code, no leading 0), so it shows "The phone number shared via url is invalid." for essentially every normally-entered Algerian customer. Nowhere in the path is 213 prepended or the leading 0 stripped, so the feature is broken for the standard case. Fix direction is correct: strip non-digits then map a leading '0' to '213'+rest (Algeria = +213), which turns 0551234567 into 213551234567. Minor unhandled edge: a number typed with the 00 international prefix (e.g. "00213...") would be mangled by that same startsWith('0') branch, but that is a rare edge and does not affect the correctness of the fix for the dominant local-format case.

findings.title: Packs have a price and advertised 'savings' but no order path can ever charge the pack price
findings.evidence: PromotionsPage computes `Math.max(0, individualTotal - pack.pack_price)` as customer savings (line 199) and packs are pushed to the customer display as 'Special Offers' with `pack_price` (cloud-sync.ts:52, server.ts:48-54, display-ui.ts:808-821). But nothing consumes packs on the ordering side: OrderScreen/orderStore have zero pack handling (no `pack` reference in the POS cart code), computeDiscount only iterates promotions, and ordersRepo.create prices strictly per menu item. `packs.getActive` is exposed in preload but only PromotionsPage/display code call pack APIs.
findings.scenario: Owner creates an active pack 'Burger + Fries + Drink = 800 DA' (items individually 950 DA); the TV advertises it with the savings badge. A customer orders the pack; the cashier taps the three items and the POS totals 950 DA. The only workaround is manually price-overriding lines. Every 'pack' sale either overcharges the customer by the advertised savings or depends on unaudited manual overrides.
findings.fix: Add packs to the POS order flow: a pack button that inserts its component items and applies `individualTotal - pack_price` as a discount line (discount_details = pack name), reusing the existing discount_amount plumbing.

refuter.reason: Confirmed real. Packs are a defined entity (promotions.repo.ts createPack/getActivePacks) with a pack_price and component items, and they are actively advertised to customers with a concrete price + "Save X" badge: PromotionsPage.tsx:199 computes savings, and packs are pushed to the customer/TV display as Special Offers with pack_price (server.ts:48-54 getInfoPayload; display-ui.ts:808-834; cloud-sync.ts). But NO ordering path consumes packs. orderStore.ts computeDiscount (lines 60-91) iterates only activePromos; loadActivePromos calls promotions.getActive (line 209), never packs.getActive; there is no "pack" reference in orderStore.ts or OrderScreen.tsx at all. OrderScreen.handlePlaceOrder (641-760) builds orders purely from individual store.items with promo-only discount_amount. The tablet self-order endpoint server.ts:278-322 (POST /api/order) likewise builds only {menu_item_id, quantity} items with forceMenuPrice:true and no pack. ordersRepo.create (orders.repo.ts:90-125) prices each line from menuItem.price and applies only input.discount_amount — no pack lookup. The other renderer "pack" hits are false positives (DayRecapModal imports the Package icon; AmbianceScreen has a panel label). Failure scenario: owner creates active pack "Burger+Fries+Drink=800 DA" (items sum 950 DA), TV shows "Save 150 DA"; customer orders it; cashier taps 3 items; POS totals 950 DA with no pack button or pack discount. Every pack sale overcharges by the advertised savings or requires an unaudited manual price override. This is a concrete money-correctness gap and is not on the accepted/known-issues list.

tracer.reason: Independent code trace confirms the gap. Packs are fully built on the create/advertise side: promotions.repo.ts:224 getActivePacks() reads pack_price+items; server.ts:48-54 and cloud-sync.ts:50-52 feed them to the customer TV; display-ui.ts:808-813 renders each pack in the "Special Offers" panel at pack_price; PromotionsPage.tsx:199 computes Math.max(0, individualTotal - pack.pack_price) and shows a "Save {amount}" badge. But NO order path consumes packs: orderStore.ts has no pack reference (loadActivePromos loads only promotions.getActive; computeDiscount lines 60-91 iterates only activePromos), OrderScreen.tsx has zero pack references and sends discount_amount = store.getDiscount() (promo-only) at line 719, and orders.repo.ts:110-118 create() prices strictly unitPrice*quantity with the only discount input being discount_amount (clamped 124-126), which no pack code populates. packs.getAll is called only in PromotionsPage:51; packs.getActive (preload:259) is consumed only by display/admin code. Concrete money failure: owner makes active pack Combo=800 DA from items totaling 950, TV advertises it, cashier taps the 3 items -> POS totals 950 DA, overcharging 150 vs the advertised bundle unless the cashier does an unaudited per-line price override (updateItemPrice). Two caveats: (1) the report slightly overstates the customer-facing savings — display-ui.ts:811 sets badge:'' for packs, so the explicit "save X" number appears only in the owner admin page, though the TV still advertises the bundle at pack_price the POS can't honor, so the gap holds; this is an incomplete/half-shipped feature rather than a code regression, but the daily money impact is real. findings.title: Receipt Editor social media saves to the social_media TABLE, but printing reads the settings key — preview shows handles that never print

Nothing syncs the two stores.
findings.scenario: Owner opens Receipt Editor → 'Manage Social Media Accounts' → adds '@myrestaurant' Instagram → live preview shows it → saves template. Printed receipts show nothing (or stale handles previously entered in Settings > General). Conversely, handles edited in Settings > General print correctly but never appear in the editor preview.
findings.fix: Use one source of truth: have the Receipt Editor read/write the `social_media` settings key (like SettingsPage and the tablet server), or make buildFromTemplate read from receiptTemplatesRepo.getAllSocialMedia().

WRITE path (editor): ReceiptEditor.tsx:219 handleSaveSocial -> window.api.receipt.saveSocialMedia -> IPC 'receipt:saveSocialMedia' (receipt-editor.ipc.ts:102-104) -> receiptTemplatesRepo.saveSocialMedia (receipt-templates.repo.ts:69-79) which does DELETE/INSERT on the dedicated `social_media` TABLE (created in migration 012_receipt_editor.ts:17).

findings.title: Start Bot UI shows 'Running' immediately even when the bot fails to connect (bad token / offline)
findings.evidence: handleStart: `const result = await window.api.telegram.start(); if (result.success) { setIsRunning(true) }`. But bot.ts startBot returns `{ success: true }` (line 68) before grammy's async `bot.start()` has validated the token — a revoked token or no network rejects AFTER the reply (acknowledged in the bot.ts:53 comment) and only sets main-process isRunning=false. The UI never re-polls telegram:status, so the green 'Running' badge and no error are shown.
findings.scenario: Owner pastes a token with a trailing space (or the revoked token). Clicks Start Bot → UI shows green 'Running', no error. They close settings believing notifications work; every order notification silently does nothing. Only reopening the settings page later reveals 'Stopped'.
findings.fix: After start(), poll `window.api.telegram.status` once after ~2-3s and update isRunning/startError from it — or make the startBot IPC await the connection (return the bot.start onStart/first-error outcome).

refuter.reason: Confirmed real. Path: TelegramSettings.tsx:68-70 sets local isRunning=true whenever result.success is truthy; preload:157 -> telegram.ipc.ts:32-34 -> startBot() in bot.ts. startBot (bot.ts:56-68) fires bot.start() as fire-and-forget (onStart flips module isRunning true; a .catch on bad/revoked token or offline sets isRunning=false and bot=null AFTER return) and unconditionally returns { success:true } at line 68 before grammy's getMe validates the token. The comment at bot.ts:52-55 explicitly acknowledges this async rejection. The renderer therefore paints the green 'Running' badge (line 92) and label 'Running' (lines 95-98) with no error. There is NO re-poll: the component's only status read is loadConfig() in useEffect(...,[]) (lines 44-55) which runs once on mount; window.api.telegram.status (preload:159, ipc:41-43) is never called here, so the stale green badge survives until the page is remounted. Downstream, sendOrderNotification (bot.ts:107-108) returns early when !bot || !isRunning, so after the async rejection every order notification silently no-ops while the UI shows Running. Realistic inputs (revoked token, trailing-space token, or no network) all reach this: new Bot(token) does not validate connectivity synchronously. Refutations fail: the fix hardened only the main-process isRunning, not the renderer's trust of the synchronous {success:true}. Scenario matches exactly.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED. Execution path: handleStart (TelegramSettings.tsx:68) awaits window.api.telegram.start → IPC telegram:start (telegram.ipc.ts:32-34) → startBot() (bot.ts:23). With token+chatId configured, startBot constructs the Bot synchronously and fires the async bot.start({onStart}) (bot.ts:56), whose getMe/init rejection is handled only LATER by the .catch (bot.ts:61-66) that sets main-process isRunning=false and bot=null. startBot returns {success:true} synchronously at bot.ts:68. Back in the renderer, result.success===true so setIsRunning(true) runs (line 70), rendering the green 'Running' badge (lines 92-98) with no error. The renderer never re-reads status: TelegramSettings only calls loadConfig() once on mount (useEffect line 44-46); I grep-verified no telegram:status poll or event listener exists anywhere in src/renderer, even though the telegram:status IPC handler (telegram.ipc.ts:41) exists. So the badge stays green while the main process has bot=null, and sendOrderNotification (bot.ts:108) short-circuits on `if (!bot || !isRunning) return`, silently dropping every order notification. Airtight scenario needing no assumption about grammy token-format validation: momentary network outage — owner clicks Start Bot with a valid, previously-working token; new Bot(token) succeeds (no network in constructor), bot.start()'s getMe rejects asynchronously; UI shows 'Running' with no error, notifications never fire. Revoked-token / trailing-space variants behave identically (well-formed token rejects async, not at construction). The bug-fix comment at bot.ts:52-55 fixed the MAIN-process side (isRunning/auto-start) but left the renderer optimistically trusting the always-true success flag. Fix direction is correct; the stronger option (resolve the IPC on grammy's onStart vs first .catch) is right, with the caveat the reporter half-notes: you cannot naively await bot.start() because that promise does not resolve until the bot STOPS (long-polling loop), so it must be wrapped to await whichever of onStart or .catch fires first. The 'poll status once after 2-3s' alternative works but is racy on slow networks.

findings.title: Attendance date defaults to the UTC day, so attendance marked between 00:00 and 01:00 local is written to (and can overwrite) the previous day
findings.evidence: `const [attendanceDate, setAttendanceDate] = useState(new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0])` uses the UTC calendar date, while orders use restaurant-local localDate() (orders.repo.ts:12) and the renderer already has localToday() in src/renderer/src/utils/localDate.ts written specifically to fix this class of bug — this call site was missed. workersRepo.setAttendance uses `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO worker_attendance` keyed on UNIQUE(worker_id, date) (workers.repo.ts:169), so a write to the wrong date silently replaces that day's real record.
findings.scenario: Algeria is UTC+1 and the restaurant is open past midnight. At 00:30 local the manager opens Workers to mark the night shift: the page defaults to YESTERDAY's date. Marking a worker 'full' replaces yesterday's real attendance row (e.g., a worker who was absent yesterday now shows a paid full day yesterday) and today's attendance row is never created. getProfitSummary/getCostsByDay then attribute the pay to the wrong day, and the pay report is missing a day for the worker.
findings.fix: Initialize attendanceDate with localToday() from src/renderer/src/utils/localDate.ts instead of new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0].

refuter.reason: Verified in the working tree: WorkerManagement.tsx:58 initializes attendanceDate from new Date().toISOString() (UTC day), while orders use restaurant-local localDate() (orders.repo.ts:12) and the renderer's localToday() (utils/localDate.ts) — written specifically for this bug and already applied in OrdersHistory.tsx:15-16 — was not applied here. The date flows unmodified through IPC to workersRepo.setAttendance, which is INSERT OR REPLACE on UNIQUE(worker_id, date) (workers.repo.ts:169, 001_initial.ts:179), so marking attendance between 00:00-00:59 local (Algeria UTC+1) silently replaces YESTERDAY's real attendance row and never creates today's. Worse, loadAttendance() (lines 89-106) auto-writes full-day pay rows for ALL workers onto the wrong day just from opening the Attendance tab if that day has no records. analytics.repo.ts sums worker_attendance.pay_amount by date, so pay lands in the wrong day's profit window. No downstream normalization exists; refutation attempts failed.

tracer.reason: Verified by full code trace. WorkerManagement.tsx:58 initializes attendanceDate with `new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]` (UTC), so between 00:00 and 00:59 Algeria local time (UTC+1) the Attendance tab defaults to YESTERDAY. Both write paths use that state: handleSetAttendance (line 174) and the auto-fill in loadAttendance (line 99, which writes full-day pay for ALL workers when the loaded date has zero rows — triggered just by opening the tab). Writes go through workersRepo.setAttendance (workers.repo.ts:169) `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO worker_attendance` keyed on UNIQUE(worker_id, date) (migrations/001_initial.ts:179), silently replacing yesterday's real attendance row while today's row is never created. analytics.repo.ts (lines 26-30, 72-78) sums pay_amount by that date string, so worker pay lands in the wrong day's profit/cost report. The repo's own localToday() (src/renderer/src/utils/localDate.ts:10) documents exactly this UTC-midnight bug and was applied to OrdersHistory.tsx:15-16 but this call site was missed. Proposed fix (init with localToday()) is correct and consistent with the existing fix pattern; note lines 90 and 112 parse the date string safely with 'T00:00:00' so no further change is needed there.

findings.title: reprobeLanIfOnCloud commits last_url before verifying the load and ignores failure — TV can strand on an error page until reboot
findings.evidence: `prefs.edit().putString("last_url", lanUrl).putBoolean("via_cloud", false).apply(); switched = true; ui.post { loadDisplay(lanUrl) { } }` (lines 153-155). The result callback is empty, so if the LAN load fails nothing happens: no showPairing, no scheduleRetry, and since via_cloud was already flipped to false the 10-minute reprobe chain also stops (`if (!switched)` is not taken and the next entry would early-return anyway). This directly contradicts the invariant added in the same diff in connectWithCode (line 300: "only write last_url AFTER the load is verified ... so a dead/HTTP-error URL never becomes the remembered target").
findings.scenario: TV is on the cloud fallback (via_cloud=true). The POS PC comes online, the TCP probe at reprobe time succeeds, but the load then fails (POS app closed between probe and load, tablet server restarting, or main-frame HTTP >=400 which the new onReceivedHttpError now treats as failure). The TV replaces its working cloud display with a WebView error page and sits there for the rest of the day — no retry runnable is pending — until someone power-cycles it (after reboot the dead saved LAN url fails and connectWithCode recovers).
findings.fix: In the reprobe switch, pass a real callback: on ok, persist last_url/via_cloud=false; on failure, revert to the cloud URL (reload prefs last_url) and keep via_cloud=true so the reprobe chain continues — i.e. only commit prefs inside the ok branch, matching connectWithCode.

In reprobeLanIfOnCloud (MainActivity.kt:153-155), last_url is committed and via_cloud flipped to false BEFORE the load is verified, and the loadDisplay callback is empty (`{ }`). If the LAN load then fails (TCP probe passed but connection refused between probe and load, or main-frame HTTP >=400, which onReceivedHttpError at line 243 now treats as failure), nothing handles it: no showPairing, no scheduleRetry, `switched = true` suppresses the 10-min reschedule (line 161), and via_cloud=false makes any future reprobeLanIfOnCloud early-return (line 140). I verified no other recovery exists: retryRunnable is not pending in the on-cloud steady state, onRenderProcessGone only covers renderer crashes, and BootReceiver only fires at boot. Result: the TV replaces a working cloud display with an error page and strands with the dead LAN URL persisted as last_url until app restart/reboot (where connectWithCode via the saved code recovers). This directly contradicts the invariant the same diff added in connectWithCode (lines 300-307: commit last_url only inside the ok branch), confirming the reprobe path was simply missed.

tracer.reason: Verified by full code trace of tv-app/app/src/main/java/com/fastfood/tv/MainActivity.kt (working tree). In reprobeLanIfOnCloud, line 153 commits prefs (last_url=lanUrl, via_cloud=false) BEFORE the load, line 154 sets switched=true (killing the line-161 10-min reprobe reschedule), and line 155 passes an empty result callback to loadDisplay: `ui.post { loadDisplay(lanUrl) { } }`. The gate is a bare 900ms TCP connect (reachable(), lines 344-353), so a POS app/PC shutdown between probe and page load, or a main-frame HTTP >=400 (now treated as failure by onReceivedHttpError, lines 237-244), makes loadDisplay report false into the empty callback — nothing reloads the cloud URL, no showPairing, no scheduleRetry.
