findings.title: onRenderProcessGone → recreateWebView → reload has no backoff or crash counter — persistent renderer OOM becomes an infinite immediate crash/reload loop
findings.evidence: `override fun onRenderProcessGone(...): Boolean { ui.post { recreateWebView() }; return true }` (lines 246-249 and 187-190). recreateWebView() (line 200) immediately rebuilds the WebView and calls loadDisplay(url) with the same saved URL. The class comment itself names the OOM cause: "OOM on low-RAM TV sticks decoding the base64 logo + up to 10 slideshow images" — i.e. the crash is caused by the page content, so reloading the identical page reproduces it.
findings.scenario: A restaurant configures a 10-image slideshow with large photos on a 512MB-1GB TV stick. The renderer OOMs every time the page finishes decoding the images. The app enters a tight crash → recreate → reload → crash loop with zero delay between cycles: the TV flickers black forever, never shows the menu, hammers the POS server with page loads, and heats the stick — with no path back to the pairing screen or any status message.
findings.fix: Track consecutive renderer crashes with a timestamp; add an escalating delay (e.g. 5s → 30s → 60s) before the reload in recreateWebView, and after N rapid crashes show a status message (and/or load a lightweight ?lite variant) instead of immediately reloading the same URL.

refuter.reason: Confirmed in the working tree. onRenderProcessGone (MainActivity.kt lines 187-190 and 246-249) recovers with a bare `ui.post { recreateWebView() }` (no delay). recreateWebView() (lines 200-215) rebuilds the WebView and immediately reloads the same prefs["last_url"] via loadDisplay(url) at line 209, with no crash counter, no postDelayed backoff, and no cloud/LAN fallback. Grep confirms the backoff machinery (scheduleRetry/retryAttempt, capped 10/20/40/60s) is invoked ONLY on network/resolve failures (lines 104, 130, 272, 295, 319, 322) and is never touched by the renderer-crash path. Given a content-driven OOM — which the code's own comment (lines 195-198) explicitly describes as reproducible on low-RAM TV sticks decoding the base64 logo + up to 10 slideshow images — a fresh renderer loading the identical oversized content OOMs identically, so the recreate→reload→OOM cycle is an unbounded tight loop: the display never stabilizes (flickering black) and every cycle re-fetches the display page, hammering the LAN/cloud server. Refutation angles (handling elsewhere / input impossible / diff misread) all fail. Confidence high; the precondition (reliable OOM) is the exact scenario the recovery code was written for.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by direct trace. In tv-app/.../MainActivity.kt, onRenderProcessGone (loadDisplay client line 246-249; base client line 187-190) does `ui.post { recreateWebView() }; return true` with no delay/counter/cap. recreateWebView() (lines 200-215) rebuilds the WebView and at line 209 immediately re-loads the SAME saved URL (`url != null -> loadDisplay(url) { ... }`). If the display page reliably OOMs the renderer — the exact trigger the code's own comment names at lines 194-198 ("OOM on low-RAM TV sticks decoding the base64 logo + up to 10 slideshow images"), which is content-driven and reproducible when a restaurant uploads several large slideshow images on a 1GB TV stick — the sequence loops forever: OOM -> onRenderProcessGone -> recreateWebView -> loadDisplay(same url) -> page decodes -> OOM. Grep confirms the only backoff (retryAttempt / scheduleRetry, lines 113-119) is wired solely into the connect/resolve-failure path and is never touched by the renderer-crash path; there is no postDelayed, no consecutive-crash counter, no attempt cap, and no LAN/cloud fallback between recreate attempts. Result: black flicker plus CPU (and, absent cache hits, network) pegged indefinitely, display never stabilizes — matching the claimed scenario. Fix direction (timestamped consecutive-crash counter + escalating postDelayed backoff, reset after the page survives) is correct for stopping the tight loop; caveat: backoff alone won't render OOMing content, so a full fix should also degrade content or fall back to an error/pairing screen after N crashes, and the reporter's LAN-vs-cloud fallback idea won't help since both serve the same OOMing page.

findings.title: resolve() treats every non-200 as "unknown code" — a resolver 5xx shows staff "Code not found" instead of a service/offline error
findings.evidence: `if (conn.responseCode != 200) return null` (line 336), and the caller comments "resolve() returns null ONLY for a genuine non-200 (unknown code)" then shows `setStatus("Code not found. Check the code on the POS screen.")` (lines 268-273). But non-200 includes 500/502/503 from the Vercel resolver (outage, cold-start failure, the free-tier pausing the README explicitly mentions) and 429 rate limiting — none of which mean the code is wrong.
findings.scenario: The Vercel pairing endpoint is down or paused and returns 503. Staff pairing a new TV type the correct 4-digit code from the POS Ambiance screen and are told "Code not found. Check the code on the POS screen." They regenerate the code, retype it, get the same message, and conclude the POS is broken — the one message the wrong-code/offline split (IOException → "check the TV's internet") was built to prevent is shown for a server outage.
findings.fix: Return null only for 404 (or 4xx); for >=500 (and 429) throw IOException (or a dedicated result) so the existing "Can't reach the pairing service" branch handles it and auto-retry proceeds.

refuter.reason: CONFIRMED. At tv-app/.../MainActivity.kt:336, `resolve()` does `if (conn.responseCode != 200) return null`. In Java, HttpURLConnection.getResponseCode() does NOT throw for HTTP 4xx/5xx — it returns the numeric status; only transport failures throw IOException. So a Vercel 503/500 (bad deploy, paused free-tier — explicitly acknowledged in this same file at lines 240-242) or a 429 rate-limit yields responseCode != 200 and returns null, without ever reaching the error inputStream that would throw. The caller connectWithCode (lines 267-274) maps info==null to setStatus("Code not found. Check the code on the POS screen."), and the comment at 269-271 wrongly assumes null == unknown code. The IOException handler at 315-318 ("Can't reach the pairing service") is never reached for HTTP-level outages. The resolver route.ts confirms the intended design: unknown code = 404, bad format = 400, success = 200 — so distinct statuses exist and are conflated. Verified the missing handling exists nowhere on the path and the input is real (Vercel 5xx/429; also a Supabase error maps to 404 at route.ts:40). Aggravating: on a first-time TV pairing the code is not yet persisted (written only at line 302 after success), so scheduleRetry() early-returns at line 115 and NO auto-retry fires — the misleading "Code not found" message persists with no recovery, so staff regenerate codes / re-pair as described. Failure scenario concrete and restaurant-experienced. Not on the do-not-report list.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED real bug. Trace: staff taps Connect with a correct 4-digit code (MainActivity.kt line 400) -> connectWithCode() -> resolve(code) at line 267. If the Vercel resolver returns 503 (paused project/bad deploy) or 429 (rate limit), HttpURLConnection.getResponseCode() (line 336) RETURNS that code without throwing (Android's OkHttp-backed HttpURLConnection only throws IOException for transport-level failures like timeout/DNS/reset, never for a valid 4xx/5xx status). So 503 != 200 -> return null, the IOException catch at line 315 is bypassed, info==null at line 268 is true, and line 271 shows 'Code not found. Check the code on the POS screen.' during a pure service outage. The comment at lines 269-270 ('null ONLY for a genuine non-200 (unknown code)') is the exact wrong assumption. I verified the resolver contract in admin/app/api/pair/route.ts: it returns 404 for a genuinely unknown code (line 41) and 200 for a valid one, so the proposed fix (map only 404 -> null, throw IOException for other non-200s) is CORRECT and matches the real contract; it correctly routes 5xx/429 to the 'Can't reach the pairing service' branch + scheduleRetry. Minor caveat on the fix: the resolver also returns 400 for a malformed code (line 27), which 'throw for any non-404' would mislabel as service-unreachable, but the TV validates code.length==4 before sending (line 395) so 400 is unreachable in practice; a cleaner fix maps both 400 and 404 to null. Added severity note the report missed: on FIRST-TIME pairing prefs 'code'/'last_url' are still null (line 302 saves only after success), so scheduleRetry() at line 272 hits the guard at line 115 and returns without scheduling any auto-retry, so the TV is stuck on the wrong 'Code not found' message with no self-recovery until staff manually retry.

findings.title: Manual pairing does not cancel an in-flight connectWithCode background thread — stale thread can overwrite the new code, hijack the display, and re-arm the cancelled retry
findings.evidence: Connect click does `ui.removeCallbacks(retryRunnable); retryAttempt = 0; connectWithCode(code)` (lines 396-400, comment claims "Manual entry wins over any pending retry"). But removeCallbacks only removes the *scheduled* runnable; a connectWithCode `thread { ... }` already launched by a previous auto-retry keeps running (resolve() alone can take up to 12s, plus 900ms per LAN probe). When it finishes it unconditionally executes `prefs.edit().putString("code", code)...` (line 302), `ui.post { loadDisplay(finalUrl) ... }` (line 303), `ui.post { setStatus(...) }` and `scheduleRetry()` — none of which check whether they were superseded.
findings.scenario: TV is being re-pointed from POS A to POS B (two-POS restaurant or replaced PC). An auto-retry for the old code is mid-resolve when staff type the new code and press Connect. The new display loads; seconds later the old thread completes, writes the OLD code back into prefs, and its posted loadDisplay(oldUrl) replaces the just-loaded new display — the TV shows the wrong restaurant/profile and remembers it (last_url persisted for the old target on its onPageFinished). In the wrong-code variant, the stale thread posts "Code not found" over the new attempt's "Connecting…" and scheduleRetry() re-arms the retry the user explicitly cancelled.
findings.fix: Add a generation counter (e.g. `@Volatile var connectGeneration`): increment it in the Connect click handler and at the start of connectWithCode; capture the value in the thread and bail out of every prefs write / ui.post / scheduleRetry if the generation no longer matches.

refuter.reason: CONFIRMED. The Connect handler at line 397 (`ui.removeCallbacks(retryRunnable)`) only cancels a not-yet-fired retry timer; it does nothing to in-flight async work. `connectWithCode` (line 263) launches a fire-and-forget `thread{}` (line 265) with NO cancellation, NO generation guard, and NO re-entrancy lock. That thread does a multi-second `resolve()` (6s connect + 6s read timeouts, line 333-334, plus 900ms LAN probes line 347), then UNCONDITIONALLY writes `prefs.putString("code", code)` (line 302) and posts `loadDisplay(finalUrl)` (line 304), which on success unconditionally writes `last_url` (line 307). `loadDisplay` unconditionally swaps `web.webViewClient` (line 220) and `web.loadUrl` (line 257) — last poster wins. A retry that already fired reaches `connectWithCode(oldCode)` via retrySaved line 129. Because the pairing UI (input + Connect button) is shown during "Connecting…" (connectWithCode -> setStatus -> showPairing), staff can press Connect for branch B while the branch-A thread is still resolving. Both threads then run to completion concurrently. Concrete outcomes, both grounded in code: (1) if A still resolves, its thread overwrites prefs code=A (line 302) and loads A's display (line 304->257) over B — TV shows the wrong restaurant and re-pairs to A on next boot; (2) if A now resolves null, `setStatus("Code not found")` (line 271) with statusView null (B's successful load already called removePairing) triggers showPairing (line 430), popping the pairing screen over B's working display. No existing code refutes this: no version counter, no thread interruption, no conditional guarding the prefs/loadUrl writes. The proposed generation-counter fix is appropriate. Scenario (TV moved between branches) matches the app's stated use case.

tracer.reason:
CONFIRMED real concurrency defect. The manual Connect handler (MainActivity.kt lines 396-400) only calls ui.removeCallbacks(retryRunnable) + retryAttempt=0 + removePairing() + connectWithCode(code). removeCallbacks cancels only a queued-but-unfired timer; it does NOT cancel an already-executing retry flow. Nothing in the file versions or aborts an in-flight connect: connectWithCode (263-325) spawns a bare thread{ resolve(code) } with no generation/cancel token, and its side effects are ungated — prefs code write at line 302 (background thread), the ui.post loadDisplay at 303, and the last_url write at 307. loadDisplay (217-259) just reassigns web.webViewClient (220) and posts loadUrl (257): last poster wins.

Concrete traceable path: last_url=branchA_url, code=branchA_code, branch A POS off so the retry loop is active. retryRunnable fires -> retrySaved() (123) -> loadDisplay(branchA_url) which removePairing()+loadUrl; the load fails (POS off) -> onResult(false) -> line 129 connectWithCode(branchA_code). That calls setStatus("Connecting...") which, since statusView is now null after removePairing, re-shows the pairing screen (setStatus->showPairing, 430) while a background resolve(branchA_code) thread is ALREADY in flight (this thread can run ~3-12s: 6s resolve timeouts + 900ms-per-IP LAN probes on the unreachable POS + cloud page load). Staff now see the pairing screen, type branchB_code, press Connect -> removeCallbacks (no pending timer to cancel) + connectWithCode(branchB_code) -> a SECOND background thread. Two ungated flows now race. Branch B (LAN reachable) completes fast (~1s): writes code=B, loads lanUrl_B, writes last_url=lanUrl_B. Branch A finishes later because of its slow LAN-probe timeouts: it then writes code=A (302), posts loadDisplay(cloudUrl_A) over branch B's display, and writes last_url=cloudUrl_A (307). Restaurant-visible outcome: the TV briefly shows branch B, then gets overwritten with branch A's cloud menu and re-pairs to branch A on next boot (wrong restaurant's menu). If instead branchA_code no longer resolves, the stale thread posts setStatus("Code not found...") (271) which re-invokes showPairing over the freshly-connected branch B display, popping the pairing screen over a working display. Both wrong outcomes match the report.

Even simpler realistic trigger needing no branch-move/auto-retry: staff type a wrong/old code, press Connect, get impatient during the multi-second "Connecting..." thread, retype the correct code and press Connect again -> two overlapping connectWithCode threads race with last-completion-wins on prefs and loadUrl.

Proposed fix direction is CORRECT: a monotonically-incremented connectGen captured at the start of each connect flow and re-checked on the UI thread before every side effect (the line-302 and line-307 prefs writes, the ui.post loadDisplay, and setStatus) properly discards stale flows. Two implementation notes: (1) the guard must cover the line-302 prefs write and the ui.post inside the background thread, not only the final loadDisplay onResult callback, since resolve() itself runs on the background thread; (2) loadDisplay must also gate the actual loadUrl (line 257), because reprobeLanIfOnCloud (155) posts loadDisplay from a background thread and would otherwise be another ungated writer. connectWithCode always runs on the UI thread (called from onCreate/retrySaved/recreateWebView/button/loadDisplay callbacks, all UI-posted), so incrementing the counter at connectWithCode entry is race-free.

findings.title: Search text is interpolated raw into a PostgREST .or() filter — commas/parentheses break the query
findings.evidence: `instQuery.or(\`restaurant_name.ilike.%${search}%,machine_id.ilike.%${search}%,phone.ilike.%${search}%\`)` — in PostgREST or() syntax, `,` separates conditions and `()` groups them, so any search containing them corrupts the filter string and the request errors; `instData` comes back null and the page silently renders the empty state.
findings.scenario: Admin searches for a restaurant saved as 'Le Grill, Oran' (or pastes a name with a comma/parenthesis). The Supabase query fails to parse, the page shows 'No users found.' even though the restaurant exists, with no error surfaced.
findings.fix: Escape/strip PostgREST reserved characters from the search term (e.g. remove [,()] before interpolation) or quote the pattern per PostgREST rules.

refuter.reason: Confirmed real at admin/app/admin/users/page.tsx:92. `search` (searchParams.q, only .trim()ed, line 59) is interpolated raw into a PostgREST .or() expression where `,` and `()` are structural. lib/supabase.ts is a vanilla supabase-js client that passes the .or() string verbatim as `or=(...)` with no escaping. PostgREST requires reserved chars in values to be double-quoted; percent-encoding doesn't help because the server decodes the param before the logical-tree parser splits on commas. So searching a name like 'Le Grill, Oran' yields `or=(restaurant_name.ilike.%Le Grill, Oran%,machine_id.ilike...)`, the in-value comma is parsed as a separator → malformed fragment → HTTP 400 / PGRST100 parse error. Line 95 destructures only `{ data: instData }` and discards `error`, so instData is null; line 107 `(instData || [])` → []; lines 165-168 render 'No users found.' with no error surfaced, even though the restaurant exists. Parentheses in the search term break it identically. No upstream sanitization or error handling exists on this path, so the claim cannot be refuted.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED at admin/app/admin/users/page.tsx:92. Trace: searchParams q -> search (line 58-59, trimmed, no sanitization) -> line 91-93 interpolates raw search into instQuery.or(`restaurant_name.ilike.%${search}%,machine_id.ilike.%${search}%,phone.ilike.%${search}%`). In PostgREST/.or() grammar, top-level commas separate OR conditions and () are logical-group delimiters, so a search value containing ',' or '()' (e.g. 'Le Grill, Oran' or 'Chicken (Halal)') produces broken fragments like ' Oran%' that are not valid column.operator.value triples -> PostgREST returns HTTP 400. supabase-js does not throw by default, so at line 95-99 the query resolves to {data:null,error}; only {data: instData} is destructured, error is discarded -> instData=null. Line 107 (instData||[]).map -> users=[]. Line 165-169 renders 'No users found.' with no error surfaced. Matches the claimed scenario exactly. Fix direction is roughly correct but imperfect: stripping [,()] avoids the crash but silently loses those chars from matching; the cleaner PostgREST-correct approach is to double-quote the pattern value (e.g. restaurant_name.ilike.\"%value%\"), which additionally must escape any embedded double-quote in the search term or it re-breaks. Scope note: this is an admin-portal search functionality bug, not a money-correctness issue, but it is real and concrete.

findings.title: 'extend' on a paused trial reactivates it but leaves stale paused_remaining_ms behind
findings.evidence: The extend branch sets `updateData = { expires_at: ..., status: 'active', updated_at: ... }` without `paused_remaining_ms: null`, unlike 'resume', 'reactivate', 'setExpiry' and 'setMode' which all clear it. The admin detail page renders the field unconditionally: `{trial.paused_remaining_ms && (<Row label="Paused With" value={...min remaining} />)}` (admin/app/admin/users/[machineId]/page.tsx:99).
findings.scenario: Admin pauses a trial with 5 days left (paused_remaining_ms stored), then later types '+7' in Adjust trial days. Trial becomes active for 7 days, but the user detail page keeps showing 'Paused With 7200 min remaining' on an active trial, misleading the admin about the machine's state.
findings.fix: Add `paused_remaining_ms: null` to the extend branch's updateData (it already forces status 'active').

refuter.reason: Confirmed end-to-end. The 'extend' case in admin/app/api/trial/action/route.ts:30 sets updateData = { expires_at, status: 'active', updated_at } with NO paused_remaining_ms: null, while every other branch that flips status to 'active' (resume L52, reactivate L70, setExpiry L102, setMode/trial L126) clears it. Supabase .update() only writes provided keys, so the value stored during 'pause' (L39) survives. The path is reachable on a paused trial: TrialControls.tsx renders the 'Adjust trial days' input unconditionally (no trialStatus gate), and handleAdjustDays (L52-56) sends action 'extend' with positive days; the extend case has no status guard. The detail page renders the field unconditionally at page.tsx:99 ({trial.paused_remaining_ms && <Row label='Paused With' .../>}), not gated on status==='paused'. Scenario: pause a trial with ~5 days left (paused_remaining_ms = 432,000,000 ms stored, expires_at frozen to now), later type '+7' -> extend sets status active, expires now+7d, but leaves paused_remaining_ms. The user detail page then shows 'Trial Active' badge alongside 'Paused With 7200 min remaining', misleading the admin. Real and concrete (admin-display bug, not money). Proposed fix (add paused_remaining_ms: null to extend's updateData) is correct.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by full code trace. admin/app/api/trial/action/route.ts:30 (extend branch) sets updateData = { expires_at, status:'active', updated_at } and omits paused_remaining_ms, so a partial Supabase .update() (route.ts:138) leaves any previously stored paused_remaining_ms intact. Precondition (paused trial) is a real, supported state: the pause action (route.ts:33-43) stores paused_remaining_ms and freezes expires_at, and the app renderer plus admin pages fully handle 'paused' (localized en/ar/fr strings, status badges, reduce-branch logic). The extend UI (TrialControls.tsx:126-139) is always shown regardless of status; typing '+7' calls handleAdjustDays->doAction('extend',{days:7}). Concrete state: paused trial, paused_remaining_ms=432000000 (5d), expires_at in past. After extend: currentExpiry(past) < now so baseDate=now, expires_at=now+7d, status='active', paused_remaining_ms stays 432000000. On re-render page.tsx:49 shows 'Trial Active' badge while page.tsx:99 `{trial.paused_remaining_ms && ...}` is truthy and renders 'Paused With 7200 min remaining' (432000000/60000=7200) — matching the reporter's number exactly. So an active trial misleadingly displays a stale paused row. Proposed fix (add paused_remaining_ms: null to the extend branch) is correct and consistent with resume/reactivate/setExpiry/setMode, and the `&&` guard then hides the row. Minor unrelated note: extend on a paused trial also drops the frozen remaining time by basing newExpiry on now, but that's outside the claimed display bug.

findings.title: Cloud display default font 'Inter' diverges from the desktop LAN display default 'Playfair Display'
findings.evidence: `fontFamily: raw[p + 'font_family'] || 'Inter'` — the desktop's SSE payload for the same display uses `dget('font_family') || 'Playfair Display'` (src/main/tablet/server.ts:95), and AmbianceScreen's UI default is also 'Playfair Display'. The keys are only written when the user changes a setting, so an untouched profile has no font_family key.
findings.scenario: A restaurant never customizes fonts. Its TV on the LAN shows the display in Playfair Display; the moment the TV falls back to the cloud URL (POS PC off / different WiFi), the whole screen switches to Inter — visibly different typography between the two paths that are supposed to be pixel-identical.
findings.fix: Change the buildInfo fallback to 'Playfair Display' to match server.ts.

refuter.reason: Confirmed real. admin/app/api/tv-html/route.ts:42 uses `raw[p + 'font_family'] || 'Inter'` while the LAN path src/main/tablet/server.ts:95 uses `dget('font_family') || 'Playfair Display'` (and AmbianceScreen.tsx:218 also defaults to 'Playfair Display'). The premise that an untouched profile has no font_family key is verified: it is written only via AmbianceScreen updateSetting (line 256/271), there is no default seeding anywhere in src (settings.repo.ts has none; grep finds only the 4 consumer sites), and cloud-sync.ts:33-36 uploads only keys already present in settingsRepo.getAll() without resolving defaults — so raw['display_font_family'] is undefined in the cloud route and the 'Inter' fallback fires. Both display-ui.ts files are identical and the client (display-ui.ts:1079) does `state.fontFamily = data.fontFamily || 'Inter'`, passing the server-provided value through unchanged (buildInfo always emits a non-empty string, so the client's own fallback is a no-op). Net: a restaurant that never customizes fonts sees Playfair Display on the LAN TV but Inter when the TV falls back to the cloud URL — a visible typographic divergence between two paths the code explicitly intends to be pixel-identical (route.ts:94). Not a money bug, but a genuine, concrete visual regression. Proposed fix (change route.ts:42 fallback to 'Playfair Display') is correct.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by full code trace. For a restaurant that never picks a font, the `display_font_family` key is never written: AmbianceScreen.tsx only calls settings.set on user click (lines 256, 267-271), and there is no setup seed for it. cloud-sync.ts:26-36 copies only existing `display_*` keys, so the key is also absent from Supabase `display_settings.settings` (=`raw`). LAN path server.ts:95 `dget('font_family') || 'Playfair Display'` → undefined key → 'Playfair Display', sent over SSE and applied by the shared client (display-ui.ts:1079/1098) as the serif. Cloud tv-html path route.ts:42 `raw[p+'font_family'] || 'Inter'` → undefined key → 'Inter', injected into the byte-identical getDisplayHTML template (route.ts:94-95 explicitly aims for the EXACT same HTML) and applied by the same client as sans-serif. AmbianceScreen's own UI default is 'Playfair Display' (lines 93, 218), so the operator-visible design is the serif. Concrete failure: a shop that never customizes fonts sees its main customer-facing display render in Playfair Display over LAN, then abruptly switch to Inter the moment the TV falls back to the cloud URL (POS PC off / different WiFi) — the two paths meant to be pixel-identical show different typography. Both templates load the Playfair font via the Google Fonts <link> (display-ui.ts:21), so it renders fine on both; only the fallback string diverges. The proposed fix (change route.ts:42 fallback to 'Playfair Display') is the correct direction — it matches both the LAN payload and the UI default. Note the same 'Inter' default also lives in the client (display-ui.ts:1079) and in the separate React TVDisplay.tsx renderer (lines 213, 248), but those only matter when fontFamily is genuinely missing; the canonical/correct default is Playfair Display, so fixing route.ts is the right minimal change for this specific LAN-vs-cloud divergence. Cosmetic only, not a money bug.

findings.title: Cloud TV 'Now Preparing' queue uses UTC today with gte, showing yesterday's stale order numbers after local midnight
findings.evidence: `todayStr()` returns `new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]` (UTC) and the query is `.eq('status','preparing').gte('order_date', todayStr())` while owner_orders.order_date is restaurant-LOCAL. The desktop's own queue builder was explicitly fixed to use localDate() with the comment 'not UTC — otherwise the TV Now Preparing queue ... shows the wrong day for a shop open past local midnight' (src/main/tablet/server.ts getQueuePayload).
findings.scenario: Between 00:00 and 01:00 local (UTC still on the previous day), the gte filter also matches yesterday's rows: any order left in 'preparing' (status sync silently failed or never completed) reappears on the cloud TV queue as e.g. '#42' while tonight's real orders are #1–#5 — customers see phantom order numbers.
findings.fix: Compute the local date (Africa/Algiers) and use `.eq('order_date', localToday)` to mirror the desktop's getQueuePayload.

refuter.reason: Confirmed real. admin/app/api/tv-html/route.ts:75 filters owner_orders (a LOCAL order_date column) with `.eq('status','preparing').gte('order_date', todayStr())`, where todayStr() (line 7-9) is `new Date().toISOString()` = UTC. The route runs server-side on Vercel (UTC) via the service-role client (admin/lib/supabase.ts). owner_orders.order_date is written as the restaurant-LOCAL day (orders.repo.ts:92/153 uses localDate(); owner-sync.ts:21/32 upserts order.order_date||localDate()). Algeria = UTC+1: during 00:00-00:59 local the UTC date is yesterday-local, so `.gte('order_date', yesterday-local)` also matches yesterday's rows. Any order still status='preparing' from yesterday (realistic: syncOrderStatusToCloud in owner-sync.ts:42-64 early-returns on offline and swallows errors, leaving stale preparing rows) reappears on the cloud TV queue as a phantom number while tonight's orders are #1-#5. The desktop's getQueuePayload (src/main/tablet/server.ts:136-140) was explicitly fixed to use localDate()+getByDate (exact-day) with a comment warning against exactly this UTC bug; the cloud route was not. The only cleanup (index.ts:511-521) runs only at startup, conditionally, and also uses UTC today (line 519), so it misses the same window and never fires for a shop running continuously past midnight. The proposed fix (local date + .eq) is correct.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED by full trace. admin/app/api/tv-html/route.ts line 75 filters `.eq('status','preparing').gte('order_date', todayStr())` where todayStr() (lines 7-9) = new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0] = a UTC date. Meanwhile owner_orders.order_date is written restaurant-LOCAL: src/main/sync/owner-sync.ts line 21/32 sets order_date = order.order_date || localDate(), and localDate() (orders.repo.ts lines 12-15) returns the local wall-clock day. The desktop's own getQueuePayload (server.ts lines 136-140) deliberately uses ordersRepo.getByDate(localDate()) with the comment 'not UTC ... shows the wrong day for a shop open past local midnight', so the cloud route diverges. Concrete failure (Algiers = UTC+1, no DST): at local 00:30 on 2026-07-10, UTC is still 23:30 on 2026-07-09, so todayStr()='2026-07-09' and .gte('order_date','2026-07-09') matches BOTH 07-09 and 07-10 rows. Yesterday's orders still stuck at status='preparing' — realistic because syncOrderStatusToCloud swallows all errors silently (owner-sync.ts lines 37/61), so a completed order whose status update failed stays 'preparing' in owner_orders forever — reappear on the cloud TV 'Now Preparing' queue as phantom numbers (e.g. #42) mixed with tonight's real #1–#5 (order_number=daily_number, which restarts each local day). Window is 00:00–00:59 local (the exact UTC+1 offset); the rest of the day UTC-date==local-date so the query is fine, which is why it went unnoticed. Proposed fix direction is CORRECT: mirror the desktop by computing Algiers-local today and using .eq('order_date', localToday) — .eq matches getByDate's exact-day semantics and avoids .gte also matching future dates. Hardcoding Africa/Algiers is acceptable given all shops are UTC+1 no-DST (deriving the machine's offset would be more general but yields the same result here).

findings.title: TVDisplay component is dead code (page redirects to /api/tv-html) and keeps /api/tv-orders + /api/tv-settings alive as orphan endpoints
findings.evidence: `export function TVDisplay(props: TVDisplayProps)` is imported nowhere — app/tv/[machineId]/page.tsx always `redirect()`s to /api/tv-html and only imports TVPicker. The only consumers of /api/tv-settings and /api/tv-orders are this dead component (grep: no other references; tv-app calls only /api/pair). The dead copy has already drifted from the real renderer: it reads only unprefixed `display_*` keys (lines 212-236), so it would render named profiles wrongly, and its tv-orders feed has no date filter at all.
findings.scenario: No runtime impact today, but ~700 lines of a second, diverged TV renderer plus two public API routes invite someone to 'fix' the wrong display path or resurrect a component whose per-profile key reading is wrong; the orphan endpoints also expose order numbers with stale unfiltered data.
findings.fix: Delete TVDisplay.tsx and the /api/tv-orders and /api/tv-settings routes (TVPicker + /api/tv-html cover the whole cloud TV flow).

findings.title: Profile name embedded unencoded in tv-html redirect breaks profiles containing & / + / #
findings.evidence: `redirect(\`/api/tv-html?machineId=${machineId}&profile=${searchParams.profile}\`)` (and line 48 `profile=${profiles[0].name}`) re-embed the already-decoded profile name without encodeURIComponent, while every other producer encodes it (TVPicker.tsx:70/84, pair/route.ts:63, AmbianceScreen buildTvUrl). Profile names are unvalidated free text from handleAddProfile.
findings.scenario: A restaurant names a display profile 'Grill & Go'. Opening the QR link /tv/<id>?profile=Grill%20%26%20Go decodes fine, but the server redirect emits profile=Grill & Go — /api/tv-html parses profile as 'Grill ' (rest becomes a bogus 'Go' param), finds no display_settings row, and the TV renders a default-styled screen (wrong colors, no panels) instead of the configured profile.
findings.fix: Wrap both redirect interpolations in encodeURIComponent(...).

refuter.reason: Confirmed real. admin/app/tv/[machineId]/page.tsx:18 (and :48) interpolate searchParams.profile / profiles[0].name into the /api/tv-html redirect WITHOUT encodeURIComponent, while every other producer encodes (TVPicker.tsx:70/84, AmbianceScreen buildTvUrl at :153-162). In Next.js App Router searchParams.profile is already decoded, so a name like 'Grill & Go' is spliced in raw. The callee admin/app/api/tv-html/route.ts:62 does url.searchParams.get('profile') then :73 .eq('profile_name', profile).single(); the literal '&' is parsed as a query separator so profile becomes 'Grill ' (trailing space) + a bogus 'Go' param, no display_settings row matches, raw falls back to {} (line 78) and buildInfo returns all defaults -> TV renders default colors/gradient/panels instead of the configured profile. '#' (client fragment, never sent) and '+' (decoded to space by URLSearchParams) break the same way. Profile names are unvalidated free text: handleAddProfile at AmbianceScreen.tsx:292 only .trim()s, and the UI placeholder example 'Terrace TV' already contains a space, so 'Grill & Go' / 'TV #2' are realistic. Next.js redirect() cannot fix this because a post-assembly encoder cannot distinguish the literal '&' from the structural separator, and Next preserves query '&'/'=' by design. Refutation attempts (redirect encodes it, input impossible, searchParams not decoded) all fail. Second instance at line 48 for the single-profile auto-redirect. Proposed fix (wrap both interpolations in encodeURIComponent) is correct.

tracer.reason: Verified by full trace. admin/app/tv/[machineId]/page.tsx:18 re-embeds the already-decoded searchParams.profile with a literal '&' and no encodeURIComponent: `redirect(`/api/tv-html?machineId=${machineId}&profile=${searchParams.profile}`)`. Concrete state/inputs: owner creates a profile named "Grill & Go" (AmbianceScreen.tsx:292-296 handleAddProfile stores newProfileName.trim() as free text with zero validation; the row's profile_name = "Grill & Go"). The QR/share link is built correctly via buildTvUrl with encodeURIComponent (AmbianceScreen.tsx:158) → /tv/<id>?profile=Grill%20%26%20Go. Opening it: Next decodes searchParams.profile = "Grill & Go" (page.tsx:17 truthy) → line 18 emits a 307 Location `/api/tv-html?machineId=<id>&profile=Grill%20&%20Go` (browser encodes spaces but never the structural '&'). Consumer tv-html/route.ts:62 `url.searchParams.get('profile')` splits on the injected '&' → profile = "Grill " (bogus ' Go' param discarded). Line 69 p="display_Grill _", line 73 `.eq('profile_name','Grill ')` matches no row → dsResult.data null → raw={} → buildInfo returns all defaults (accent #f97316, text #fff, gradientPreset 0, empty restaurant_name/logo/panels). Result: TV shows an unbranded default-styled screen instead of the configured profile. Also breaks for '+' (decoded to space) and '#' (truncates query). Same defect on line 48 (single-profile fast-path) for a lone '&'-named profile. Inconsistency confirmed: every other producer encodes — TVPicker.tsx:70/84, pair/route.ts:63, buildTvUrl:158 — only page.tsx:18/48 omit it (line 30 uses literal 'default', safe). Proposed fix is correct: wrapping both interpolations in encodeURIComponent restores round-trip (encodeURIComponent("Grill & Go")→Grill%20%26%20Go, which URLSearchParams.get decodes back exactly). redirect() treats the URL as an opaque Location string and does not re-encode query params, so the fix is required and sufficient. machineId is a UUID-like id so leaving it unencoded is harmless in practice.

findings.title: Undeployable skeleton: crypto.ts references scripts/genkeys.mjs which does not exist, and license-server/ has no wrangler.toml, package.json, or tsconfig
findings.evidence: `/** Import the PKCS8 (base64) private key produced by scripts/genkeys.mjs. */` — no genkeys.mjs exists anywhere in the repo (repo scripts/ contains only the old HMAC tools: generate-serial.ts, generate-unlock.ts, keygen.js), and license-server/ contains only schema.sql + src/. VERDICT for the folder: coherent-but-unfinished, not broken — the schema matches every column index.ts reads/writes, all SQL uses bound parameters (the dynamic UPDATE at index.ts:260 builds column names from hardcoded Object.keys of code-constructed objects, so no injection), the base64url padding math and Ed25519 usage are correct, and admin auth is a reasonable constant-time-style compare. But it cannot be deployed (no D1 binding/secret config, no key generation), and the desktop app has no verifier for these tokens yet (it still uses the old HMAC activation in src/main/activation/activation.ts, whose 16-hex-uppercase machineId does match the server's regex).
findings.scenario: Anyone trying to deploy this today cannot: wrangler has no config for the DB binding or LICENSE_PRIVATE_KEY/ADMIN_API_KEY secrets, and there is no documented way to produce the PKCS8 Ed25519 keypair the code expects.
findings.fix: Add license-server/wrangler.toml (D1 binding + secret names), a package.json/tsconfig, and a scripts/genkeys.mjs that outputs the PKCS8-base64 private key and the raw public key the desktop verifier will embed.

findings.title: First-contact race: two concurrent checks from an unknown machine make the second INSERT violate the PRIMARY KEY and return an unhandled 500
findings.evidence: `if (!lic) { ... env.DB.prepare('INSERT INTO licenses (machine_id, ...)').run() }` — a plain INSERT with machine_id as PRIMARY KEY, and there is no try/catch anywhere in fetch(). Two overlapping /v1/license/check requests for the same new machine_id both see lic === null; the loser's .run() rejects with a UNIQUE constraint error and the Worker returns a raw 500 (no JSON body, no CORS headers).
findings.scenario: Fresh install: the app's startup license check and an immediate retry (or a second window) fire near-simultaneously; one request gets a 500 instead of the trial token, so the first-run experience intermittently shows a license error.
findings.fix: Use INSERT OR IGNORE and always re-read the row afterwards; additionally wrap fetch() in a try/catch that returns json({error:'internal'}, 500) so failures still carry CORS/JSON.

refuter.reason: Confirmed real code-level defect in license-server/src/index.ts. The SELECT at line 104 (getLicense) and the plain INSERT at lines 111-118 are two non-atomic D1 operations with no transaction; schema.sql:5 makes machine_id a PRIMARY KEY, so a duplicate INSERT throws "UNIQUE constraint failed". The default fetch() (index.ts:273-288) has no try/catch, and handleCheck only try/catches req.json() — so a losing concurrent first-contact request's rejected .run() propagates as an unhandled rejection and Cloudflare returns a raw 500 with no JSON body and none of the CORS headers (which are only attached inside the json() helper). Two overlapping /v1/license/check calls for the same new machineId can both read lic===null → both INSERT → the loser 500s. This is a textbook non-atomic upsert TOCTOU, and the proposed INSERT OR IGNORE + re-read + top-level try/catch is the correct fix. Refutations fail: no error handling exists elsewhere on this path, the INSERT is genuinely plain (not OR IGNORE), machine_id validation + PK are verified. Confidence is medium (not high) only because the license-server is an untracked WIP skeleton and no desktop client calls this endpoint yet (the app still uses the old HMAC activation per F060), so the "restaurant experiences it today" impact is forward-looking; the defect and its failure mode, however, are concrete and accurately described.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED at the code level. schema.sql:5 declares `machine_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY` (plain table, no ON CONFLICT), and index.ts does a non-atomic check-then-insert: getLicense at line 104 returns null for a fresh machine, then the INSERT at 111-118 (.run() at 118) is not wrapped in try/catch (the only try/catch in handleCheck is around req.json() at 88-92), and fetch() at 273-288 has no try/catch either — it just `return handleCheck(...)` at 282. Cloudflare Worker invocations run concurrently and D1 offers no serialization across the SELECT and INSERT, so two overlapping POST /v1/license/check with the same never-seen machineId (e.g. {machineId:"ABC123"}) both see lic===null; the loser's .run() rejects with `UNIQUE constraint failed: licenses.machine_id`, the rejection propagates out of the fetch handler, and the Workers runtime returns a bare HTTP 500 with no JSON body and no CORS headers (CORS is only attached by the json() helper). That matches the claim exactly. The proposed fix is correct and idiomatic: INSERT OR IGNORE lets the loser fall through and re-read the winner's row (the code already re-reads at line 119), and a top-level try/catch in fetch() returning json({error:'internal'},500) preserves CORS/JSON on any failure. Confidence is medium, not high, for two reasons: (1) the race is a one-time, per-machine event confined to a single D1 round-trip window (~tens of ms) before the row's first-ever insert — after that the row exists permanently and the path is never hit again; and (2) nothing currently calls /v1/license/check — grep found no caller in the desktop app (this is an untracked WIP skeleton), so it cannot actually bite a restaurant in production today. It is a genuine latent defect that goes live the moment the app is wired to check in, where a startup double-fire, double-launch, or retry-on-timeout would intermittently 500 the first-run license check.

findings.title: Unauthenticated /v1/license/check overwrites admin-curated restaurant_name/phone and allows unbounded junk-row creation
findings.evidence: `restaurant_name = COALESCE(?, restaurant_name), phone = COALESCE(?, phone)` — COALESCE only protects against NULL: any non-null client-supplied value replaces the stored one on every check, and the endpoint has no auth or rate limit. Any id matching /^[A-Z0-9]{6,64}$/ also auto-creates a fresh licenses row (line 111), so a script can insert unlimited garbage rows.
findings.scenario: Owner cleans up a restaurant's name/phone in the admin data; the very next app check (or anyone who knows the 16-hex machine id) POSTs a different restaurantName and silently clobbers it. Separately, a loop POSTing random ids pollutes the D1 licenses table with thousands of junk trial rows, drowning the real customers in /v1/admin/list.
findings.fix: Fill metadata only when currently NULL (COALESCE(restaurant_name, ?)) or store app-reported metadata in separate columns from admin-entered ones; add basic per-IP rate limiting on the check endpoint.

refuter.reason: Verified in the working tree (license-server/src/index.ts). Lines 96-97 set restaurantName/phone to null only when the client omits them; the check UPDATE at lines 125-126 (bound at 129) uses COALESCE(?, restaurant_name)/COALESCE(?, phone), which substitutes the stored value ONLY when the arg is NULL. So any non-null client string overwrites the stored value. These are the same restaurant_name/phone columns the admin curates via the setInfo action (lines 243-248), so a check overwrites admin edits — the intent comment ('don't clobber with nulls') confirms only NULLs were guarded. The path has no auth: fetch() (line 282) routes /v1/license/check straight to handleCheck; requireAdmin guards only /v1/admin/*; CORS is '*'. Line 111 INSERTs a fresh trial row for any machineId matching /^[A-Z0-9]{6,64}$/ (autoTrial defaults true, line 102), with no rate limit anywhere (no wrangler.toml/KV/DO; dir holds only schema.sql + src/). Concrete unrefutable scenario needing no client: because the endpoint is public + CORS '*' + unauthenticated, anyone who knows a machine id can POST an arbitrary restaurantName/phone and silently overwrite it, and a loop of random ids mass-creates junk trial rows that sort to the top of /v1/admin/list (ORDER BY last_seen DESC), drowning real customers. Caveats lowering confidence: (1) impact is on the vendor's licensing/admin dashboard, NOT money/POS state — effective() (lines 59-71) derives status only from status + subscription_until, which the check UPDATE never modifies, so no restaurant is wrongly locked or billed; (2) the 'app overwrites admin edits' half depends on the desktop client actually sending restaurantName, and no client code exists yet (grep for license/check/signToken in src/ found nothing — WIP untracked skeleton). But the unauthenticated arbitrary-overwrite and unbounded-junk-row facts follow directly from the code regardless of client wiring, and I could not refute them, so the finding stands.

tracer.reason: Confirmed by code trace. /v1/license/check is routed at index.ts:282 with NO auth (requireAdmin is only invoked in handleAdmin). CLOBBER (line 125): the existing-row UPDATE binds the client-supplied restaurantName/phone (index.ts:96-97,129) into `restaurant_name = COALESCE(?, restaurant_name)`. SQLite COALESCE returns the first non-NULL arg, so any non-null client value overwrites the stored value; the "don't clobber with nulls" comment shows only the null case was guarded. Scenario: admin corrects a name via /v1/admin/mutate setInfo (lines 243-249), then the next check carrying any restaurantName (the app's own setup name via the registerInstallation pattern, or an attacker who knows the machine_id) silently overwrites it. JUNK ROWS (line 111): regex /^[A-Z0-9]{6,64}$/ (line 94) accepts any random alphanumeric id, and an unknown id triggers an unconditional INSERT of a fresh trial row (lines 106-118) with no auth or rate limit — a loop creates unlimited rows. /v1/admin/list (lines 170-184) defaults to 200 rows ordered last_seen DESC; junk rows have last_seen=now so they sort to the top and bury real customers. Both paths are concrete and reachable. Fix direction is sound: COALESCE(restaurant_name, ?) preserves stored/admin data and only populates while NULL, or use separate app-reported columns; per-IP rate limiting is a reasonable (though not complete, given IP rotation) mitigation — a stronger guard is to not auto-create on the unauthenticated check path. Caveat: license-server is a WIP untracked skeleton with no client wired up yet (app currently uses the Supabase cloud.ts path), so the fully-automatic app re-clobber depends on the forthcoming client, but the unauthenticated endpoint makes the manual clobber and random-id junk-row creation real on any deployed instance. Not covered by the accepted-exclusions list (junk creation needs no machine_id at all).

findings.title: 'reinstate' without days on a lapsed subscription returns ok:true but leaves the machine effectively expired
findings.evidence: `case 'reinstate': set = { status: 'active', subscription_until: Number.isFinite(days) ? addDaysIso(null, days) : lic!.subscription_until }` — when no days are given it keeps the old subscription_until; if that date is in the past, effective() (line 65) still derives 'expired', so the action is a functional no-op while responding { ok: true }.
findings.scenario: A monthly customer lapses and gets revoked; they pay again and the owner calls {action:'reinstate'} with no days (the natural 'undo revoke' call). The API answers ok:true; the restaurant's POS stays locked and the owner believes it is fixed.
findings.fix: If the stored subscription_until is in the past (or NULL on a non-lifetime plan) and no days were supplied, return 400 requiring days — or extend from now, matching the 'extend' semantics.

refuter.reason: Confirmed at license-server/src/index.ts. With no `days` in the request body, line 212 `parseInt(body?.days,10)` yields NaN, so at line 241 `reinstate` takes the else branch: `subscription_until = lic!.subscription_until` (unchanged) while `status='active'`. If that stored date is in the past, effective() (line 63-65) returns 'expired' for an active license whose subDate < now, so the next /v1/license/check signs a token with st:'expired' and the POS stays locked — yet handleAdmin returns `{ ok:true }` (line 267). This reproduces on both natural "undo" flows: revoke (line 238, leaves the lapsed past date) and even the documented expire→reinstate pairing (expire sets subscription_until=nowIso() at line 235, which is in the past by the time reinstate runs). Reachability is real: unlike `extend` (line 226 guards `bad_days`), `reinstate` has no days-required guard, and the Next.js admin portal uses a separate action set (extend/reduce) so the Worker's /v1/admin/mutate is called directly, making `{action:'reinstate'}` with no days a valid, natural request. No compensating handling exists elsewhere. The only mild caveat — the response body also carries license.effective:'expired' that a careful UI could inspect — does not negate the ok:true no-op defect.

tracer.reason: CONFIRMED real. File license-server/src/index.ts, line 240-242. Trace: POST /v1/admin/mutate with {action:'reinstate'} and no days → days = parseInt(undefined,10) = NaN → Number.isFinite(NaN)=false → subscription_until is left at lic!.subscription_until unchanged. For a lapsed customer that stored date is in the past (either naturally expired, or set to nowIso() by a prior 'expire' at line 235, or an old paid-through date carried through 'revoke' at line 238 which never touches subscription_until). The write sets status='active' but keeps the past date. effective() (lines 63-66): status='active' with a past subDate → now<=subDate is false → returns {st:'expired'}. So the mutate handler returns {ok:true} (line 267) while the machine is effectively expired, and the next /v1/license/check (line 133) signs a token with st:'expired' → the POS stays locked. Concrete state: machine MACHINE123 with status='revoked' (or 'expired'), subscription_until='2026-07-01T00:00:00Z', server date 2026-07-09; call reinstate with no days → response ok:true but effective='expired', POS remains locked. The 'undo expire' path (the natural use, per the 'can be reinstated' note on line 234) is broken identically because expire stamps subscription_until=nowIso(). One nuance worth noting: the mutate RESPONSE object at line 267 does include effective:'expired', so a careful admin UI could surface the real state — but the top-level ok:true is what a naive 'undo revoke' caller keys on, matching the reported scenario. Proposed fix direction is sound: when no days supplied and stored subscription_until is null-on-non-lifetime or in the past, either 400 requiring days or extend-from-now; it correctly preserves the working lifetime case (status='active' + null sub → active at line 64) and the working case where the stored date is still in the future. Returning 400 to force explicit days is the safest of the two options.

findings.title: Trial expiry is enforced only against the local clock — rolling the clock back keeps an expired trial 'active' indefinitely
findings.evidence: Lines 105-110: `if (data.status === 'active' && data.expires_at) { const expiresAt = new Date(data.expires_at); if (expiresAt < new Date()) { return { status: 'expired', ... } } }` — the comparison uses the client machine's clock. Nothing server-side ever flips trials.status to 'expired': the trials table has no cron, and admin/app/api/trial/action/route.ts only updates rows on manual admin actions. So the cloud row stays status='active' forever unless an admin intervenes.
findings.scenario: A trial user sets the Windows clock back two weeks. Every 30s checkTrialCloud gets status 'active' (row says active, local now < expires_at), refreshes trial_expires_at locally, and the app never locks — the 7-day trial runs indefinitely with no tampering of the app itself, just the OS clock.
findings.fix: Compare expires_at against a server-derived timestamp (e.g. select now() via an RPC, or read the Date response header), or have the admin portal / a scheduled Supabase function flip status to 'expired' so the client's status check is authoritative.

refuter.reason: Confirmed. cloud.ts:107 is the ONLY expiry enforcement for an 'active' trial row and it compares expires_at to the local clock (new Date()); the comment claims 'server-side' but it is client-side. Repo-wide search confirms nothing server-side ever flips trials.status to 'expired': the only writers are the client's startTrial insert and admin/app/api/trial/action/route.ts (manual admin actions only — no vercel.json cron, no Supabase functions/pg_cron, license-server WIP is unwired). checkTrialCloud (src/main/index.ts:208-213) then refreshes trial_expires_at locally and broadcasts 'active' every 30s; the lock only fires on 'expired'/'paused'. No clock-tamper protection exists anywhere, and the staleness lock (index.ts:175) computes Date.now()-lastCloudSuccessTime which goes NEGATIVE after rollback, defeating even that. Rolling the Windows clock back keeps the trial 'active' indefinitely across restarts with no app tampering — distinct from the accepted 'renderer-side trial lock' risk since this is main-process + server design trusting the OS clock.

tracer.reason: Confirmed by full code trace. The only expiry decision for an 'active' trial row is cloud.ts:107 `if (expiresAt < new Date())` — the client machine's clock. Nothing server-side ever flips trials.status to 'expired': admin/app/api/trial/action/route.ts does so only on manual admin actions, and the repo contains no SQL trigger/cron for the Supabase trials table (the 'derived automatically' expiry exists only in the untracked WIP license-server/schema.sql, not wired in). The comment at cloud.ts:108 ('Expired but status not yet updated — treat as expired') confirms the row stays 'active' past expiry by design. Trace: watcher (index.ts:246, every 30s) → checkTrialStatus → with clock rolled back, day7 < day1 is false → returns 'active' → index.ts:208-213 refreshes local trial_expires_at and pushes 'active'; the renderer lock (App.tsx:42/154) fires only on a trial:locked push, and appStore.ts:114 sets trialStatus 'active' at boot with no local expiry check. The staleness guard (index.ts:175) resets on every successful cloud check and net.isOnline() stays true, so no offline lock triggers. Scenario: on day 8 the user rolls Windows back to day 1 and stays online — the 7-day trial runs indefinitely (a 2-week rollback stays within TLS cert validity, so Supabase calls succeed). This is a main-process flaw, distinct from the accepted 'renderer-side trial lock' item. Proposed fix direction is sound: server-derived timestamp (RPC now() or Date response header) and/or a scheduled function flipping status; note bare 'select now()' needs an RPC under PostgREST, and a cron-only fix leaves up to one cron-interval of slack, so combining both is best.

findings.title: Dead triggerBackupAfterChange would kill the 1-minute live backup: clearTimeout() on the interval handle, new timer never stored
findings.evidence: `if (backupInterval) { clearTimeout(backupInterval) } setTimeout(() => { checkAndBackup() }, 30000)` — clearTimeout on a setInterval id cancels the interval (Node shares the timer pool), permanently stopping the every-minute live backup (and its WAL checkpoint), and the debounce timer id is discarded so it can never be cleared. The function is currently called from nowhere (grep confirms only the definition), so it is dead code carrying a latent bug.
findings.scenario: No current runtime impact; but the first developer who wires up 'backup after change' as the name invites will silently disable the live backup system that the Backup UI promises ('max 1 minute data loss').
findings.fix: Delete the function, or fix it to use a separate `debounceTimer` variable with clearTimeout/setTimeout and leave backupInterval untouched.

findings.title: triggerBackupAfterChange is dead code that would permanently kill the 1-minute live backup loop if ever wired up
findings.evidence: `if (backupInterval) { clearTimeout(backupInterval) }` — backupInterval holds the setInterval handle for the every-minute live backup (line 100). In Node, clearTimeout on an interval handle cancels the interval, so the first call would silently stop the continuous backup while leaving backupInterval non-null; the setTimeout at line 126 is never stored, so the 'debounce' can never actually debounce. Grep confirms no caller anywhere in src/.
findings.scenario: Currently unreachable (no caller). If a future change calls triggerBackupAfterChange() after a DB write — as its name and comment invite — the first invocation cancels the live 1-minute backup system for the rest of the session, so a PC crash later that day loses up to a full day of orders instead of at most one minute.
findings.fix: Delete the function, or store the debounce handle in its own `let debounceTimer` variable and clearTimeout that instead of backupInterval.

findings.title: categoriesRepo.delete (plus its IPC/preload chain) is dead code and can never succeed for a category that has menu items
findings.evidence: `const result = getDb().prepare('DELETE FROM categories WHERE id = ?').run(id)` — menu_items.category_id has a plain `FOREIGN KEY (category_id) REFERENCES categories(id)` (001_initial.ts:78, no cascade), and connection.ts enables foreign_keys, so this DELETE throws 'FOREIGN KEY constraint failed' for any category containing menu items — including soft-deleted (is_active=0) ones, which delete flows never clean up. The whole chain (categories.ipc.ts:21-23, preload index.ts:33) is exposed but no renderer page ever calls window.api.categories.delete.
findings.scenario: Unreachable from the UI today. If a future 'delete category' button calls it, deleting any real category (they all contain items, active or soft-deleted) rejects the IPC promise with a raw SqliteError instead of deleting or showing a meaningful message.
findings.fix: Either remove the dead delete chain, or make delete() reassign/soft-handle: refuse with a clear error when active items exist and NULL-out or migrate category_id of soft-deleted items before deleting.

findings.title: menuRepo.hardDelete is dead code and would throw an FK constraint error for any item that was ever ordered
findings.evidence: `hardDelete(id: number): boolean { const result = getDb().prepare('DELETE FROM menu_items WHERE id = ?').run(id) ... }` — no caller anywhere (menu:delete IPC uses the soft delete()). order_items.menu_item_id references menu_items(id) with no ON DELETE action and foreign_keys=ON (connection.ts:60), so hard-deleting any menu item present in past orders throws 'FOREIGN KEY constraint failed'.
findings.scenario: Dead today. If wired to a future 'delete permanently' button, deleting any menu item that appears in even one historical order would throw instead of deleting, and an item deleted successfully (never ordered) is fine — inconsistent, confusing behavior.
findings.fix: Remove hardDelete, or keep it but explicitly document/guard it (check order_items references first and fall back to soft delete).

findings.title: settingsRepo.getMultiple is dead code and throws a SQL syntax error when given an empty keys array
findings.evidence: `const placeholders = keys.map(() => '?').join(',')` followed by `SELECT key, value FROM settings WHERE key IN (${placeholders})` produces `WHERE key IN ()` for keys = [], which is a SqliteError (syntax error) in SQLite. Grep across src/ shows no caller — the function is dead code.
findings.scenario: No current caller, so no user-visible failure today; any future caller passing a dynamically-built (possibly empty) key list would crash the IPC handler with 'SqliteError: near ")": syntax error'.
findings.fix: Delete the function, or add `if (keys.length === 0) return {}` before preparing the statement.

findings.title: Wake-from-sleep instantly fires the stale-cloud trial lock before the first cloud check can run — spurious lock screen with working internet
findings.evidence: Lines 175-179: `const secondsSinceCloud = Math.floor((Date.now() - lastCloudSuccessTime) / 1000); if (secondsSinceCloud >= CLOUD_STALE_SECONDS) { ... mainWindow?.webContents.send('trial:locked', 'offline'); return }`. checkOfflineInstant runs every 3 seconds; lastCloudSuccessTime does not advance while the PC sleeps, and the stale check runs BEFORE net.isOnline() is consulted and independently of whether a cloud check has had a chance to run since resume.
findings.scenario: A trial restaurant's POS PC sleeps overnight (Windows default power settings). On resume with perfectly working internet, within 3 seconds checkOfflineInstant sees secondsSinceCloud > 600 and sends trial:locked 'offline' — App.tsx locks the POS ('offline-locked') — and it stays locked for up to ~30s until the next trialCheckInterval tick's checkTrialCloud succeeds and sends status 'active'. Staff see a scary license-lock screen every morning for no reason.
findings.fix: On resume (powerMonitor 'resume' event) or whenever the stale threshold is crossed, trigger an immediate checkTrialCloud() and only send trial:locked if that check fails; alternatively reset lastCloudSuccessTime on powerMonitor resume before evaluating staleness.

refuter.reason: Confirmed in the working tree. src/main/index.ts:175-179: checkOfflineInstant (every 3s, line 243) evaluates `secondsSinceCloud >= CLOUD_STALE_SECONDS` (600s) BEFORE consulting net.isOnline() and sends `trial:locked 'offline'` unconditionally. lastCloudSuccessTime (line 128) only advances after a successful Supabase fetch in checkTrialCloud (line 206) and is frozen during system sleep while Date.now() keeps advancing. There is no powerMonitor resume handler and no powerSaveBlocker anywhere in src/, so overnight sleep is both possible and unhandled. On resume, the first 3s tick sees hours of staleness and locks; the competing 30s checkTrialCloud cannot win the race because it early-returns when net.isOnline() is false (line 197, common right after resume) and otherwise needs an async Supabase round-trip before sending 'active', while the lock send is synchronous — and checkOfflineInstant re-locks every 3s until a fetch succeeds. Renderer confirms impact: App.tsx:42-45 sets 'offline-locked' and renders the full-screen TrialLockedPage (App.tsx:154-159), cleared only by trial:status-update 'active' (App.tsx:60-62). Result: trial restaurants get a spurious license-lock screen within ~3s of every wake-from-sleep despite working internet, lasting until the next successful cloud check (up to ~30s+). Claim's mechanism, scenario, and proposed fix (powerMonitor resume → verify-then-lock or reset staleness) are all accurate.

tracer.reason: Confirmed by full code trace. src/main/index.ts:128 initializes lastCloudSuccessTime = Date.now() (wall clock) and it is only refreshed inside a successful checkTrialCloud() (line 206). checkOfflineInstant runs every 3s (line 243) and at lines 174-180 evaluates the stale-cloud condition FIRST and returns after sending trial:locked 'offline' — before consulting net.isOnline() (line 182) and independent of whether any cloud check has run since resume. There is no powerMonitor handling anywhere in src/. Concrete scenario: trial machine sleeps overnight; wall clock advances >600s (CLOUD_STALE_SECONDS) while timers are suspended; on resume the overdue 3s timer fires the synchronous checkOfflineInstant immediately, while checkTrialCloud needs an async Supabase fetch (plus post-wake Wi-Fi re-association), so trial:locked always wins the race. Renderer (App.tsx:42-45, 154-159) then shows the full-screen TrialLockedPage z-[200] overlay 'App Locked — No Internet' with NO retry button for the offline reason (TrialLockedPage.tsx:125), re-asserted every 3s, until the 30s trialCheckInterval's checkTrialCloud succeeds (lines 206-213) and App.tsx:58-62 clears it — i.e., a spurious scary license-lock for ~3-35+ seconds every morning with working internet. Proposed fix direction is right (powerMonitor 'resume' → immediate checkTrialCloud, and/or reset lastCloudSuccessTime on resume); note that resetting the timestamp alone slightly weakens the anti-tamper intent (sleep/wake cycling while firewalling Supabase renews the grace window, since net.isOnline() stays true), so it should be paired with the immediate cloud check.

findings.title: Dead event chain: main sends 'updater:up-to-date' and preload exposes onUpToDate, but no renderer component ever subscribes
findings.evidence: src/main/index.ts:280-282: "autoUpdater.on('update-not-available', () => { mainWindow?.webContents.send('updater:up-to-date') })" and src/preload/index.ts:189-193 expose "onUpToDate".
