findings.title: Startup owner_orders bulk-complete uses UTC date, missing local-yesterday's orders when the app starts between 00:00 and 00:59 local
findings.evidence: Line 519-520: `const today = new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]` then `.lt('order_date', today)`. owner_orders.order_date is the restaurant-LOCAL date (written from localDate()/order.order_date per owner-sync.ts:21-32), but this cleanup computes 'today' in UTC. In Algeria (UTC+1), between 00:00 and 00:59 local the UTC date is still the previous local day, so `.lt('order_date', <local-yesterday>)` excludes exactly the rows autoCompletePreviousDays just completed locally.
findings.scenario: Staff open the POS at 00:30 local after a late night. ordersRepo.autoCompletePreviousDays() marks yesterday's leftover 'preparing' orders completed locally, but the Supabase update skips them (order_date == UTC 'today'), so the owner dashboard keeps showing yesterday's orders stuck in 'preparing' until some later startup after 01:00 or a manual status change.
findings.fix: Use the same restaurant-local date as the rest of the sync layer: `const today = localDate()` (imported from orders.repo), matching the fix already applied in owner-sync.ts and analytics-sync.ts.

refuter.reason: Confirmed in working tree. src/main/index.ts:519 computes `today` in UTC (`new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]`) while owner_orders.order_date is restaurant-LOCAL (owner-sync.ts:21 uses order.order_date || localDate(); local orders stamp order_date via localDate(), orders.repo.ts:92/153). In Algeria (UTC+1), between 00:00 and 00:59 local the UTC date equals local-yesterday, so `.lt('order_date', today)` excludes order_date == local-yesterday — exactly the rows ordersRepo.autoCompletePreviousDays() (orders.repo.ts:269-275, which uses localDate()) just bulk-completed locally. No other path reconciles: autoCompletePreviousDays is a raw SQL UPDATE with no per-order cloud sync, and syncOrderStatusToCloud fires only on manual IPC status changes (orders.ipc.ts:42,48). Worse than claimed: the cloud cleanup is inside `if (completed > 0)` (index.ts:514), so a later restart after 01:00 finds 0 local rows to complete and skips the Supabase update entirely — stale rows persist until a future day again has local leftovers. Visible impact: admin/app/api/tv-orders/route.ts:14-19 selects status='preparing' with NO date filter, so the TV 'now preparing' board shows yesterday's ghost order numbers indefinitely, and the owner dashboard shows them stuck in 'preparing'. The comment in owner-sync.ts:16-20 documents this exact UTC-vs-local 00:00-00:59 bug class; the fix was applied there and in analytics-sync.ts but missed at index.ts:519. Proposed fix (use localDate()) is correct.

tracer.reason: Verified by code trace. src/main/index.ts:519-520 computes `today` via `new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]` (UTC) and runs `.lt('order_date', today)` on owner_orders, but owner_orders.order_date is written as the restaurant-LOCAL date (owner-sync.ts:21/32 uses `order.order_date || localDate()`; localDate() in orders.repo.ts:12-15 is explicitly local, with a comment citing Algeria UTC+1). autoCompletePreviousDays() (orders.repo.ts:269-275) uses localDate(), so at 00:00-00:59 local (UTC still previous day) a startup completes local-yesterday's leftover 'preparing' orders locally while the Supabase cleanup's UTC `today` equals that local-yesterday, and `.lt` excludes exactly those rows — owner dashboard rows stay 'preparing'. autoCompletePreviousDays is a raw bulk SQL update that never calls syncOrderStatusToCloud, so line 520 is the only repair path. Worse than claimed: the cleanup is gated on `if (completed > 0)` (line 514), so the next startup finds nothing to complete locally and never retries the cloud update — stale rows persist until a future day again leaves local leftovers with the app started after 01:00. Proposed fix (`const today = localDate()` from orders.repo) is correct and matches the convention already applied in owner-sync.ts:47 and analytics-sync.ts:20.

findings.title: Scheduled daily backup requires an exact minute match — a missed tick (sleep, blocked event loop) skips that day's backup with no catch-up
findings.evidence: `if (currentTime === schedTime && lastScheduledBackupDate !== today)` — the 60s setInterval produces roughly one tick per wall-clock minute, but if the PC is asleep/hibernating at schedTime or the main thread is blocked >60s (synchronous copyFileSync of a large DB to a slow USB target on order creation), no tick lands inside that exact minute and the condition never becomes true again that day.
findings.scenario: Backup scheduled for 23:00; the POS PC is asleep or busy at exactly 23:00 and wakes at 23:03. No scheduled backup runs that day at all — silently, since performAutoBackup also swallows errors.
findings.fix: Change the condition to fire once per day when currentTime >= schedTime (e.g. `if (currentTime >= schedTime && lastScheduledBackupDate !== today)`), keeping lastScheduledBackupDate as the once-per-day latch.

refuter.reason: The code-level observation is accurate: at src/main/ipc/backup.ipc.ts:202, `if (currentTime === schedTime && lastScheduledBackupDate !== today)` with a 60s setInterval requires a tick to land inside the exact HH:MM minute of schedTime, and lastScheduledBackupDate is only a once-per-day latch, not catch-up. So a sleep/hibernate across 23:00 (or a >60s main-thread block) would skip that day's SCHEDULED fire. However, the reviewer's asserted IMPACT — "no backup runs that day, restaurant left without a backup" — is refuted by handling that exists elsewhere (the classic false-positive pattern). performAutoBackup() is invoked on EVERY order creation: orders.ipc.ts:15 (POS), tablet/server.ts:311 (tablet), remote-order-listener.ts:128 (remote). All call the same performAutoBackup(), which writes the identical filename fastfood-backup-<today>.db (getTodayBackupName, lines 10-13) to the identical backup_paths targets. So on any day with orders, the last order already wrote/overwrote today's backup to every target, current as of that order; skipping the 23:00 scheduled tick removes nothing. On a zero-order day the DB is unchanged, so an existing backup already captures the full state. The scheduled backup is a redundant backstop, not load-bearing for data safety, so the exact-minute fragility does not produce a concrete data-loss/wrong-behavior a restaurant would experience. It is a real minor reliability smell (the proposed >= fix is reasonable), but not the concrete bug claimed.

tracer.reason: Confirmed by trace. backup.ipc.ts:178 -> setupScheduledBackup() installs a setInterval(...,60000) (lines 192/209) whose only trigger for the scheduled backup is line 202: `if (currentTime === schedTime && lastScheduledBackupDate !== today)`. currentTime is a local zero-padded "HH:MM" (line 199) built each tick; the check demands EXACT minute equality. The 60s interval is not minute-aligned and is suspended during OS sleep/hibernate and can be starved when the single-threaded Electron main is blocked (performAutoBackup does synchronous copyFileSync at line 28 and is also called synchronously on order creation at orders.ipc.ts:15). Concrete failure: backup_schedule_time="23:00" (default), valid backup_paths, PC asleep at 23:00 and resumes 23:03; first post-resume tick has currentTime="23:03" != "23:00", and no other tick that day matches, so performAutoBackup() (line 204) never runs. It fails silently: the interval body catch (206) and performAutoBackup (29-35) swallow all errors. Grep confirms no catch-up/missed-run recovery anywhere. Impact is partially softened because performAutoBackup also fires on every order creation, but the scheduled end-of-day snapshot the owner configured is silently skipped on any sleep/hibernate/long-block day. Proposed fix (currentTime >= schedTime with the lastScheduledBackupDate latch) is correct: zero-padded HH:MM strings compare in time order, and the today latch keeps it once-per-day. Minor non-blocking caveats: the today latch uses UTC date (toISOString, line 200) while schedTime is local (harmless at 23:00 in UTC+1), and a restart after schedTime re-runs a harmless idempotent same-day overwrite; the fix also won't catch a next-morning resume (08:00 >= 23:00 is false), which is acceptable for a daily latch.

findings.title: Excel import / version restore recreates workers with new IDs, silently orphaning per-worker printer assignments
findings.evidence: clearForImport/restoreVersion soft-delete workers and insert fresh rows (`INSERT INTO workers (name, role, ...)` line 224-230) without printer_name, and worker IDs are AUTOINCREMENT so they never match the old ones. printer_assignments rows of type 'worker' keep the old worker_id, and workers.printer_name overrides are not carried over, so getPrinterForWorker(newId) always falls through to the kitchen_all printer.
findings.scenario: Restaurant uses split kitchen printing (grill printer for Ali, fryer printer for Sami). They update the menu via Excel import. All per-worker printer routing silently resets: every worker's tickets now print on the main kitchen printer until someone notices and reconfigures the Printer tab.
findings.fix: Snapshot and restore workers.printer_name in saveVersion/restoreVersion, and after import/restore remap 'worker' printer_assignments by worker NAME to the new IDs (or warn the user that printer assignments must be redone).

refuter.reason: CONFIRMED real. Traced the full path in the working tree. (1) saveVersion (src/main/ipc/data.ipc.ts:70-75) snapshots workers as only name/role/pay_full_day/pay_half_day/phone — it omits the workers.printer_name override column (real column from migration 008). The Excel export sheet (ExcelImportExport.tsx:118-126) also omits it. (2) restoreVersion soft-deletes workers (is_active=0, line 162) then re-INSERTs them with fresh AUTOINCREMENT ids and no printer_name (lines 224-230, guilty line 229). Excel import does the same via workersRepo.create (workers.repo.ts:80). Old rows are kept, so ids change. (3) printer_assignments has FK ON DELETE CASCADE, but soft-delete never triggers cascade, and neither clearForImport nor restoreVersion deletes from printer_assignments — so 'worker' rows keep the OLD worker_id. (4) getPrinterForWorker(newId) (printer-assignments.repo.ts:76-95): new worker's printer_name is NULL → no match; printer_assignments worker_id=newId → no match (rows hold old ids); falls through to getKitchenAllPrinter(). This is the real routing path (printer.ipc.ts:480 split-kitchen print, and :514), with split_kitchen_tickets defaulting to 'true' (migration 008:38). Result: after an Excel menu import or version restore, every worker's kitchen ticket routes to the single kitchen_all printer instead of their assigned printer (Ali's grill / Sami's fryer), exactly the scenario. Tellingly, restore DOES re-link worker_categories by NAME (lines 232-247), proving the author knew to remap across the id change but forgot printer routing. The uncommitted fix pass added FK try/finally and worker_categories snapshotting but did not address printer_name/printer_assignments, so the bug stands in the current tree.

tracer.reason:
CONFIRMED real. Full trace verified against the working tree:

PER-WORKER PRINTING IS KEYED BY WORKER ROW ID. Split-kitchen printing (src/main/ipc/printer.ipc.ts:458-489) groups an order's items by item.worker_id and, per worker, resolves the printer via printerAssignmentsRepo.getPrinterForWorker(workerId) (line 480). getPrinterForWorker (src/main/database/repositories/printer-assignments.repo.ts:76-95) resolves in order: (1) workers.printer_name for that active worker id, (2) printer_assignments row with assignment_type='worker' AND worker_id=id, (3) else getKitchenAllPrinter(). Both per-worker mechanisms are keyed by the worker's AUTOINCREMENT id.

VERSION RESTORE (the line-229 path): saveVersion snapshots workers with only "SELECT name, role, pay_full_day, pay_half_day, phone" (data.ipc.ts:70-75) — printer_name is NOT captured, and printer_assignments is never snapshotted. restoreVersion soft-deletes all workers (line 162, keeping old ids + printer_name + their printer_assignments rows) then re-inserts fresh workers via INSERT INTO workers (name, role, pay_full_day, pay_half_day, phone, is_active) (lines 224-230) — printer_name defaults to NULL and each row gets a new id. printer_assignments is never touched/remapped. So getPrinterForWorker(newId): workers.printer_name = NULL -> no 'worker' assignment for newId (old rows still hold old ids) -> falls through to kitchen_all. Confirmed.

EXCEL IMPORT: ExcelImportExport.tsx:161 calls clearForImport (soft-deletes workers, leaves printer_assignments intact), then line 232 re-creates workers via workers:create -> workersRepo.create (workers.repo.ts:76-83) which INSERTs without printer_name (NULL) and mints new ids. The Excel "Workers" sheet has no printer column, so printer_name is never repopulated. Same orphaning result. Confirmed.

CONCRETE FAILURE: Ali (worker id=3, printer_name='Grill-Printer'; Sami id=4 -> 'Fryer-Printer'), split_kitchen_tickets='true'. Owner does Excel import (or restores a version). Ali is recreated as id=17 / Sami id=18, printer_name NULL, old 'worker' printer_assignments still reference ids 3/4. Next order's items are tagged worker_id=17/18; printOrder loop calls getPrinterForWorker(17/18) -> both fall back to getKitchenAllPrinter(). Every worker's kitchen ticket now prints on the single main kitchen printer until someone re-enters the Printer tab. Real operational disruption (not money loss).

FIX DIRECTION mostly sound but incomplete: snapshotting/restoring workers.printer_name in saveVersion/restoreVersion fixes the restore path, and remapping 'worker' printer_assignments by worker NAME (old soft-deleted rows retain the name for lookup) fixes both paths for the assignments-table mechanism. BUT for the Excel-import path there is no prior snapshot of workers.printer_name to restore (Excel has no printer column), so the printer_name half of the fix does nothing there — clearForImport would need to itself snapshot printer_name-by-name and reapply, or rely solely on the name-based printer_assignments remap. The name-based remap is the robust half and should be applied in BOTH clearForImport and restoreVersion, not just saveVersion/restoreVersion.

Not on the do-not-report list. Files: src/main/ipc/data.ipc.ts:70-75 (saveVersion omits printer_name) and 224-230 (restore insert), src/main/database/repositories/printer-assignments.repo.ts:76-95 (getPrinterForWorker), src/main/ipc/printer.ipc.ts:458-489 (split routing), src/renderer/src/pages/excel/ExcelImportExport.tsx:161/232 (import recreates workers).

findings.title: 'Modern' and 'Full Featured' presets ship a QR block with qrContent:'phone' — a key nothing reads, so the QR never renders
findings.evidence: Preset blocks: `{ id: '8', type: 'qr_code', enabled: true, config: { qrContent: 'phone' } }` (lines 28 and 53). Both the printer (printer.ipc.ts:122 `const qrUrl = cfg.qrUrl || ''; if (qrUrl) {...}`) and the editor preview (ReceiptEditor.tsx:440) read only `config.qrUrl`, so the block renders nothing on paper and shows 'Enter a URL to generate QR code' in the editor.
findings.scenario: Owner picks the 'Full Featured' preset expecting the advertised QR code; printed receipts contain no QR and the editor shows an empty placeholder they must manually fill — the preset's QR intent (encode the restaurant phone) is dead.
findings.fix: Either drop qrContent from the presets, or support it: when cfg.qrContent === 'phone', generate the QR from settings.restaurant_phone in buildFromTemplate (and mirror it in the preview).

refuter.reason: Confirmed. The 'Modern' (receipt-editor.ipc.ts:28) and 'Full Featured' (line 53) presets ship a qr_code block with config { qrContent: 'phone' } and no qrUrl. loadPreset (ReceiptEditor.tsx:170-172) sets blocks verbatim with no transformation. The print path (printer.ipc.ts:121-134) reads only `cfg.qrUrl || ''` and gates rendering on `if (qrUrl)`, never touching cfg.qrContent, so the block prints nothing. A repo-wide grep shows qrContent is read nowhere — it exists only in the type decl (ReceiptEditor.tsx:20) and the two preset definitions, making it a dead key. Owner picking either preset expecting a QR gets an empty block on paper and a placeholder in the editor. Real, concrete, non-money-critical UX/feature defect.

CONFIRMED by full code trace. The 'Modern' (receipt-editor.ipc.ts:28) and 'Full Featured' (line 53) presets ship a qr_code block whose only config is `{ qrContent: 'phone' }`. However the alternative 'just drop qrContent from the presets' does NOT deliver the promised QR — it leaves an empty-config qr_code block that still renders the placeholder and still prints nothing, forcing the owner to type a URL manually. findings.title: Dead channel: 'tablet:isRunning' handler is registered but not exposed in preload and never invoked by any window
findings.evidence: src/main/ipc/tablet.ipc.ts:66-68: "ipcMain.handle('tablet:isRunning', () => { return isTabletServerRunning() })". The preload tablet namespace (src/preload/index.ts:277-296) exposes no isRunning method, and the only raw-invoke consumer (public/splash.html via window.electronAPI.invoke) calls only 'settings:getAll' and 'splash:close'. The renderer instead uses 'tablet:status' (tablet.ipc.ts:41-43), whose getTabletServerStatus() result already includes a 'running' field consumed at AmbianceScreen.tsx:198-199.
findings.scenario: No runtime failure — purely unreachable code that suggests two parallel status APIs exist; a maintainer reading tablet.ipc.ts may assume some window depends on 'tablet:isRunning' and keep it in sync, when nothing can ever call it.
findings.fix: Delete the 'tablet:isRunning' ipcMain.handle block; 'tablet:status' fully supersedes it.

findings.title: getShortCodes conflates 'no code row' with query failure — offline or transient errors return empty codes instead of the existing ones
findings.evidence: Lines 119-127: `const { data } = await supabase.from('short_codes').select('code')...single(); if (data) { result[type] = data.code } else { /* insert new */ }` — the select's error is discarded, so a network failure (supabase-js returns it as an error result, not a throw) looks identical to 'code not yet created'. The function then tries 5 inserts (lines 130-142) which also fail offline, leaving `result[type] = ''`. There is no net.isOnline() guard (unlike the sync functions) and no local caching of previously issued codes.
findings.scenario: Restaurant already has short codes issued. The owner opens the TV/owner-dashboard connect screen while the internet is briefly down: cloud:getShortCodes returns { tv: '', owner: '', order: '' } and the UI renders blank/broken share links even though valid codes exist in the cloud, with no error indication. On a transient blip where the select fails but a later insert succeeds, a second code row can also be minted for the same (machine_id, type).
findings.fix: Check the select's error: treat only PGRST116 (zero rows) as 'create new'; on network-level errors return a cached copy (persist issued codes in settingsRepo when first obtained) or an explicit failure the UI can show.

verifier_notes.refuterReason: The code reading is accurate (cloud-sync.ts:119 discards the select error; offline yields empty codes), but getShortCodes is dead code: repo-wide, it exists only as the definition, the 'cloud:getShortCodes' IPC handler (tablet.ipc.ts:159), and the preload bridge (preload/index.ts:298) — no renderer code ever invokes it. The actual TV/owner/order connect screens build links directly from the local machineId (AmbianceScreen.tsx:153-158 '/tv/<mid>', SettingsPage.tsx:1149/1153 '/owner/<machineId>', SettingsPage.tsx:275/1276/1280 '/r/<machineId>'), which works offline, so the claimed 'blank share links during an internet blip' scenario cannot occur. The duplicate-code-mint sub-claim also has no impact: admin/ has zero short_codes references (no resolver route), and createDisplayProfile's returned code is discarded (AmbianceScreen.tsx:308). A latent flaw in an unreachable function is not a real restaurant-facing bug.
verifier_notes.tracerReason: The code reading is accurate but the failure is unreachable. src/main/sync/cloud-sync.ts:119-127 does discard the select error ("const { data } = await supabase.from('short_codes').select('code')...single(); if (data) {...} else { /* insert */ }"), and with @supabase/supabase-js ^2.98.0 a network failure resolves to {data:null, error} rather than throwing, so offline the function would return {tv:'',owner:'',order:''}. However, getShortCodes is dead code: a full-repo grep shows the only references are its definition, the IPC handler (src/main/ipc/tablet.ipc.ts:159-161), and the preload exposure (src/preload/index.ts:298) — no renderer file ever calls window.api.cloud.getShortCodes. The claimed trigger UI does not use short codes at all: the TV connect link is built from machineId (AmbianceScreen.tsx:153-158, `fastfood-manager.vercel.app/tv/${mid}`), the owner-dashboard link is `/owner/${machineId}` (SettingsPage.tsx:1149,1153; owner:getQR in tablet.ipc.ts:149-156), and the remote-order link is `/r/${machineId}` (SettingsPage.tsx:1276,1280) — all pure local string interpolation that renders fine offline. Even createDisplayProfile's returned code is discarded by its only caller (AmbianceScreen.tsx:308), and admin/ has zero short_codes references (no resolver route exists). So no user action, timer, or network event executes the flawed path, and neither the blank-links scenario nor the duplicate-code-minting scenario can occur. The proposed fix (treat only PGRST116 as create-new, cache codes) is directionally correct IF the function is ever wired to UI, but the right action today is to delete or actually wire up the orphaned short-code path.

findings.title: Periodic sync now uploads full logo+slideshow base64 payloads once per profile every 5 minutes
findings.evidence: `for (const name of getLocalProfiles()) { try { await syncDisplaySettings(name) } ... }` runs from the 5-minute interval (line 264). Each syncDisplaySettings() call re-reads and re-encodes the logo (`settings._logo_base64 = 'data:image/png;base64,' + buf.toString('base64')`, line 43), up to 10 slideshow images as base64 (lines 63-70), and the ENTIRE `display_*` keyspace of ALL profiles (line 27-31) into that one profile's row — regardless of whether anything changed.
findings.scenario: A restaurant with 3 profiles and a 10-image slideshow (~5-10 MB base64 total) on typical Algerian ADSL uploads ~15-30 MB of identical data every 5 minutes, all day — saturating upstream (which also delays syncOrderToCloud/remote-order marking) and bloating the display_settings rows.
findings.fix: Skip unchanged profiles (hash the assembled settings blob and compare to the last-sent hash per profile before upserting), or only re-send heavy base64 fields when their source files' mtimes changed.

refuter.reason: Confirmed in the working tree. The new syncAllDisplayProfiles() (src/main/sync/cloud-sync.ts:213-218) is called from the 5-minute setInterval (line 263-264) and awaits syncDisplaySettings(name) for every local profile. syncDisplaySettings() unconditionally re-reads and base64-encodes the logo (lines 40-45: `settings._logo_base64 = 'data:image/png;base64,' + buf.toString('base64')`), re-encodes up to 10 slideshow images (lines 62-70), includes every `display_*` key of all profiles in each row (lines 27-31, `k.startsWith('display_')`), and upserts the full blob (lines 80-85). There is no hash/mtime/dirty-flag gating anywhere on this path (verified all callers: index.ts interval, tablet.ipc.ts, createDisplayProfile), and supabase upsert POSTs the entire row each time. findings.title: Customer display cart always shows the base (English) item name, ignoring the configured food language

The cashier's cart and the printed receipt show the Arabic name, but the customer-facing display shows "Cheese Burger" — inconsistent with everything else the customer sees, on an Arabic-speaking storefront.
findings.fix: Resolve the localized name when building the payload, e.g. reuse the same fallback chain: name = (foodLanguage==='ar' && i.name_ar) ? i.name_ar : (foodLanguage==='fr' && i.name_fr) ? i.name_fr : i.name.

findings.scenario: On the POS touchscreen the owner aims for the pencil to edit the 'Ramadan -20%' promo, hits the adjacent trash icon instead, and the promotion (with its specific-item list) is gone instantly with no undo — it must be rebuilt from memory, and until noticed, customers stop receiving the discount.

refuter.reason: The code claim is factually accurate: deletePromo (PromotionsPage.tsx:110-113) and deletePack (:162-165) call window.api.promotions.delete/packs.delete with no confirmation, wired directly to trash buttons (:288, :357) adjacent to the edit pencils (:285, :354). The premise that "destructive actions elsewhere get a confirmation modal" is false as stated: confirmation exists only for live-order operations (OrderScreen.tsx:1659, OrdersHistory.tsx:252) and backup restore. So the promo/pack delete is not an anomalous oversight; it matches the app's established management-page pattern. There is no logic error, no wrong output for any data input, and no money miscalculation — the delete does exactly what it is designed to do and the cascade is intended DB behavior. Harm only occurs if the operator physically mis-taps, which is a UX robustness concern ("add a confirm dialog"), falling in the same category as the excluded "add error handling everywhere" advice rather than a specific input/state -> wrong-behavior defect. A skeptical senior would push back that adding confirmations is a separate UX ticket to be applied uniformly, not a bug fix for this one file.

tracer.reason: Verified by full code trace. PromotionsPage.tsx:110-113 deletePromo (and 162-165 deletePack) call window.api.promotions.delete(id)/packs.delete(id) with NO confirmation, wired to a small trash button (line 288 / 357) sitting in the same `flex gap-2` row ~8px from the edit pencil (line 285 / 354), both tiny p-1.5 h-4 w-4 targets — genuinely mis-tap-prone on a touchscreen. Migration 011 (011_promotions.ts:25 and :47) declares promotion_items/pack_items ON DELETE CASCADE, so the specific-item list is permanently destroyed with the parent. Concrete: with a 'Ramadan -20%' specific-item promo, one accidental trash tap irreversibly removes it and its item associations, silently stopping the discount at checkout until manually rebuilt. Caveat: this is a UX/data-safety defect, not a logic/money-correctness bug — the code executes as written; the classification as a 'bug' vs accepted design choice is the only soft spot, hence medium confidence. findings.title: Dead 60s cap in backoff — shift is clamped to 2 so the delay never exceeds 40s; comment says 'capped 60s'

The unsynchronized RMW-vs-write can leave retryAttempt=1+ instead of 0, so the next scheduleRetry computes `10_000L shl 1`=20s (or 40s) at line 117 instead of the designed 10s. A second path (retryRunnable→retrySaved line 132 spawning a new connectWithCode thread while the old one still runs) yields two concurrent `retryAttempt++` and a lost increment. Impact is exactly as reported: TV auto-reconnects after 20/40/60s instead of 10s — genuinely real but LOW severity (timing only; no money/order-correctness impact). Proposed fix direction is correct: wrapping scheduleRetry's body in `ui.post{}` serializes all retryAttempt accesses onto the main looper (resets are already main-thread), fully removing the race; cleaner than volatile/Atomic which wouldn't cover the compound RMW-vs-reset ordering as neatly.

findings.title: Reprobe chains are untracked anonymous postDelayed lambdas — they multiply per (re)connect and are never cancelled in onDestroy
findings.evidence: `if (!switched) ui.postDelayed({ reprobeLanIfOnCloud() }, 10 * 60 * 1000L)` (line 161) posts a fresh anonymous Runnable each cycle, so there is no handle to cancel; onDestroy (line 466) only removes retryRunnable. reprobeLanIfOnCloud() is started anew on every successful cloud connect (lines 99, 128, 308), and each start creates an independent self-perpetuating 10-minute chain — nothing deduplicates them. Additionally the stale loadDisplay client from a previous connect keeps firing onPageFinished -> onResult(true) on later navigations (line 251-253), which re-runs the success block including reprobeLanIfOnCloud().
findings.scenario: A TV runs on the cloud fallback for weeks. Every network blip or renderer hiccup that leads to a reconnect (connectWithCode success at line 308) adds another 10-minute reprobe chain while the previous ones keep running. After N reconnects the app makes N resolve() HTTPS calls + N LAN probe sweeps every 10 minutes, and each surviving chain holds an implicit reference to the (possibly destroyed) Activity via `ui`, leaking it.
findings.fix: Mirror the retryRunnable pattern: store one `reprobeRunnable`, call `ui.removeCallbacks(reprobeRunnable)` before posting and in onDestroy, and guard reprobeLanIfOnCloud with an `reprobeInFlight` flag so only one chain exists.

The proposed fix direction (single stored reprobeRunnable + removeCallbacks before posting and in onDestroy + a dedup flag) is correct, but note the guard must cover the spawned background thread's whole lifetime and reset on all exit paths (switch success, exception, re-post), not just the synchronous method body.

findings.title: HTTP 4xx/5xx main-frame detection silently absent on Android 5.x (minSdk 21) — the documented 'locked onto error page forever' bug still exists there
findings.evidence: `onReceivedHttpError` (lines 237-244) is only invoked on API 23+; tv-app/app/build.gradle sets `minSdk 21` (line 12) and the code comment at lines 232-233 calls Android 5.x boxes "a stated target". On API 21/22 a main page answering with 4xx/5xx fires neither error callback, only onPageFinished → onResult(true). The comment at lines 240-243 says exactly what happens without this check: "it counted as a successful load and the TV locked onto the error page forever" — that remains the behavior on 5.x.
findings.scenario: An Android 5.1 TV box saved the cloud display URL; the Vercel project pauses and returns 503. onPageFinished reports success, retryAttempt resets, last_url is (re)confirmed, and the TV displays the 503 error page indefinitely with no retry — while the same setup on a newer box would fail over correctly.
findings.fix: On API < 23, verify the load out-of-band (e.g. after onPageFinished, do a quick HttpURLConnection HEAD/GET of the URL on a background thread and call fail() on status >= 400), or inject a tiny JS check of document readiness/known marker element.

findings.title: loadDisplay's onResult is not one-shot for success — every later main-frame navigation re-fires onResult(true), accumulating perpetual reprobeLanIfOnCloud loops
findings.evidence: `override fun onPageFinished(view: WebView?, finishedUrl: String?) { if (!failed) ui.post { onResult(true) } }` — fail() is guarded by the `failed` flag but success is not, and the WebViewClient stays attached until the next loadDisplay. Each extra onResult(true) in connectWithCode's callback (lines 304-308) re-runs `prefs.edit().putString("last_url", ...)` and reprobeLanIfOnCloud(), and each reprobe call that doesn't switch chains its own un-cancellable anonymous `ui.postDelayed({ reprobeLanIfOnCloud() }, 10 * 60 * 1000L)` (line 161) — these are never removed, not even in onDestroy (line 466 only removes retryRunnable).
findings.scenario: TV is on the cloud fallback and the display page reloads/navigates itself (self-refresh, redirect, fragment navigation). Each reload fires onPageFinished → onResult(true) → a new reprobe loop. After a day, dozens of parallel loops each spawn a thread and hit the cloud resolver every 10 minutes; when the LAN returns, several loops independently rewrite prefs and post competing loadDisplay calls. If the activity is ever recreated (config change not in configChanges), the old activity leaks because its reprobe timers can't be cancelled.
findings.fix: Make onResult one-shot: reuse the `failed` flag as a `done` flag (`if (!done) { done = true; ui.post { onResult(true) } }`), and store the reprobe re-post as a named Runnable removed in onDestroy and de-duplicated (removeCallbacks before postDelayed) like retryRunnable.

findings.title: Auto-retry unconditionally tears down the pairing screen while staff are typing, discarding their input
findings.evidence: loadDisplay always ends with `ui.post { removePairing(); web.loadUrl(url) }` (lines 255-258), and retrySaved() (line 127) calls loadDisplay on the saved URL every 10-40s while the pairing screen is up (showPairing + scheduleRetry cycle, lines 103-104, 130, 310-311). Nothing checks whether the user is mid-entry; removePairing() also nulls statusView and drops the EditText.
findings.scenario: The saved POS URL is dead (PC replaced), so the TV shows the pairing screen and auto-retries every 10-40s. Staff enter the new 4-digit code with the TV remote's D-pad (takes 20-60s). Mid-typing, retrySaved fires: the pairing UI vanishes, the screen goes black/error for the duration of the doomed page load, then showPairing(code) returns with the OLD code prefilled — the digits they typed are gone. This repeats every retry until they happen to finish within one backoff window.
findings.fix: Skip the automatic retrySaved cycle (or at least don't call removePairing/reload) while pairingView != null and the input has focus/user-modified text; alternatively only remove the pairing UI in loadDisplay's success path (onResult(true)) instead of before the load starts.

findings.title: via_cloud is persisted before the load is verified — a failed LAN attempt sets via_cloud=false while last_url still points at the cloud, permanently disabling the LAN re-probe
findings.evidence: `prefs.edit().putString("code", code).putBoolean("via_cloud", viaCloud).apply()` runs before loadDisplay verifies the target, while last_url is deliberately only written after success (line 307). The two keys can therefore disagree: via_cloud describes the attempt, last_url describes the last *working* URL.
findings.scenario: TV is on the cloud fallback (last_url=cloudUrl, via_cloud=true). A blip makes the cloud page fail → connectWithCode runs, the LAN is now TCP-reachable so viaCloud=false is persisted, but the LAN page load fails (server mid-restart). retrySaved then reloads the still-saved cloudUrl successfully → reprobeLanIfOnCloud() reads via_cloud=false and returns immediately (line 140). The TV is pinned to the slow/paid cloud path with the periodic LAN re-probe permanently switched off — exactly the egress-cost path the design says it should escape — until someone re-enters the code.
findings.fix: Persist via_cloud together with last_url inside the verified-success branch (line 307), not before the load; only the code needs to be saved up front.

findings.title: setStatus re-creates the pairing screen prefilled with the OLD saved code, not the code currently being attempted
findings.evidence: `if (statusView == null) showPairing(prefs.getString("code", null))` (line 430). The Connect handler calls removePairing() before connectWithCode(code) (lines 399-400), so the very first setStatus("Connecting…") at line 264 rebuilds the pairing form with prefs' old code — the new code the user just typed is not in prefs yet (it is only persisted after resolve succeeds, line 302). The later `showPairing(code)` at line 310 is a no-op because `if (pairingView != null) return` (line 361).
findings.scenario: TV was paired with code 1234. Staff re-pair with 5678; resolve finds it but the display load fails (POS mid-boot). The pairing screen shown during/after the attempt has 1234 in the input box. Staff glance at it, press Connect, and unknowingly retry the wrong/old code 1234 — the "failure shows the attempted code" intent of `showPairing(code)` at line 310 never takes effect.
findings.fix: Thread the attempted code into setStatus (e.g. `setStatus(msg, attemptCode)`), and when the pairing view already exists, update the EditText prefill instead of returning early in showPairing.

refuter.reason: The claim's central mechanism is wrong. It asserts `showPairing(code)` at line 310 is a no-op via the `if (pairingView != null) return` guard (line 361), so the failure keeps showing the old code. But on the load-failure path, `loadDisplay` (line 217) unconditionally runs `removePairing()` (line 256) inside its posted runnable together with `web.loadUrl(url)`, nulling `pairingView` BEFORE the failure callback fires. The failure callback (`onReceivedError`/`onReceivedHttpError` → `fail()` → `ui.post { onResult(false) }`) is queued strictly after that removePairing runnable, so when line 310 `showPairing(code)` executes, `pairingView` is null and it rebuilds the form prefilled with the ATTEMPTED code (5678), not the old 1234. Android's Handler queue makes this ordering deterministic. Thus after a failed re-pair the input correctly shows the attempted code, and the claimed outcome (staff see and retry the old 1234) does not occur. The only accurate sliver is a transient 'Connecting…' screen at line 264 that briefly prefills the old code before loadDisplay clears it — but that is not the failure/after-state the claim describes, and line 310 is not a no-op. Claim refuted.

tracer.reason:
The guilty line is real: setStatus (line 430) rebuilds the pairing screen via `showPairing(prefs.getString("code", null))`, i.e. with the OLD saved code, never the code currently being attempted. Concrete repro: TV saved code=1234; POS has since regenerated its pairing code to 5678. Boot fails, pairing screen appears; staff clear the box, type 5678, press Connect. The handler calls removePairing() then connectWithCode("5678"); the first thing connectWithCode does is setStatus("Connecting…") (line 264). Because statusView was just nulled, line 430 fires showPairing(prefs["code"]) and prefs["code"] is still "1234" (the new code is only persisted at line 302 AFTER resolve succeeds). So the box reverts to 1234. If resolve("5678") then returns null (typo / code changed again) or the POS is unreachable, the flow hits setStatus at line 271/294/318/321 on that same statusView, so the RESTING screen shows the input box prefilled "1234" with the error text — exactly the "staff glance and retry the wrong/old code" hazard. Real, concrete, user-visible (though it is a pairing-UX confusion, not a money/data bug).

HOWEVER, the reporter's SPECIFIC scenario and mechanism are inaccurate: in the resolve-OK-but-load-FAILS path they describe, the final screen actually shows the CORRECT code 5678, not 1234. Their claim that `showPairing(code)` at line 310 is a no-op (blocked by line 361 `if (pairingView != null) return`) is false, because loadDisplay (lines 255-258) calls removePairing() before web.loadUrl, so pairingView is null by the time onResult(false) runs — line 310 rebuilds with the attempted code and works. The bug is really exposed by the non-load failure branches (code-not-found, couldn't-reach-POS, IOException) and the transient Connecting… state, not by the load-failure branch they cited.

Proposed fix is partially right: threading the attempted code into setStatus so it rebuilds showPairing with that code is the correct core fix. The second half (change showPairing to update the EditText instead of early-returning when pairingView != null) targets line 310, which is a non-issue for the reported path since loadDisplay already removed the view; it's harmless but requires keeping an EditText reference (currently input is a local, so the fix also needs to store it as a field). Net: bug is real, but the reporter's causal chain and after-state need correcting.
